It invites reflection on the fate of earlier peoples: 'see how (kayfa) was the end of the deniers' (3:137), and on creation: 'Do they not look at the camels, how (kayfa) they were created?' (88:17).

primaryMeaning: One of a pair — each of two things that go together. Zawj is a spouse, husband or wife, and more broadly a mate, a pair, or a kind.
extendedMeaning: 'He created for you from yourselves spouses (azwājan) that you may find tranquillity in them' (30:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 81 times. 'He created you from a single soul and created from it its mate (zawjahā)' (4:1). Pairs run through creation: 'of everything We created pairs (zawjayn)' (51:49), and Nuh was told to carry 'of every kind two, a pair (zawjayn)' (11:40). The spouses of Paradise are 'purified spouses (azwājun muṭahhara)' (2:25).

primaryMeaning: The heel, and from it, what comes after — following behind. ʿĀqiba is the outcome or end; ʿiqāb is punishment that follows a deed; ʿuqbā is the final reward.
extendedMeaning: ʿUqbā al-dār, 'the final home', is the good end promised to the patient (13:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 80 times. ʿĀqiba, 'the end', invites reflection: 'see how was the end (ʿāqibatu) of the deniers' (3:137), and 'the end belongs to the God-conscious' (7:128). Allah is 'severe in retribution (shadīd al-ʿiqāb)' (2:196). Turning 'on one's heels (ʿaqibayhi)' means going back on faith (2:143).

primaryMeaning: Width, and the side of a thing. From 'side' come aʿraḍa, 'to turn aside', to turn away from something, and ʿaraḍa, 'to set out' or 'present' something before someone. ʿAraḍ is what passes by — transient gain.
extendedMeaning: 'A Garden whose width (ʿarḍuhā) is the heavens and the earth' (3:133). ʿAraḍ al-ḥayāt al-dunyā, 'the passing goods of worldly life' (4:94).
quranUsage: Occurs 79 times. Muʿriḍūn, 'turning away', describes those who reject reminders (2:83). The Prophet is told, 'turn away (fa-aʿriḍ) from them, but advise them' (4:63). People 'will be presented (yuʿraḍūna) before their Lord' (11:18).

primaryMeaning: The face — the front of anything, and by extension its direction and its very self. Wijha is the direction one faces, and tawajjaha is to turn towards something.
extendedMeaning: 'Everything will perish except His Face (wajhahu)' (28:88). 'Whoever submits his face (wajhahu) to Allah' means submitting oneself wholly (2:112).
quranUsage: Occurs 78 times. 'Turn your face (wajhaka) towards the Sacred Mosque' (2:144). Wajh Allāh, 'the Face of Allah', means Allah Himself: 'seeking the Face (wajhi) of Allah' (2:272), and 'wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah' (2:115). Faces show the outcome: 'the Day some faces (wujūhun) will turn bright and some dark' (3:106).

primaryMeaning: To communicate quickly and in secret — by a sign, a hint or inspiration. Waḥy is revelation from Allah to His prophets, and also the inspiration He places in other creatures.
extendedMeaning: Zakariyya 'signalled (fa-awḥā) to them' when he could not speak (19:11). Devils 'inspire (yūḥī) one another with decorative speech' (6:112).
quranUsage: Occurs 78 times. 'We have revealed (awḥaynā) to you as We revealed to Nuh and the prophets after him' (4:163). The Prophet speaks from revelation: 'It is only a revelation revealed (waḥyun yūḥā)' (53:4). Waḥy is also inspiration to the mother of Musa (28:7) and to the bee (16:68).

primaryMeaning: To reach, to arrive at an end. Balagha is to reach a place, age or goal; ballagha is to make something reach — to convey a message; balāgh is conveyance.
extendedMeaning: 'O Messenger, convey (balligh) what has been sent down to you from your Lord' (5:67).
quranUsage: Occurs 77 times. The Messenger's duty is 'only to convey (al-balāgh)' (3:20). The prophets tell their people, 'I convey (uballighukum) to you the messages of my Lord' (7:62). Balagha describes reaching maturity: 'when he reached his full strength (balagha ashuddahu)' (46:15).

primaryMeaning: To hit the mark — to go straight to the target. Aṣāba is to strike or befall; muṣība is a misfortune that strikes; ṣawāb is being right, hitting the truth. Ṣayyib is rain that comes down.
extendedMeaning: Ṣayyib, 'a rainstorm', appears in the parable of 2:19. Ṣawāb, 'what is right', is spoken on the Day of Judgment only by those permitted (78:38).
quranUsage: Occurs 77 times, mostly for what befalls people: the patient, 'when a misfortune (muṣībatun) strikes them, say, "We belong to Allah and to Him we will return"' (2:156). 'No misfortune strikes except by the permission of Allah' (64:11), and 'whatever misfortune befalls you is because of what your hands have earned' (42:30).

primaryMeaning: To be few or little, the opposite of kathra, 'being many'. Qalīl is 'little' or 'few', and qilla is scarcity.
extendedMeaning: Before Badr, 'He made you appear few (yuqallilukum) in their eyes' (8:44).
quranUsage: Occurs 76 times, mostly as qalīlan, 'little', often in the phrase thamanan qalīlan, 'a small price', for selling Allah's signs for worldly gain (2:41). 'Few (qalīlun) of My servants are grateful' (34:13). 'The enjoyment of this world is little (qalīl)' (4:77).

primaryMeaning: Pain. Alam is pain or suffering, and alīm is 'painful'.
quranUsage: Occurs 75 times, almost always in ʿadhābun alīm, 'a painful punishment' (2:10). It also describes the shared suffering of battle: 'if you are suffering (ta'lamūna), they too are suffering as you suffer' (4:104).

primaryMeaning: Gratitude — recognising a favour and showing it. Al-Rāghib describes shukr as picturing the blessing and making it evident. A shakūr animal is one that grows well even on little fodder, so al-Shakūr is the One who rewards much for little.
extendedMeaning: 'Few of My servants are grateful (al-shakūr)' (34:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 75 times. 'Be grateful to Me (wa-shkurū lī) and do not be ungrateful' (2:152). 'If you are grateful (shakartum), I will surely increase you' (14:7). Laʿallakum tashkurūn, 'so that you may be grateful', closes many verses (2:52). Al-Shakūr, 'the Most Appreciative', is a name of Allah (35:30).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two senses: meaningful speech and wounding. Kalima is a word, kalām is speech, and kallama is to speak to someone; kalm, 'a wound', is the other branch.
extendedMeaning: 'If the sea were ink for the words (kalimāt) of my Lord, the sea would run out first' (18:109).
quranUsage: Occurs 75 times. 'Allah spoke (kallama) to Musa directly' (4:164). Kalima, 'word', is used for Allah's decree — 'the word of your Lord (kalimatu rabbika) has been fulfilled in truth and justice' (6:115) — and for ʿĪsā, 'a word from Him' (3:45). 'A good word (kalimatan ṭayyibatan) is like a good tree' (14:24).

primaryMeaning: Harm — the opposite of benefit. Ḍurr is harm or affliction, ḍarrā' is hardship, and iḍṭurra, 'to be compelled', is to be driven by harm or need into something.
extendedMeaning: Ayyub called out, 'Harm (al-ḍurr) has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful' (21:83).
quranUsage: Occurs 74 times, often in the challenge that false gods 'possess for you neither harm (ḍarran) nor benefit' (5:76). People remember Allah in hardship: 'when affliction (al-ḍurr) touches man, he calls on Us' (10:12). One 'compelled by necessity (uḍṭurra)' may eat what is otherwise forbidden (2:173).

primaryMeaning: Strength and hardship. Ba's is might or the force of battle, and also punishment; ba'sā' is distress. Bi'sa, 'how wretched!', is a verb of blame.
extendedMeaning: Iron is described as holding 'great strength (ba'sun shadīd) and benefits for people' (57:25).
quranUsage: Occurs 73 times. Bi'sa condemns: 'how wretched (bi'sa) a destination' (2:126). Ba'sunā, 'Our punishment', describes what struck earlier peoples: 'when Our punishment (ba'sunā) came to them' (6:43). The patient are praised 'in poverty, hardship (al-ḍarrā') and in times of battle (al-ba's)' (2:177).

primaryMeaning: To spend the night. A bayt, 'house', is originally the place one stays for the night; bayāt is a night attack.
extendedMeaning: Bayātan, 'by night', describes punishment coming while people slept (7:4). Ahl al-bayt, 'people of the house', refers to a household (33:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 73 times. Al-bayt, 'the House', is the Kaaba: 'We made the House (al-bayt) a place of return and security for people' (2:125), and Ibrahim and Ismail raised its foundations (2:127). Buyūt, 'houses', appear in the rules of entering homes (24:61).

primaryMeaning: The foot, and walking on foot. Rajul, 'man', is classically linked to this root; rijāl are men, and rājil is one on foot.
extendedMeaning: Arjul, 'feet', appears in the ablution verse: 'wash … your feet (arjulakum) to the ankles' (5:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 73 times, mostly as rajul and rijāl, 'man' and 'men': 'men (rijālun) whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah' (24:37). The creation of mankind: 'He spread from them many men (rijālan) and women' (4:1). Two men (rajulayn) are required as witnesses to a debt (2:282).

primaryMeaning: To be pleased and content — the opposite of anger. Riḍā is contentment, and riḍwān is Allah's good pleasure.
extendedMeaning: The soul at peace returns 'well-pleased and pleasing (rāḍiyatan marḍiyya)' (89:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 73 times. Raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhum wa raḍū ʿanhu, 'Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him', describes the people of Paradise (5:119). Riḍwān is the greatest reward: 'and the pleasure (riḍwānun) of Allah is greater' (9:72). The believer gives himself 'seeking the pleasure (marḍāti) of Allah' (2:207).

primaryMeaning: To be free of need, to have enough. Ghinā is sufficiency and wealth; al-Ghanī is the One who needs nothing. Aghnā ʿan, 'to avail', is to be of use — to spare someone a need.
extendedMeaning: Of the destroyed peoples: 'as if they had never lived (yaghnaw) there' (7:92).
quranUsage: Occurs 73 times. 'Allah is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghanī), and you are the needy' (47:38), and 'Allah is Self-Sufficient (ghaniyyun), Forbearing' (2:263). Often it says what will not help on the Day of Judgment: 'their wealth and children will not avail them (lan tughniya) anything against Allah' (3:10).

primaryMeaning: To separate, to split apart. Farīq is a group split off from others; tafarruq is division; furqān is what separates truth from falsehood.
extendedMeaning: The sea was 'parted (faraqnā)' for the Children of Israel (2:50).
quranUsage: Occurs 72 times. 'Hold fast to the rope of Allah all together, and do not be divided (lā tafarraqū)' (3:103). Believers 'make no distinction (lā nufarriqu) between any of His messengers' (2:136). Al-furqān, 'the Criterion', is a name for revelation (3:4) and the title of Surah 25.

primaryMeaning: To know and recognise — knowledge that comes from reflection and experience. Maʿrūf is what is recognised as good, and ʿurf is custom.
extendedMeaning: 'We made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another (li-taʿārafū)' (49:13). 'Arafāt' is named in 2:198.
quranUsage: Occurs 71 times, most often as bil-maʿrūf, 'in a fitting way', for dealings with others — especially in family law (2:229). Believers 'enjoin what is right (al-maʿrūf) and forbid what is wrong' (3:104). The People of the Book 'recognise (yaʿrifūnahu) it as they recognise their own sons' (2:146).

primaryMeaning: The right side, and blessing. Yamīn is the right hand, and yumn is good fortune — the right being the side of honour. Yamīn also means an oath, sworn by striking right hands together.
extendedMeaning: Mā malakat aymānukum, 'those your right hands possess', refers to people held in bondage (4:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 71 times. Aṣḥāb al-yamīn, 'the companions of the right', are the saved (56:27), and the fortunate 'will be given his record in his right hand (bi-yamīnihi)' (69:19). Aymān also means 'oaths': 'Allah will not hold you to account for thoughtless oaths (aymānikum)' (2:225).

primaryMeaning: To be high, to rise. ʿUluww is height and exaltation; taʿālā, 'He is exalted', declares Allah high above all; and taʿālaw, 'come!', is literally 'rise up to me'.
extendedMeaning: ʿUluww can also mean arrogance: 'you will rise to a great haughtiness (ʿuluwwan)' (17:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 70 times. Al-ʿAlī, 'the Most High', is a name of Allah (2:255), and subḥānahu wa taʿālā, 'glorified and exalted is He', answers false claims (6:100). Taʿālaw, 'come!', invites: 'come to a word common between us and you' (3:64). 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (al-aʿlā)' (87:1).

primaryMeaning: Enjoyment that lasts a while. Matāʿ is provision, goods, or any benefit of short duration; tamattaʿa is to enjoy something for a time.
extendedMeaning: 'The life of this world is only the enjoyment (matāʿ) of delusion' (3:185).
quranUsage: Occurs 70 times, often to show that this world is brief: 'the enjoyment (matāʿu) of this world is little' (4:77), and 'on the earth you will have a place to stay and provision (matāʿun) for a time' (2:36). Divorced women are owed 'a provision (matāʿun) in a fitting manner' (2:241).

primaryMeaning: To entrust one's affairs to another and rely on them. Tawakkul is putting one's trust in Allah; wakīl is the one to whom affairs are entrusted — the Guardian or Disposer of affairs.
extendedMeaning: The believers are those who, when Allah is mentioned, feel awe, and 'upon their Lord they rely (yatawakkalūn)' (8:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 70 times. 'Upon Allah let the believers rely (fal-yatawakkali)' (3:122). 'Whoever relies on Allah, He is sufficient for him' (65:3). The Prophet says, 'In Him I have put my trust (tawakkaltu)' (9:129), and Allah is 'sufficient as Disposer of affairs (wakīlan)' (4:81).

primaryMeaning: To be still after movement, to settle down. Sakan is rest and a dwelling; sakīna is inner calm; and miskīn, 'poor', is one whom need has brought to a standstill.
extendedMeaning: 'Look at their dwellings (masākinihim)' — the ruined homes of past peoples (20:128).
quranUsage: Occurs 69 times. The night was made 'for you to rest (li-taskunū) in it' (10:67), and spouses were made 'that you may find rest (li-taskunū) in them' (30:21). Sakīna, 'tranquillity', is sent down on the believers (9:26). Al-masākīn, 'the needy', are named among those owed kindness (2:83).

primaryMeaning: To think or suppose — an opinion that falls between doubt and certainty. Ẓann is assumption; in context it can mean firm belief or mere guessing.
extendedMeaning: 'Avoid much suspicion (al-ẓann); some suspicion is sin' (49:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 69 times. It often means baseless guessing: 'they follow only assumption (al-ẓann)' (6:116), and 'assumption avails nothing against the truth' (10:36). But it can mean confident belief: the humble 'who are certain (yaẓunnūna) that they will meet their Lord' (2:46).

primaryMeaning: To praise someone for their good qualities and actions. Al-Rāghib distinguishes ḥamd, praise for excellence, from shukr, thanks for a favour received. Muḥammad, 'the much praised', and Aḥmad, 'most praiseworthy', come from this root.
extendedMeaning: The Prophet is named Muḥammad (48:29) and Aḥmad (61:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 68 times. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīn, 'All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds', opens the Quran (1:2), and the people of Paradise say it at the end (7:43). Al-Ḥamīd, 'the Praiseworthy', is a name of Allah (22:64). Creation 'glorifies with His praise (bi-ḥamdihi)' (13:13).

primaryMeaning: To perish, to be lost or ruined. Ahlaka is to destroy; halāk is destruction.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction (al-tahluka)' (2:195).
quranUsage: Occurs 68 times, often for the destruction of earlier peoples: 'How many generations before them did We destroy (ahlaknā)?' (6:6). 'Everything will perish (hālikun) except His Face' (28:88). Halaka, 'he died', appears in the inheritance rulings (4:176).

primaryMeaning: To be one, single and alone. Wāḥid is 'one', waḥdahu is 'alone', and tawḥīd — declaring Allah one — comes from this root.
extendedMeaning: Al-Wāḥid al-Qahhār, 'the One, the Prevailing', is a name of Allah (13:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 68 times. 'Your god is one God (ilāhun wāḥid)' (2:163). Mankind came from one origin: 'He created you from a single soul (nafsin wāḥidatin)' (4:1), and 'mankind was a single community (ummatan wāḥidatan)' (2:213). The deniers resent worship of 'Allah alone (waḥdahu)' (7:70).

primaryMeaning: To send forth, to stir up and set something moving. Baʿth is sending — messengers or armies — and raising the dead to life.
extendedMeaning: Yawm al-baʿth, 'the Day of Resurrection' (30:56). The Quran argues from creation: 'if you are in doubt about the Resurrection (al-baʿth), We created you from dust' (22:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 67 times. It is used for resurrection — 'the Day they are raised (yubʿathūna)' (7:14) — which the deniers mocked: 'will we really be raised (la-mabʿūthūn)?' (17:49). It is also used for sending messengers: 'We sent (baʿathnā) after them Musa' (7:103), and 'Allah has sent (baʿatha) Talut as a king for you' (2:247).

primaryMeaning: To earn, to gain by one's own effort — what a person acquires through their actions.
extendedMeaning: 'Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned (kasabat)' (30:41).
quranUsage: Occurs 67 times, mostly for moral accounting: each soul 'will have what it earned (kasabat), and bear what it earned' (2:286), and 'every soul is held in pledge for what it earned' (74:38). 'That was a community which has passed; it will have what it earned (kasabat)' (2:134).

primaryMeaning: To cut off — originally, cutting fruit from a tree. From this comes jurm, 'crime', a deed that cuts one off from what is right. Lā jarama, 'no doubt', means literally 'it is cut and settled'.
extendedMeaning: 'Thus do We deal with the criminals (al-mujrimīn)' recurs as a warning (7:40).
quranUsage: Occurs 66 times, mostly as al-mujrimūn, 'the criminals' or 'the guilty', whose way the Quran makes clear (6:55). 'Do not let hatred of a people incite you (yajrimannakum) to transgress' (5:2), and to act unjustly (5:8). Lā jarama, 'assuredly', affirms a conclusion (11:22).

primaryMeaning: To be complete and whole. Awfā is to fulfil a promise or pay something in full; wafā' is keeping one's word; and tawaffā is to take something in full — above all, to take a soul at death.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim is praised as the one 'who fulfilled (waffā)' his duties (53:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 66 times. 'Fulfil (awfū) My covenant, and I will fulfil yours' (2:40), and 'O you who believe, fulfil (awfū) your contracts' (5:1). Tawaffā describes death and sleep: 'It is He who takes your souls (yatawaffākum) by night' (6:60). On the Day of Judgment 'every soul will be repaid in full (wuffiyat)' (3:25).

primaryMeaning: Loss — to lose, to fall short, as a trader who loses his capital. Khusr and khusrān are loss.
extendedMeaning: 'The Quran increases the wrongdoers only in loss (khasārā)' (17:82).
quranUsage: Occurs 65 times, mostly as al-khāsirūn, 'the losers' (2:27). Surah Al-ʿAṣr swears by time that 'man is in loss (la-fī khusr), except those who believe and do righteous deeds' (103:2–3). The real loss is on the Day of Judgment: 'the losers are those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection' (39:15).

primaryMeaning: The eye, and a spring of water — both are sources: the eye of sight and the spring of water flowing from the ground. ʿAyn also means the thing itself.
extendedMeaning: Ḥūr ʿīn, 'companions with beautiful wide eyes', are promised in Paradise (44:54). Qurrat ʿayn, 'coolness of the eyes', means joy (25:74).
quranUsage: Occurs 65 times. ʿUyūn, 'springs', are in Paradise: 'the God-conscious will be among gardens and springs (ʿuyūnin)' (15:45), and twelve springs gushed for the tribes of Israel (2:60). Bi-aʿyuninā, 'under Our eyes', describes Nuh building the ship under Allah's watch (11:37).

primaryMeaning: To flow or run. Jaraya is water flowing or a ship moving; jāriya is 'running' — used for ships and for a flowing spring.
extendedMeaning: Al-jawārī, 'the ships', 'like mountains on the sea', are among His signs (42:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 64 times, mostly in 'Gardens beneath which rivers flow (tajrī)' (2:25). Sun and moon 'each run (yajrī) for an appointed term' (13:2), and ships 'sail (li-tajriya) on the sea by His command' (14:32).

primaryMeaning: To carry or bear — a load on the back, a child in the womb, or a responsibility on the soul. Ḥaml is pregnancy, and ḥiml a burden.
extendedMeaning: Man took on the trust: 'and man bore it (ḥamalahā)' (33:72). 'Our Lord, do not lay (lā taḥmil) on us a burden like the one You laid on those before us, and do not burden us (tuḥammilnā) with what we cannot bear' (2:286).
quranUsage: Occurs 64 times. 'His mother carried him (ḥamalathu) in weakness upon weakness' (31:14). On the Day of Judgment, 'if a heavily laden soul calls for help with its load (ḥimlihā), nothing of it will be carried (yuḥmal)' (35:18). 'We carried (ḥamalnā) their offspring in the laden ship' (36:41) — those carried with Nuh (17:3).

primaryMeaning: To follow closely, one thing after another. Tilāwa, 'recitation', is reading words in their order, one following the next — and following what they say.
extendedMeaning: The sense of 'following' appears in 'By the moon when it follows it (talāhā)' — follows the sun (91:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 63 times, mostly for reciting revelation: 'when His verses are recited (tutlā) to them, it increases them in faith' (8:2), and a messenger 'who recites (yatlū) to them Your verses' (2:129). Those given the Book 'recite it as it should be recited (ḥaqqa tilāwatihi)' — which classical scholars explain as following it truly (2:121).

primaryMeaning: To taste — to perceive something with the tongue, and by extension to experience it directly.
extendedMeaning: Adam and his wife 'tasted (dhāqā) the tree' (7:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 63 times. 'Every soul will taste (dhā'iqatu) death' (3:185). Dhūqū, 'taste!', is said to the people of the Fire: 'taste (dhūqū) the punishment of the burning' (3:181). Allah lets people taste mercy and hardship: 'when We let mankind taste (adhaqnā) mercy after hardship' (10:21).

primaryMeaning: To turn something from its true nature or appearance — magic that deceives the eye. Siḥr is magic, sāḥir a magician; saḥar is the last part of the night before dawn, when darkness turns into light.
extendedMeaning: Al-asḥār, 'the hours before dawn', is when the believers seek forgiveness (3:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 63 times. 'This is nothing but obvious magic (siḥrun mubīn)' is the deniers' charge against signs (5:110). Pharaoh summoned his magicians (al-saḥara) to face Musa, and they came to believe (7:113–120). Magic was taught by devils, not by Sulayman (2:102).

primaryMeaning: To go back, to return to something, to repeat it. ʿĀda is habit — what one returns to; maʿād is the place of return; aʿāda is to do again, to restore. The corpus also places here ʿĀd, the ancient people sent the prophet Hud.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever returns (ʿāda) to it' — to taking usury — faces the Fire (2:275).
quranUsage: Occurs 63 times. Allah 'begins creation, then repeats it (yuʿīduhu)' — the resurrection (10:4). ʿĀd is named many times among the destroyed peoples: 'to ʿĀd We sent their brother Hud' (7:65).

primaryMeaning: To settle something firmly and finish it. Ibn Fāris says the root means perfecting and completing a thing. From this come qaḍā', 'decree' — settling what will be — and judgment, settling disputes; qāḍī is a judge.
extendedMeaning: It can mean finishing an act: 'when you have completed (qaḍaytum) the prayer, remember Allah' (4:103).
quranUsage: Occurs 63 times. 'When He decrees (qaḍā) a matter, He only says to it "Be"' (2:117). 'Your Lord has decreed (qaḍā) that you worship none but Him, and be good to parents' (17:23). Quḍiya, 'it has been decided', describes final judgment (10:47).

primaryMeaning: Water. Mā' is water of any kind — rain, rivers, springs or the fluid from which life begins. Its original form is mawah, which is why its plural is miyāh.
extendedMeaning: Before creation, 'His Throne was upon the water (al-mā')' (11:7). Man is created 'from a humble fluid (mā'in mahīn)' (77:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 63 times, mostly for rain sent from the sky: 'He sent down rain (mā'an) from the sky and brought forth fruits by it as provision for you' (2:22). Water is the origin of life: 'We made from water (al-mā') every living thing' (21:30).

primaryMeaning: To increase, to grow more. Zāda is to add to something or make it grow; mazīd is 'more' — an increase beyond what is due.
extendedMeaning: 'My Lord, increase me (zidnī) in knowledge' (20:114). In Paradise 'they will have whatever they wish, and with Us is more (mazīd)' (50:35).
quranUsage: Occurs 61 times. Revelation increases faith: 'when His verses are recited to them, it increases them (zādathum) in faith' (8:2), and it increases wrongdoers only in loss (17:82). Allah rewards the grateful with more: 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you (la-azīdannakum)' (14:7).

primaryMeaning: To touch — to make contact with the hand, and by extension for something good or bad to reach a person. Mass is touch; it is also used for marital relations.
extendedMeaning: Mass also refers to marital relations: divorce 'before you have touched them (tamassūhunna)' (2:236). Maryam asked, 'How will I have a son when no man has touched me (yamsasnī)?' (19:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 61 times, mostly for hardship or good that 'touches' people: 'when harm touches (massa) man, he calls on Us' (10:12), and 'if a wound has touched you (yamsaskum), a like wound has touched the other people' (3:140). 'If Allah touches you (yamsaska) with harm, none can remove it but He' (6:17).

primaryMeaning: To be hidden, absent or out of sight. Ghayb is 'the unseen' — all that is beyond the reach of the senses; ghāba is to vanish or set, as the sun does.
extendedMeaning: Bil-ghayb also means 'in secret' — the righteous wife guards 'in the husband's absence (lil-ghayb)' (4:34). Ghayāba is the bottom of the well into which Yusuf was cast (12:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 60 times. The God-conscious 'believe in the unseen (bil-ghayb)' (2:3). Allah alone knows it: 'with Him are the keys of the unseen (al-ghayb); none knows them but He' (6:59), and He is 'Knower of the unseen and the seen' (6:73). The Prophet is told to say, 'I do not know the unseen (al-ghayb)' (6:50).

primaryMeaning: To put gold into fire to separate it from impurity — to test by burning. Fitna is a trial or test that shows what someone truly is; it also means temptation, persecution and civil strife.
extendedMeaning: 'Fear a trial (fitnatan) that will not strike only the wrongdoers among you' (8:25). Those who seek hidden meanings in the unclear verses are 'seeking discord (al-fitna)' (3:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 60 times. 'Your wealth and your children are a trial (fitna)' (8:28). Allah tests people: 'Do people think they will be left to say "We believe" and not be tested (yuftanūn)?' (29:2). Fitna, 'persecution', is 'worse than killing' (2:191).

primaryMeaning: To cut and shape, as a craftsman cuts leather. Iftarā, 'to fabricate', is to cut out a lie and shape it — inventing something false.
extendedMeaning: Maryam's people said, 'You have brought something unheard of (shay'an fariyyā)' (19:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 60 times, mostly for inventing lies about Allah: 'Who does more wrong than one who invents (iftarā) a lie against Allah?' (6:21). The deniers said of the Quran, 'he has invented it (iftarāhu)', and were challenged to bring a surah like it (10:38). 'What they used to invent (yaftarūna)' leaves them on the Day of Judgment (6:24).

primaryMeaning: To send back, to return something — or to turn someone away. Irtadda is to turn back, above all to turn back from faith.
extendedMeaning: 'When Allah wills harm for a people, there is no turning it back (maradda lahu)' (13:11). Musa was returned (radadnāhu) to his mother (28:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 59 times. 'His punishment will not be turned back (lā yuraddu) from the criminal people' (6:147). Believers are warned: 'they will not stop fighting you until they turn you back (yaruddūkum) from your religion' (2:217), and 'whoever of you turns back (yartadda) from his religion' (5:54). Disputes are to be referred back (ruddūhu) to Allah and the Messenger (4:59).

primaryMeaning: To grow and to be pure. Ibn Fāris says the root means growth and increase. Zakāt is the portion of wealth given that purifies what remains and makes it grow; tazkiya is purifying the soul.
extendedMeaning: Azkā, 'purer', describes what is better for people's hearts and lives (2:232). 'He has succeeded who purifies himself (tazakkā)' (87:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 59 times. Al-zakāh, the prescribed charity, is paired with prayer: 'establish the prayer and give the zakah' (2:43). The Prophet was sent to 'recite to them His verses and purify them (yuzakkīhim)' (2:129). 'He has succeeded who purifies it (zakkāhā)' — the soul (91:9).

primaryMeaning: The back, and from it, what is visible on the outside. Ẓāhir is apparent; ẓahara is to appear or to rise above; ẓahīr is a supporter who has your back; aẓhara is to make prevail.
extendedMeaning: 'He is the First and the Last, the Outward (al-Ẓāhir) and the Inward' (57:3). The challenge of 17:88 says jinn and humans could not produce the Quran 'even if they were supporters (ẓahīran) of one another'.
quranUsage: Occurs 59 times. Allah sent His Messenger 'to make it prevail (li-yuẓhirahu) over all religion' (9:33). Believers are to avoid immoralities 'what is apparent (ẓahara) of them and what is hidden' (6:151). Throwing the Book 'behind their backs (ẓuhūrihim)' means ignoring it (2:101).

primaryMeaning: Nisā', 'women', is a plural with no singular of its own; imra'a is used for 'a woman'. It is a different root from nasiya, 'to forget' (n-s-y).
extendedMeaning: The Prophet's wives are addressed, 'O wives of the Prophet (yā nisā'a al-nabī), you are not like any other women' (33:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 59 times. Surah 4, Al-Nisā', is named after it and sets out many rights of women. 'Men will have a share of what they earned, and women (al-nisā') a share of what they earned' (4:32). Nisā'ukum, 'your wives', appears in family law: 'your wives (nisā'ukum) are a tilth for you' (2:223).

primaryMeaning: To strike. From the blow comes setting out a likeness — ḍaraba mathalan, 'to strike a parable', stamping an image on the mind — and ḍaraba fī al-arḍ, 'to strike out into the land', to travel.
extendedMeaning: Humiliation 'was struck (ḍuribat) upon them' — laid on them like a stamp (2:61).
quranUsage: Occurs 58 times. Most often, 'Allah sets forth (ḍaraba) a parable': 'a good word is like a good tree' (14:24). Ḍarabtum fī al-arḍ, 'when you travel in the land', relaxes the rules of prayer (4:101). Musa was told, 'Strike (iḍrib) the sea with your staff' (26:63).

primaryMeaning: Breath, wind and ease. Rīḥ is wind; rūḥ is the spirit — the breath of life; rawḥ is relief and rest, like a cool breeze; and rāḥa is ease.
extendedMeaning: Rūḥ al-qudus, 'the Holy Spirit', is Jibrīl, with whom ʿĪsā was supported (2:87). Yaʿqub told his sons, 'do not despair of the relief (rawḥ) of Allah' (12:87).
quranUsage: Occurs 57 times. Al-riyāḥ, 'the winds', are 'sent as good news before His mercy' (7:57). Al-rūḥ, 'the spirit', is from Allah: 'they ask you about the spirit (al-rūḥ); say, the spirit is of the command of my Lord' (17:85). Allah breathed into Adam 'of My spirit (rūḥī)' (15:29).

primaryMeaning: To count and number. ʿAdad is a number; ʿidda is a set count, including the waiting period after divorce or death. Aʿadda, 'to prepare', is to have something counted out and ready.
extendedMeaning: 'Prepare (aʿiddū) against them whatever you can of strength' (8:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 57 times. Aʿadda, 'He has prepared', describes what awaits: 'Allah has prepared (aʿadda) for them gardens' (9:89) and 'a painful punishment' (4:102). The fast is 'a number of days (ayyāman maʿdūdāt)' (2:184). 'The number (ʿiddata) of months with Allah is twelve' (9:36).

primaryMeaning: To gather together — as water collects in a basin, or people settle together in one place. Qarya is a town or settlement, and Umm al-Qurā, 'Mother of Towns', is Makkah.
extendedMeaning: 'Your Lord would never destroy the towns (al-qurā) unjustly while their people were doing good' (11:117).
quranUsage: Occurs 57 times, mostly for the towns of earlier peoples: 'How many a town (qaryatin) We destroyed' (7:4). Allah sent the Quran 'to warn the Mother of Towns (umm al-qurā) and those around it' (6:92). A town that was grateful then denied Allah's blessings is set out as a parable (16:112).

primaryMeaning: A set term — an appointed time or deadline. Ajal is the time fixed for something to end, including a person's lifespan.
extendedMeaning: Ajal is also a waiting period in family law: 'when they have fulfilled their term (ajalahunna)' (2:231).
quranUsage: Occurs 56 times. 'For every community is a term (ajal); when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor bring it forward' (7:34). Ajalun musammā, 'a named term', describes the lifespan of people and of the universe (6:2). Debts are to be written down 'for a fixed term (ajalin musammā)' (2:282).

primaryMeaning: To go, to go away. Adhhaba is to take something away. Dhahab, 'gold', shares the root.
extendedMeaning: Dhahab, 'gold', adorns the people of Paradise: 'bracelets of gold (dhahabin)' (18:31). 'Good deeds remove (yudhhibna) evil deeds' (11:114).
quranUsage: Occurs 56 times. 'Allah took away (dhahaba) their light and left them in darkness' (2:17). 'If He wills, He can do away with you (yudhhibkum) and bring others' (4:133). Idhhab, 'go', sends Musa to Pharaoh (20:24).

primaryMeaning: To reach an end, a limit. Nahā, 'to forbid', is to set a limit that must not be crossed; intahā is to stop at that limit — to desist. Nuhā, 'intellect', is what holds a person back from what is wrong.
extendedMeaning: Ulū al-nuhā, 'people of intellect', are those who see signs in creation (20:54). 'To your Lord is the final end (al-muntahā)' (53:42).
quranUsage: Occurs 56 times. The believers 'enjoin what is right and forbid (yanhawna) what is wrong' (3:104). Intahaw, 'if they cease', appears in the rulings on fighting (2:192). 'Prayer restrains (tanhā) from indecency and wrongdoing' (29:45).

primaryMeaning: To go round, to turn in a circle. Dār, 'home', is classically explained as a place enclosed by walls around it; dā'ira is a circle or turn of fortune.
extendedMeaning: Dā'irat al-sū', 'the turn of evil', is what the hypocrites wished on the believers — and what fell on them instead (9:98).
quranUsage: Occurs 55 times. Diyār, 'homes', appears in the expulsion of people from their homes (2:85). Al-dār al-ākhira, 'the home of the Hereafter', is the true home: 'the home of the Hereafter (al-dār al-ākhira) is better for those who fear Allah' (6:32). 'Seek, through what Allah has given you, the home (al-dār) of the Hereafter' (28:77).

primaryMeaning: To come out — a date is fasaqat when it bursts out of its skin. Fisq is stepping out of the bounds of obedience; fāsiq is one who deliberately goes beyond what Allah commanded.
extendedMeaning: Fusūq, 'defiance', is named alongside disbelief and disobedience as what Allah made hateful to the believers (49:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 54 times, mostly as al-fāsiqūn, 'the defiantly disobedient': 'He leaves none to stray by it except the defiantly disobedient (al-fāsiqīn)' (2:26). Iblis 'went out (fasaqa) from the command of his Lord' (18:50).

primaryMeaning: To call out loudly. Nidā' is a call made in a raised voice. Nādī, 'a gathering', is a place where people meet and call to one another. Nadā is moisture and dew, the root's other branch.
extendedMeaning: Yawm al-tanād, 'the Day of Calling', is a name for the Day of Judgment (40:32). 'When the call is made (nūdiya) to prayer on Friday' (62:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 53 times. Allah called Musa: 'he was called (nūdiya), "O Musa"' (20:11). Zakariyya 'called on his Lord a private call (nidā'an khafiyyā)' (19:3). On the Day of Judgment the people of Paradise and the Fire will call out to each other (7:44).

primaryMeaning: To know something inwardly, through experience. Khabar is news or information, and khubr is knowledge of the inner reality of a thing. Al-Khabīr is the One aware of hidden details.
extendedMeaning: Al-Khiḍr told Musa, 'How can you be patient with what you have no knowledge (khubran) of?' (18:68). 'That Day it will report its news (akhbārahā)' — the earth (99:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 52 times, mostly as khabīr, 'All-Aware': 'Allah is All-Aware (khabīrun) of what you do' (2:234). Al-Khabīr is paired with al-Laṭīf, 'the Subtle' (6:103), and al-Ḥakīm (6:18).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two senses: weakness (ḍaʿf, ḍuʿf), and doubling — adding a like to a thing (ḍiʿf). Istuḍʿifa is to be treated as weak, oppressed.
extendedMeaning: 'Man was created weak (ḍaʿīfā)' (4:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 52 times. 'Allah created you from weakness (ḍaʿfin), then made after weakness strength' (30:54). Ḍiʿf, 'double', describes multiplied reward and punishment: 'it produced its fruit double (ḍiʿfayn)' (2:265), and Allah 'multiplies (yuḍāʿifu) for whom He wills' (2:261). Al-mustaḍʿafūn, 'the oppressed', are those kept weak by tyrants (7:75).

primaryMeaning: Taḥta means 'beneath' or 'below' — the lower side of something.
extendedMeaning: When Maryam gave birth, a voice called 'from beneath her (min taḥtihā)': 'Your Lord has placed a stream beneath you (taḥtaki)' (19:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 51 times, above all in 'Gardens beneath which (min taḥtihā) rivers flow' (2:25). 'To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth … and whatever is beneath (taḥta) the soil' (20:6).

primaryMeaning: To untie, to open a knot — and from that, to make free and permitted. Ḥalāl is what is released for use; ḥalla is also to settle or descend on a place, as a traveller unties his baggage.
extendedMeaning: Maḥill is the place where something is due — the sacrificial animal's destination (2:196). Musa prayed, 'untie (uḥlul) the knot from my tongue' (20:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 51 times. 'Eat of what is on the earth, lawful (ḥalālan) and good' (2:168). 'It has been made lawful (uḥilla) for you, on the night of fasting, to go to your wives' (2:187), and 'the food of the People of the Book is lawful (ḥillun) for you' (5:5). Punishment is said to 'descend (yaḥillu)' on the deniers (11:39).

primaryMeaning: To be good, pure and pleasant — the opposite of khabīth, 'foul'. Ṭayyib describes what is wholesome in food, speech, earnings and character.
extendedMeaning: Allah will 'distinguish the bad from the good (al-ṭayyib)' (3:179). Ḥayātan ṭayyibatan, 'a good life', is promised to believers who do righteous deeds (16:97).
quranUsage: Occurs 50 times. 'Eat of the good things (ṭayyibāt) We have provided you' (2:57). The Prophet 'makes lawful for them the good things (al-ṭayyibāt) and forbids them the foul' (7:157). 'A good word (kalimatan ṭayyibatan) is like a good tree' (14:24).

primaryMeaning: To go bad, to be spoiled — the opposite of ṣalāḥ, 'soundness'. Fasād is corruption and disorder; afsada is to spoil or cause corruption.
extendedMeaning: 'Corruption (al-fasād) has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned' (30:41). 'Had there been gods other than Allah in them, they would have been ruined (la-fasadatā)' (21:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 50 times. The hypocrites, told 'do not cause corruption (lā tufsidū) on the earth', claim, 'we are only reformers' (2:11). 'Allah does not love corruption (al-fasād)' (2:205), nor the corrupters (al-mufsidīn) (5:64).

primaryMeaning: Benefit — the opposite of harm. Nafaʿa is to be of use to someone, and manāfiʿ are benefits.
extendedMeaning: Ships sail 'with what benefits (yanfaʿu) people' (2:164).
quranUsage: Occurs 50 times, often paired with harm: the false gods 'neither harm nor benefit (yanfaʿu)' (10:18). On the Day of Judgment intercession 'will not benefit (tanfaʿu) except for whom the Most Merciful permits' (20:109). Wine and gambling contain 'great sin and some benefits (manāfiʿ)' (2:219).

primaryMeaning: A span of time. Sāʿa is an hour or a short while; al-sāʿa, 'the Hour', is the Day of Resurrection, which comes suddenly, in a moment.
extendedMeaning: Sāʿatan, 'an hour', measures how short life will seem: 'as if they had not remained except an hour (sāʿatan) of the day' (10:45). A people's term cannot be delayed 'an hour (sāʿatan)' (7:34).
quranUsage: Occurs 49 times, mostly as al-sāʿa, 'the Hour': 'They ask you about the Hour (al-sāʿa), when is its arrival? Say, its knowledge is only with my Lord' (7:187). 'The Hour is surely coming' (15:85), and it will come 'suddenly (baghtatan)' (6:31).

primaryMeaning: To tie up and hold back — ʿiqāl is the cord that hobbles a camel's legs. ʿAql, 'reason', is what holds a person back from rash words and deeds, and what binds knowledge together.
extendedMeaning: 'These parables We set forth for people, but none will understand them (yaʿqiluhā) except those of knowledge' (29:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 49 times, almost always as a verb — the Quran never uses the noun ʿaql. A-fa-lā taʿqilūn, 'will you not reason?', challenges the listener (2:44). Signs in creation are 'for a people who reason (yaʿqilūn)' (2:164). The people of the Fire say, 'Had we listened or reasoned (naʿqilu), we would not be among the companions of the Blaze' (67:10).

primaryMeaning: Sin — a deed that holds a person back from reward. Ithm is wrongdoing that deserves blame, and athīm is one steeped in sin.
extendedMeaning: 'Avoid much suspicion; some suspicion is sin (ithmun)' (49:12). 'Allah does not love every sinning (athīm) disbeliever' (2:276).
quranUsage: Occurs 48 times. 'Cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin (al-ithm) and aggression' (5:2). Wine and gambling contain 'great sin (ithmun kabīr)' (2:219). Where there is necessity, 'there is no sin (ithma) on him' (2:173).

primaryMeaning: Fear mixed with awe and reverence. Al-Rāghib describes khashya as fear joined with veneration, usually arising from knowledge of the one who is feared.
extendedMeaning: Some stones 'fall down out of fear (khashyati) of Allah' (2:74). 'Do not kill your children for fear (khashyata) of poverty' (17:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 48 times. 'Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear (yakhshā) Allah' (35:28). The Quran is 'a reminder for whoever fears (yakhshā)' (20:3). Believers are told, 'do not fear them, but fear Me (wa-khshawnī)' (5:3).

primaryMeaning: To taste and to eat. Ṭaʿām is food; aṭʿama is to feed someone.
extendedMeaning: ʿĪsā and his mother 'both used to eat food (al-ṭaʿām)' — a sign of their humanity (5:75). Allah 'fed them (aṭʿamahum) against hunger' — Quraysh (106:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 48 times. Feeding the poor is a mark of faith and a form of expiation: 'they give food (yuṭʿimūna), despite loving it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive' (76:8), and the one who cannot fast pays 'a ransom: feeding (ṭaʿāmu) a poor person' (2:184). The deniers are condemned because 'he did not urge the feeding (ṭaʿām) of the poor' (69:34).

primaryMeaning: To go before, to precede. Qadam is the foot that steps forward; qaddama is to send something ahead; qadīm is 'old' — what came before.
extendedMeaning: 'Our Lord, make our feet (aqdāmanā) firm' (2:250). Yaʿqub's sons told him, 'you are in your old (al-qadīm) error' (12:95).
quranUsage: Occurs 48 times. Most often it describes deeds sent ahead to the Hereafter: 'because of what their hands have sent ahead (qaddamat)' (2:95), and 'whatever good you send ahead (tuqaddimū) for yourselves, you will find it with Allah' (2:110). Each soul should 'look to what it has sent ahead (qaddamat) for tomorrow' (59:18).

primaryMeaning: To hurry, to want something sooner than its time. ʿAjala is haste; al-ʿājila, 'the hasty one', is this world, whose rewards come quickly. ʿIjl, 'calf', shares the root.
extendedMeaning: Al-ʿijl, 'the calf', is the golden calf the Israelites worshipped (2:51).
quranUsage: Occurs 47 times. The deniers 'ask you to hasten (yastaʿjilūnaka) the punishment' (13:6). 'Man was created of haste (ʿajal)' (21:37). Those who want 'the immediate (al-ʿājila)' are given some of it, but lose the Hereafter (17:18).

primaryMeaning: Nobility and generosity — excellence in its kind. Karīm describes something noble and fine of its kind: a generous person, a noble word, a fine crop, an honourable reward.
extendedMeaning: 'Your Lord is the Most Generous (al-akram)' (96:3). Allah is dhū al-jalāli wa al-ikrām, 'Owner of Majesty and Honour' (55:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 47 times. 'The most noble (akramakum) of you with Allah is the most God-conscious' (49:13). The Quran is 'a noble (karīm) Quran' (56:77). Believers receive 'a noble provision (rizqun karīm)' (8:4). 'We have honoured (karramnā) the children of Adam' (17:70).

primaryMeaning: To adorn, to make beautiful. Zīna is adornment and outward beauty; zayyana is to make something look beautiful — sometimes truly, sometimes deceptively.
extendedMeaning: 'Who has forbidden the adornment (zīnata) of Allah which He brought forth for His servants?' (7:32). Rules about women's adornment (zīnatahunna) are in 24:31.
quranUsage: Occurs 46 times. Worldly life 'has been made to seem beautiful (zuyyina) to those who disbelieve' (2:212), and Satan 'made their deeds seem fair (zayyana)' (6:43). Allah adorns creation: 'We adorned (zayyannā) the nearest sky with lamps' (67:5). 'Wealth and children are the adornment (zīna) of the life of this world' (18:46).

primaryMeaning: The chest, the front of the body; and ṣadara, 'to come out from', as water-drawers leave the spring. In the Quran, ṣadr is the seat of the heart's hidden thoughts.
extendedMeaning: 'Did We not open your breast (ṣadrak) for you?' (94:1). 'We will remove whatever ill feeling is in their breasts (ṣudūrihim)' in Paradise (7:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 46 times, mostly for what is hidden in hearts: 'Allah knows well what is in the breasts (al-ṣudūr)' (3:119). Allah 'opens his breast (ṣadrahu) to Islam' for whom He wills to guide (6:125). Musa prayed, 'My Lord, open for me my breast (ṣadrī)' (20:25).

primaryMeaning: To keep something in mind and look after it; ʿahd is a pledge that must be kept — a covenant, treaty or promise — and also a time one remembers.
extendedMeaning: Allah 'had taken a covenant (ʿahidnā) with Adam before, but he forgot' (20:115). 'Did I not enjoin on you (aʿhad), O children of Adam, not to worship Satan?' (36:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 46 times. 'Fulfil My covenant (bi-ʿahdī), and I will fulfil yours' (2:40). 'Fulfil the covenant (bil-ʿahd); the covenant will be asked about' (17:34). Believers are described as 'those who fulfil their covenant when they make one (ʿāhadū)' (2:177), and hypocrites as breakers of it (2:100).

primaryMeaning: The morning, the first light of day. Aṣbaḥa, literally 'to enter the morning', is also used to mean 'to become' — to find oneself in a new state.
extendedMeaning: Surahs swear by the morning: 'By the morning (wal-ṣubḥ) when it brightens' (74:34). Miṣbāḥ, 'lamp', shares the root (24:35).
quranUsage: Occurs 45 times. Aṣbaḥa often means 'became': 'you became (fa-aṣbaḥtum), by His favour, brothers' (3:103), and 'he became (fa-aṣbaḥa) of the losers' (5:30). The punishment of Lut's people came at dawn: 'Their appointed time is the morning (al-ṣubḥ)' (11:81).

primaryMeaning: A wide, clear road. Ṣirāṭ (also written sirāṭ) is a path that is easy to follow; classical scholars connect it to saraṭa, 'to swallow', as a broad road seems to swallow those who travel it.
extendedMeaning: The Quran leads 'to the path (ṣirāṭi) of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy' (14:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 45 times, most often as ṣirāṭ mustaqīm, 'a straight path'. 'Guide us to the straight path (al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm)' is asked in every prayer (1:6). 'This is My path (ṣirāṭī), straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways' (6:153). ʿĪsā says, 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path' (3:51).

primaryMeaning: To forget, and also to leave something deliberately — to neglect it. Nisyān is forgetting.
extendedMeaning: Adam 'forgot (fa-nasiya), and We found in him no firm resolve' (20:115). 'Do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves (fa-ansāhum)' (59:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 45 times. 'They forgot (nasū) Allah, so He forgot them' — that is, He left them to themselves (9:67). 'Do you command people to righteousness and forget (tansawna) yourselves?' (2:44). 'Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget (nasīnā) or err' (2:286).

primaryMeaning: To leave, to let alone. This root is used only in the present and command forms — yadharu, dhar — its past tense being supplied by taraka.
extendedMeaning: The Thamud were told, 'This is the she-camel of Allah — leave her (fa-dharūhā) to graze' (7:73).
quranUsage: Occurs 45 times. Dharhum, 'leave them', tells the Prophet to let the deniers be: 'leave them (fa-dharhum) and what they invent' (6:112). 'Give up (dharū) what remains of usury' (2:278). Widows' rulings speak of those 'who die and leave (yadharūna) wives behind' (2:234).

primaryMeaning: To put one thing in place of another. Badal is a substitute; baddala is to change or alter; istabdala is to take something in exchange.
extendedMeaning: The skins of the people of the Fire are replaced: 'We will replace them (baddalnāhum) with other skins' (4:56). Evil deeds are exchanged for good: 'Allah will replace (yubaddilu) their evil deeds with good ones' (25:70).
quranUsage: Occurs 44 times. 'No one can change (lā mubaddila) the words of Allah' (6:34), and 'you will not find any change (tabdīlan) in the way of Allah' (33:62). The wrongdoers 'changed (fa-baddala) the word to other than what they were told' (2:59). The faithful 'did not change (baddalū) in the least' (33:23).

primaryMeaning: To guard and preserve, to keep something from being lost. Ḥifẓ is guarding — and also memorising, keeping words safe in the mind. Ḥafīẓ is a guardian or keeper.
extendedMeaning: 'Guard strictly (ḥāfiẓū) the prayers, and the middle prayer' (2:238). Yusuf's brothers promised, 'we will surely be his guardians (la-ḥāfiẓūn)' (12:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 44 times. 'We sent down the Reminder, and We will surely guard it (la-ḥāfiẓūn)' (15:9). Believers 'guard (yuḥāfiẓūna) their prayers' (6:92) and 'guard their private parts' (23:5). Allah is 'Guardian (ḥafīẓun) over all things' (11:57).

primaryMeaning: The back, the rear of a thing, and what comes after. Adbara is to turn one's back; dābir is the last remnant — the root; dabbara is to plan — to look at how a matter will end; tadabbur is reflection on consequences and deeper meaning.
extendedMeaning: 'A blessed Book We sent down to you, so that they may reflect (li-yaddabbarū) on its verses' (38:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 44 times. 'Do they not reflect (yatadabbarūna) on the Quran?' (4:82). Allah 'arranges (yudabbiru) the affair' of creation (10:3). Turning backs is fleeing: 'you turned back, fleeing (mudbirīn)' (9:25). Qaṭaʿa dābir, 'cutting off the root', means destroying completely (7:72).

primaryMeaning: Something hidden and inward. Sirr is a secret; asarra is to hide or confide; surūr, 'joy', is a gladness felt deep inside; and sarīr, a couch or throne, is a place of ease.
extendedMeaning: The one given his record in his right hand 'will return to his people rejoicing (masrūrā)' (84:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 44 times. 'He knows the secret (al-sirr) and what is more hidden' (20:7), and 'Allah knows what they conceal (yusirrūna) and what they reveal' (2:77). Spending 'secretly (sirran) and openly' is praised (2:274). In Paradise the believers sit 'on couches (surur) facing each other' (15:47).

primaryMeaning: To be easy, to go smoothly. Yusr is ease; yassara is to make something easy; yasīr is a small, easy matter. Maysir, 'gambling', is an easy gain without effort.
extendedMeaning: Al-maysir, 'gambling', is paired with wine: 'in them is great sin' (2:219).
quranUsage: Occurs 44 times. 'With hardship comes ease (yusrā)' — said twice (94:5–6). 'We have made the Quran easy (yassarnā) for remembrance; is there anyone who will remember?' (54:17). 'Allah intends ease (al-yusr) for you' (2:185). 'Recite what is easy (tayassara) of the Quran' (73:20).

primaryMeaning: To leave — to let go of something, to abandon it, or to leave it behind at death.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf told his prison companions, 'I have abandoned (taraktu) the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah' (12:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 43 times, often for what a person leaves behind: the rulings of inheritance speak of 'what parents and relatives leave (taraka)' (4:7). 'Do people think they will be left (yutrakū) to say "We believe" and not be tested?' (29:2). 'Does man think he will be left (yutraka) neglected?' (75:36).

primaryMeaning: To cut through, to pierce — as a traveller cuts through the land. From this comes jawāb, 'answer', a reply that cuts through a question; istajāba is to respond.
extendedMeaning: The Thamud 'carved the rocks (jābū al-ṣakhra) in the valley' (89:9) — the literal sense of cutting through.
quranUsage: Occurs 43 times. 'Call on Me; I will respond (astajib) to you' (40:60). Believers are told, 'Respond (istajībū) to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you to what gives you life' (8:24). 'Their Lord responded (fa-stajāba) to them: I will not let the work of any of you be lost' (3:195).

primaryMeaning: To gather people together and drive them in a crowd. Ḥashr is the great gathering on the Day of Judgment.
extendedMeaning: 'When the wild beasts are gathered (ḥushirat)' (81:5). Pharaoh sent 'gatherers (ḥāshirīn)' through the cities to bring his magicians (7:111). Surah 59 is named Al-Ḥashr, 'the Gathering'.
quranUsage: Occurs 43 times. 'Know that to Him you will be gathered (tuḥsharūn)' (2:203). 'The Day He gathers them (yaḥshuruhum) all together' (6:128). Animals too will be gathered: 'then to their Lord they will be gathered (yuḥsharūn)' (6:38).

primaryMeaning: To separate one thing from another. Faṣl is a dividing — decisive judgment; faṣṣala is to set out in distinct parts — to explain in detail.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah will judge (yafṣilu) between them on the Day of Resurrection' (22:17). Surah 41 is named Fuṣṣilat, 'Explained in Detail'.
quranUsage: Occurs 43 times. Yawm al-faṣl, 'the Day of Judgment' — the Day of Separation between truth and falsehood (37:21). The Quran is 'a Book whose verses have been perfected, then set out in detail (fuṣṣilat)' (11:1), and 'thus do We explain in detail (nufaṣṣilu) the signs' (6:55).

primaryMeaning: Above, over — being higher than something, in place or in rank.
extendedMeaning: 'He is the Prevailing over (fawqa) His servants' (6:18).
quranUsage: Occurs 43 times. 'Above (fawqa) every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing' (12:76). 'I will make those who follow you above (fawqa) those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection' (3:55). The God-conscious 'will be above them (fawqahum)' on the Day of Resurrection (2:212).

primaryMeaning: To plan in secret — turning someone away from what they intend by hidden means. Makr is scheming; when used of Allah, it means His hidden planning that brings the schemers' plots to nothing.
extendedMeaning: The Quraysh plotted against the Prophet 'to restrain you, kill you or expel you' (8:30).
quranUsage: Occurs 43 times. 'They planned (makarū), and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of planners' (3:54). 'The evil plot does not encompass except its own people' (35:43). 'Do they feel secure from the plan (makra) of Allah?' (7:99).

primaryMeaning: The sea — any wide expanse of water, salt or fresh. Classical lexicographers relate it to wideness and openness.
extendedMeaning: 'If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would run out before the words of my Lord ran out' (18:109; also 31:27). 'When the seas (al-biḥār) are set ablaze' (81:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 42 times. Ships sail 'in the sea (al-baḥr) with what benefits people' (2:164). The sea was parted for Musa (2:50). The meeting of 'the two seas (al-baḥrayn)' is where Musa sought al-Khiḍr (18:60).

primaryMeaning: Rough, hard ground — and from it, grief: the roughness felt in the soul at a loss or disappointment. Ḥuzn is sorrow about what has happened.
extendedMeaning: Yaʿqub's eyes 'turned white from grief (al-ḥuzn)' over Yusuf (12:84). Maryam was told, 'Do not grieve (lā taḥzanī)' (19:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 42 times, most often in the promise 'no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve (yaḥzanūn)' (2:38). The Prophet told Abu Bakr in the cave, 'Do not grieve (lā taḥzan); Allah is with us' (9:40). Believers are told, 'do not weaken and do not grieve (taḥzanū)' (3:139).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two senses: to make something serve without payment — to subject it — and to mock. Sakhkhara is to put something at another's service; sakhira is to ridicule.
extendedMeaning: 'Let not a people mock (yaskhar) another people; perhaps they are better than them' (49:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 42 times. Sakhkhara describes creation placed at people's service: 'He subjected (sakhkhara) the sun and the moon' (13:2), and 'He subjected the sea so you may eat fresh meat from it' (16:14). Sakhira describes mockery of the prophets: 'messengers before you were mocked' (6:10).

primaryMeaning: To turn away, and to turn others away — to block or hinder them. Ṣadd is obstruction.
quranUsage: Occurs 42 times, mostly for turning people from the way of Allah: 'those who disbelieved and hindered (ṣaddū) from the way of Allah' (4:167). The hypocrites, called to the Messenger, 'turn away (yaṣuddūna) from you in aversion (ṣudūdan)' (4:61). Satan 'turned them away (fa-ṣaddahum) from the way' (27:24).

primaryMeaning: Strength and power. Quwwa is strength — of body, mind, will or arms; qawiyy is strong.
extendedMeaning: Earlier peoples 'were stronger than you in strength (quwwatan)' yet were destroyed (9:69). Qārūn's treasures were so great their keys burdened 'a band of strong men (ulī al-quwwa)' (28:76).
quranUsage: Occurs 42 times. 'Allah is All-Strong (qawiyyun), severe in punishment' (8:52). The Israelites were told, 'Take what We have given you with strength (bi-quwwatin)' (2:63). Believers are to 'prepare against them whatever you can of strength (quwwatin)' (8:60).

primaryMeaning: A mountain — something massive and firmly set. Jibilla is what is created firm and fixed: human nature, and also a great multitude or generation of people.
extendedMeaning: Jibill means a multitude: Satan 'led astray a great multitude (jibillan kathīrā) of you' (36:62). 'Fear Him who created you and the former generations (al-jibilla al-awwalīn)' (26:184).
quranUsage: Occurs 41 times, mostly as al-jibāl, 'the mountains': 'We made the mountains as pegs' (78:7). Mountains show Allah's power — 'you see the mountains, thinking them firm, while they pass like clouds' (27:88) — and at the Hour 'the mountains will be set in motion' (81:3).

primaryMeaning: Effort to the utmost, strain. Juhd and jahd are exertion; jāhada is to strive hard against something that resists — the self, Satan or an enemy. Jihād is such striving in the way of Allah.
extendedMeaning: 'Those who strive (jāhadū) for Us — We will surely guide them to Our ways' (29:69). Jahda aymānihim, 'their strongest oaths', uses the sense of utmost effort (5:53).
quranUsage: Occurs 41 times. Jāhadū, 'they strove', is paired with believing and emigrating: 'those who believed, emigrated and strove (jāhadū) in the way of Allah' (2:218). 'Strive (jāhidū) in His way, that you may succeed' (5:35). Striving is with 'wealth and lives' (4:95).

primaryMeaning: To go around something, to circle it. Ṭawāf is walking around the Kaaba; ṭā'ifa is a group — a portion of people gathered around something; ṭā'if is something that comes circling round, like a passing thought.
extendedMeaning: When 'a passing thought (ṭā'ifun) from Satan touches them', the God-conscious remember Allah and see clearly (7:201).
quranUsage: Occurs 41 times, mostly as ṭā'ifa, 'a group' or 'a party': 'a party (ṭā'ifatun) of the People of the Book wish to lead you astray' (3:69). 'Let them circle (wal-yaṭṭawwafū) the Ancient House' (22:29), and Ibrahim and Ismail were told to purify the House 'for those who circle it (lil-ṭā'ifīn)' (2:125).

primaryMeaning: To dislike, to find something hateful. Karh is being made to do what one dislikes — compulsion — and kurh is hardship borne unwillingly.
extendedMeaning: 'His mother carried him with hardship (kurhan) and gave birth to him with hardship' (46:15). 'There is no compulsion (ikrāha) in religion' (2:256).
quranUsage: Occurs 41 times. 'Perhaps you dislike (takrahū) a thing and it is good for you' (2:216). Some things are done 'willingly or unwillingly (karhan)': 'to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly' (3:83). Wives may not be inherited 'by compulsion (karhan)' (4:19).

primaryMeaning: To drive away and keep far off. Laʿna, 'a curse', is classically explained as being driven away from Allah's mercy.
extendedMeaning: Mubāhala, in which each side invokes 'the curse (laʿnata) of Allah upon the liars', is proposed in 3:61. Satan was cursed (laʿanahu) by Allah (4:118).
quranUsage: Occurs 41 times. 'Allah has cursed them (laʿanahumu) for their disbelief' (2:88). Those who hide what Allah revealed are 'cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse' (2:159). 'Upon them is the curse (laʿnatu) of Allah, the angels and all people' (2:161).

primaryMeaning: To perceive something finely. Classical lexicographers link it to shaʿr, 'hair' — perceiving something as fine as a hair. Shuʿūr is awareness; shāʿir, 'poet', is one of fine perception; shaʿā'ir are marks or symbols by which something is known.
extendedMeaning: The deniers called the Prophet 'a poet (shāʿirun)' (21:5), and the Quran answers, 'it is not the word of a poet' (69:41). 'Whoever honours the symbols (shaʿā'ir) of Allah — that is from the piety of hearts' (22:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 40 times, mostly in lā yashʿurūna, 'they do not perceive': the hypocrites 'deceive only themselves, and they do not perceive it' (2:9). The martyrs are alive, 'but you do not perceive (tashʿurūn)' (2:154). Shaʿā'ir Allāh, 'the symbols of Allah', include Safa and Marwa (2:158).

primaryMeaning: To split and cut open — fallāḥ, 'farmer', is one who splits the soil. Falāḥ, 'success', is winning through to what one seeks, as the seed breaks through the ground.
extendedMeaning: 'He has succeeded (aflaḥa) who purifies it' — the soul (91:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 40 times. The God-conscious 'are the successful (al-mufliḥūn)' (2:5). Laʿallakum tufliḥūn, 'that you may succeed', closes many commands (2:189). 'The wrongdoers will not succeed (lā yufliḥu)' (6:21). 'The believers have succeeded (qad aflaḥa)' (23:1).

primaryMeaning: To fill. Mala' are the chiefs or notables of a people — those who 'fill the eye' with their standing, or who are full of counsel.
extendedMeaning: Al-mala' al-aʿlā, 'the exalted assembly', are the angels (37:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 40 times, mostly as al-mala', 'the chiefs', who usually lead the rejection of prophets: 'the chiefs (al-mala') of his people said, "We see you in clear error"' (7:60). It describes Pharaoh and 'his chiefs (mala'ihi)' (7:103). Satan was told, 'I will fill (la-amla'anna) Hell with you all' (7:18).

primaryMeaning: The tail, the end of a thing — and from it, dhanb, 'sin', classically explained as a deed whose consequences follow after it, like a tail.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah forgives all sins (al-dhunūb)' (39:53).
quranUsage: Occurs 39 times. 'Allah seized them for their sins (bi-dhunūbihim)' (3:11). 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins (dhunūbanā)' (3:16). 'Follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins (dhunūbakum)' (3:31). 'Who forgives sins except Allah?' (3:135).

primaryMeaning: Power and dominance — having a strong hand over something. Sulṭān is authority, and also a proof or argument that carries authority.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah gives power (yusalliṭu) to His messengers over whom He wills' (59:6). Musa was sent 'with Our signs and a clear authority (sulṭānin)' (11:96).
quranUsage: Occurs 39 times, often meaning 'proof': false gods are worshipped with no authority, for 'Allah has not sent down any proof (sulṭānan) for them' (3:151), and 'bring us a clear proof (bi-sulṭānin mubīn)' (14:10). Satan has no power over the true servants: 'over My servants you have no authority (sulṭānun)' (15:42).

primaryMeaning: To drink. Sharāb is a drink; mashrab is a drinking place; shirb is a share of water.
extendedMeaning: 'Their hearts were made to drink in (ushribū) the calf' — love of it soaked into them (2:93). Milk is given 'pure, pleasant to drinkers (lil-shāribīn)' (16:66).
quranUsage: Occurs 39 times. 'Eat and drink (ishrabū) from the provision of Allah' (2:60), and 'each people knew its drinking place (mashrabahum)' (2:60). In Paradise the righteous drink 'from a cup mixed with camphor' (76:5), and their Lord 'gave them a pure drink (sharāban)' (76:21).

primaryMeaning: To overflow, to go past every limit — as floodwater rises beyond its banks. Ṭughyān is transgression beyond all bounds; ṭāghūt is anything worshipped or obeyed beyond Allah.
extendedMeaning: The literal sense of overflowing: 'when the water overflowed (ṭaghā), We carried you in the ship' (69:11). 'Man transgresses (la-yaṭghā) when he sees himself self-sufficient' (96:6–7).
quranUsage: Occurs 39 times. Pharaoh 'has transgressed (ṭaghā)' (20:24). Allah 'leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression (ṭughyānihim)' (2:15). Al-ṭāghūt is what must be rejected: 'whoever disbelieves in al-ṭāghūt and believes in Allah has grasped the firmest handhold' (2:256).

primaryMeaning: To test and try — to put something through use until its true nature shows, as a garment is worn thin. Balā' is a trial, whether by good or by hardship.
extendedMeaning: Pharaoh's oppression 'was a great trial (balā'un) from your Lord' (2:49). Death and life were created 'to test you (li-yabluwakum), which of you is best in deeds' (67:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 38 times. 'We will surely test you (la-nabluwannakum) with something of fear and hunger' (2:155). Tests come through good as well as evil: 'We test you (nablūkum) with evil and good as a trial' (21:35). Allah made people differ 'to test you (li-yabluwakum) in what He has given you' (5:48).

primaryMeaning: To scatter, as seed is scattered. Dhurriyya, 'offspring', are the descendants spread out from a person; dharra is the smallest thing — a speck or a tiny ant.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever does an atom's weight (dharratin) of good will see it' (99:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 38 times. Ibrahim asked, 'and of my offspring (dhurriyyatī)?' (2:124). Allah drew out from the children of Adam 'their descendants (dhurriyyatahum)' and took their testimony (7:172). Dharra, 'an atom's weight', measures deeds: 'Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom (dharratin)' (4:40).

primaryMeaning: To open. From opening come victory — opening a city or a way through — and judgment, which opens a closed matter; al-Fattāḥ is the One who opens and judges. Miftāḥ is a key.
extendedMeaning: 'When the help of Allah comes, and the victory (al-fatḥ)' (110:1). Surah 1, Al-Fātiḥa, is 'the Opening' of the Book.
quranUsage: Occurs 38 times. 'Indeed We have given you a clear victory (fatḥan mubīnā)' (48:1). 'With Him are the keys (mafātiḥ) of the unseen' (6:59). Nuh prayed, 'judge (fa-ftaḥ) between me and them with a decisive judgment (fatḥan)' (26:118).

primaryMeaning: To settle and stay firmly in place. Qarār is a settled abode; mustaqarr is a place of dwelling; qurrat al-ʿayn, 'coolness of the eye', is joy — the eye settles and rests when it sees what it loves.
extendedMeaning: 'Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring coolness of eyes (qurrata aʿyun)' (25:74). The glass of Paradise is qawārīr, clear crystal — named for water settling in it (76:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 38 times. 'On the earth you will have a dwelling (mustaqarrun) and provision for a time' (2:36). Allah 'made the earth a firm abode (qarāran)' (27:61). Musa was returned to his mother 'so that her eye might be cooled (taqarra)' (20:40).

primaryMeaning: Imru' is a man or a person, and imra'a a woman or wife. The root also carries the sense of being wholesome and pleasant to take in.
extendedMeaning: 'The Day a man (al-mar') will see what his hands have sent ahead' (78:40). The dowry may be enjoyed 'with pleasure and ease (hanī'an marī'ā)' (4:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 38 times. Imra'a often means 'wife': 'the wife (imra'atu) of ʿImrān' (3:35), the wife of Lut (7:83), and 'the wife of Pharaoh', given as an example of faith (66:11). 'Every person (imri'in) will be accountable for what he earned' (52:21).

primaryMeaning: To fall from a height — the space between sky and earth is hawā', 'air'. Hawā, 'desire', is the self's inclination; it is classically named for the way it drags a person down.
extendedMeaning: 'As for the one who restrained the soul from desire (al-hawā), Paradise will be his refuge' (79:40–41). Ibrahim prayed that hearts would 'incline (tahwī)' towards his family in Makkah (14:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 38 times, mostly as ahwā', 'desires', in warnings against following them: 'if you were to follow their desires (ahwā'ahum) after the knowledge that came to you' (2:120). The one who 'followed his desire (hawāhu)' is like a panting dog (7:176). 'Have you seen the one who takes his desire (hawāhu) as his god?' (45:23).

primaryMeaning: Ālā' are favours and blessings. The root also gives ālā, 'to fall short' or 'to swear' (to vow not to do something).
extendedMeaning: Ālā, 'to swear', appears in the ruling on those who 'swear off (yu'lūna) their wives' (2:226). The hypocrites 'will not fall short (lā ya'lūnakum) in harming you' (3:118).
quranUsage: Occurs 37 times, 32 of them in the refrain of Surah Al-Raḥmān: 'So which of the favours (ālā'i) of your Lord will you both deny?' (55:13). Hud reminded ʿĀd, 'remember the bounties (ālā') of Allah' (7:69).

primaryMeaning: To go ahead, to get somewhere first, to win a race. Sabq is precedence; istabaqa is to race one another.
extendedMeaning: 'No community can advance (tasbiqu) its term, nor delay it' (15:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 37 times. 'Race (fa-stabiqū) to all that is good' (2:148). Al-sābiqūn, 'the forerunners', are the first believers (9:100) and the nearest to Allah (56:10). 'A word had gone before (sabaqat) from your Lord' — a prior decree that delays judgment (10:19).

primaryMeaning: Not to recognise — the opposite of maʿrifa. Munkar is what the sound heart does not recognise as good — wrongdoing; ankara is to deny; nakīr is disapproval and punishment.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf's brothers came to him, 'and he knew them, but they did not recognise him (munkirūn)' (12:58).
quranUsage: Occurs 37 times, most often as al-munkar, 'the wrong', set against al-maʿrūf: believers 'enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong (al-munkar)' (3:104). 'Allah forbids immorality, wrongdoing (al-munkar) and oppression' (16:90). Nakīr describes Allah's punishment: 'how was My disapproval (nakīri)!' (22:44).

primaryMeaning: To go back to a place for shelter, to take refuge. Āwā is to give shelter; ma'wā is a refuge or abode.
extendedMeaning: The youths 'took refuge (awā) in the cave' (18:10). Those who 'gave shelter (āwaw) and help' — the Ansar — are praised (8:72).
quranUsage: Occurs 36 times, mostly as ma'wā, 'abode': 'their abode (ma'wāhum) is Hell' (3:197), and 'Gardens of refuge (al-ma'wā)' for believers (32:19). 'Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter (fa-āwā)?' (93:6).

primaryMeaning: To be lost, void and worthless — to come to nothing. Bāṭil is falsehood, what has no reality; abṭala is to render something null.
extendedMeaning: Reflecting on creation, the believers say, 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain (bāṭilan)' (3:191).
quranUsage: Occurs 36 times. 'Do not mix the truth with falsehood (bil-bāṭil)' (2:42). 'Truth has come and falsehood (al-bāṭil) has vanished; falsehood is bound to vanish' (17:81). 'Do not nullify (lā tubṭilū) your charities with reminders and hurt' (2:264).

primaryMeaning: To happen, to be new. Ḥadath is a new event; ḥadīth is speech or a report — news of what has happened; muḥdath is something newly come.
extendedMeaning: 'No new (muḥdathin) reminder comes to them from their Lord except that they listen to it while they play' (21:2). 'As for the favour of your Lord, speak of it (fa-ḥaddith)' (93:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 36 times, mostly as ḥadīth, 'narration' or 'speech': 'Has the story (ḥadīthu) of Musa reached you?' (20:9). The Quran is called 'the best of narrations (aḥsan al-ḥadīth)' (39:23). Allah taught Yusuf 'the interpretation of events (al-aḥādīth)' (12:6).

primaryMeaning: Doubt that brings unease — suspicion that disturbs the heart. Rayb is doubt; irtāba is to fall into doubt; murīb is disquieting.
extendedMeaning: The Day of Resurrection is 'a Day about which there is no doubt (lā rayba fīh)' (3:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 36 times. 'This is the Book about which there is no doubt (lā rayba)' (2:2). The challenge: 'if you are in doubt (raybin) about what We sent down, produce a surah like it' (2:23). True believers 'believed in Allah and His Messenger, then did not doubt (lam yartābū)' (49:15).

primaryMeaning: To join one thing to another. Qarn, 'horn', joins the head; qarn, 'generation', is a people joined in one time; qarīn is a close companion, joined to someone.
extendedMeaning: On the Day of Judgment the criminals will be seen 'bound together (muqarranīn) in chains' (14:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 36 times. Qarn most often means 'generation': 'How many generations (qarnin) before them did We destroy?' (6:6). Qarīn is a constant companion, including a devil: 'his companion (qarīnuhu) will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress"' (50:27). Dhū al-Qarnayn, 'the one with two horns', is the ruler of 18:83.

primaryMeaning: To cut, to sever. Qaṭaʿa is to cut something off or apart; taqaṭṭaʿa is to be cut into pieces; qiṭʿ is a portion — a part of the night.
extendedMeaning: Lut was told to travel 'in a part (bi-qiṭʿin) of the night' (11:81). On the Day of Judgment 'the bonds between you have been cut (taqaṭṭaʿa)' (6:94).
quranUsage: Occurs 36 times. The wrongdoers 'cut (yaqṭaʿūna) what Allah commanded to be joined' — ties of kinship (2:27). Pharaoh threatened, 'I will cut off (la-uqaṭṭiʿanna) your hands and feet' (7:124). The punishment for theft is set in 5:38.

primaryMeaning: A time or period — a stretch of time, short or long, whose length is not fixed.
extendedMeaning: 'Glorify Allah when (ḥīna) you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' (30:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 35 times. 'On the earth you will have provision for a time (ilā ḥīnin)' (2:36). 'Has there come upon man a period (ḥīnun) of time when he was nothing worth mentioning?' (76:1). Ḥīna, 'when', marks a moment: 'the patient in poverty and hardship, and at the time (ḥīna) of battle' (2:177).

primaryMeaning: To erase, as the wind wipes away traces in the sand — and to leave something alone. ʿAfw, 'pardon', is wiping away a wrong; it also means surplus — what is left over.
extendedMeaning: When asked what to spend, the answer was 'the surplus (al-ʿafw)' (2:219). 'Let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah should forgive you?' (24:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 35 times. 'Allah has pardoned (ʿafā) you' (3:152). Al-ʿAfuww, 'the Oft-Pardoning', is a name of Allah (4:43). People are urged to pardon one another: 'pardon (fa-ʿfu) them and ask forgiveness for them' (3:159), and 'to forgo (taʿfū) is nearer to piety' (2:237).

primaryMeaning: To leave something unnoticed — heedlessness that comes from inattention rather than ignorance. Ghafla is heedlessness; ghāfil is one who is unaware.
extendedMeaning: 'Warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter is decided, while they are in heedlessness (ghafla)' (19:39).
quranUsage: Occurs 35 times. 'Allah is not unaware (bi-ghāfilin) of what you do' (2:74). The heedless are warned: 'They are like cattle — rather, more astray; they are the heedless (al-ghāfilūn)' (7:179). 'Remember your Lord within yourself … and do not be among the heedless (al-ghāfilīn)' (7:205).

primaryMeaning: A plan to harm someone by hidden means — a plot or trick. When used of Allah, it means His planning that undoes the plotters.
extendedMeaning: 'They are plotting a plot (yakīdūna kaydā), and I am planning a plan' (86:15–16). Yusuf said of the women, 'unless You turn their plot (kaydahunna) away from me' (12:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 35 times. Yaʿqub warned Yusuf, 'they will plot against you a plot (kaydan)' (12:5). 'What they have made is only a magician's trick (kaydu)' (20:69). 'My plan (kaydī) is firm' (7:183). 'The plot (kayda) of Satan is ever weak' (4:76).

primaryMeaning: To pass by, to go past. Marra is to pass; marra (noun) is 'a time', one pass of something. Murr, 'bitter', is a separate branch of the root.
extendedMeaning: The Hour is 'more grievous and more bitter (amarr)' (54:46).
quranUsage: Occurs 35 times. Marra means 'once' or 'a time': 'you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time (awwala marratin)' (6:94), and 'divorce is twice (marratān)' (2:229). 'The servants of the Most Merciful … when they pass (marrū) by idle talk, pass by with dignity' (25:72).

primaryMeaning: To inherit — to receive what another leaves behind. Mīrāth is inheritance; awratha is to make someone inherit.
extendedMeaning: Allah is 'the best of inheritors (al-wārithīn)' (21:89) — all things return to Him. 'To Allah belongs the heritage (mīrāth) of the heavens and the earth' (3:180).
quranUsage: Occurs 35 times. The inheritance shares are set out in 4:11–12 and 4:176. The righteous inherit Paradise: 'This is the Garden you have been made to inherit (ūrithtumūhā)' (7:43). 'The earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance (yūrithuhā) to whom He wills' (7:128).

primaryMeaning: To lean or incline to one side. Janāḥ is a wing — a bird's side — or a person's side; junāḥ, 'blame', is leaning away from what is right.
extendedMeaning: 'Lower to them the wing (janāḥa) of humility out of mercy' — to parents (17:24). 'Lower your wing (janāḥaka) to the believers' (15:88).
quranUsage: Occurs 34 times, mostly in lā junāḥa, 'there is no blame', which permits: 'there is no blame (junāḥa) on him to walk between them' — Safa and Marwa (2:158), and 'no blame on you for seeking bounty from your Lord' (2:198). 'If they incline (janaḥū) to peace, incline to it too' (8:61).

primaryMeaning: To be hidden, to conceal. Khafiya is to be concealed; akhfā is to hide something; istakhfā is to try to hide oneself.
extendedMeaning: 'Call on your Lord humbly and privately (khufyatan)' (7:55).
quranUsage: Occurs 34 times. 'Nothing is hidden (lā yakhfā) from Allah in the earth or in the heaven' (3:5). 'Whether you reveal what is in yourselves or conceal it (tukhfūhu), Allah will call you to account for it' (2:284). 'They try to hide (yastakhfūna) from people, but cannot hide from Allah' (4:108).

primaryMeaning: To mock, to make fun of someone. Istahza'a is to ridicule; huzuw is mockery.
extendedMeaning: When Musa told his people to slaughter a cow, they asked, 'Do you take us in ridicule (huzuwan)?' (2:67).
quranUsage: Occurs 34 times, mostly for mocking prophets and revelation: 'messengers before you were mocked (ustuhzi'a)' (6:10), and 'there will come to them the news of what they used to mock (yastahzi'ūn)' (6:5).
