The hypocrites tell their devils, 'we were only mocking (mustahzi'ūn)'; 'Allah mocks them' in return (2:14–15).

primaryMeaning: To bind firmly, to make fast. Wathāq is a strong tie; mīthāq is a binding covenant; thiqa is trust — relying on something firm.
extendedMeaning: Al-ʿurwa al-wuthqā, 'the firmest handhold', is held by whoever rejects false gods and believes in Allah (2:256). Marriage is called 'a firm covenant (mīthāqan ghalīẓā)' (4:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 34 times, mostly as mīthāq, 'covenant': 'We took the covenant (mīthāqa) of the Children of Israel' (2:83), and 'We raised the mountain above you' when taking it (2:63). Breaking it is condemned: 'for their breaking of their covenant (mīthāqahum)' (4:155).

primaryMeaning: The side of something. Jānib is a side or flank; ijtanaba is to keep something to one side — to avoid it; junub is one who has been put aside from prayer until purified.
extendedMeaning: Junub, 'in a state of impurity', appears in the rulings of prayer and ablution (4:43). A soul will say, 'Alas for me, for what I neglected in regard to Allah (fī janbi Allāh)' (39:56).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. Ijtanaba, 'to avoid', is used for keeping away from wrong: 'avoid (ijtanibū) false gods' (16:36), and believers 'avoid (yajtanibūna) the major sins' (42:37). Jānib, 'side', appears in Musa being called 'from the right side (jānibi) of the Mount' (19:52).

primaryMeaning: To head towards something with purpose. Ḥajj is setting out for the House of Allah — the pilgrimage; ḥujja is an argument or proof, which heads straight for its goal; ḥājja is to argue.
extendedMeaning: 'To Allah belongs the conclusive argument (al-ḥujja al-bāligha)' (6:149).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. 'Complete the Hajj (al-ḥajj) and the ʿumra for Allah' (2:196), and 'pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah' (3:97). Ḥujja, 'argument': 'so that people will have no argument (ḥujjatun) against you' (2:150). Ibrahim argued with the king 'who argued (ḥājja) with him about his Lord' (2:258).

primaryMeaning: The sun.
extendedMeaning: Surah 91 opens 'By the sun (wal-shams) and its brightness' (91:1). Prayer is to be established 'from the decline of the sun (al-shams)' (17:78). The Queen of Sheba's people 'prostrate to the sun (lil-shams)' (27:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, often as a sign of Allah's order: 'the sun (al-shams) runs to its resting place' (36:38), and 'it is not for the sun to overtake the moon' (36:40). Ibrahim, seeing the sun set, turned from worshipping created things (6:78). The sun too prostrates to Allah (22:18).

primaryMeaning: Shade — the cover that keeps off the sun's heat. Ẓill is shade or shadow; ẓulla is a canopy; ẓalla, 'to remain', is literally to spend the daytime doing something.
extendedMeaning: Ẓalla, 'to become': when told of a daughter, 'his face becomes (ẓalla) dark' (16:58). 'The mountain was raised above them like a canopy (ẓulla)' (7:171).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. 'We shaded you (ẓallalnā) with clouds' in the desert (2:57). The righteous in Paradise are 'in shades (ẓilālin)' (36:56) and 'extended shade (ẓillin mamdūd)' (56:30). The people of the Fire have 'coverings (ẓulalun) of fire above them' (39:16).

primaryMeaning: Something raised up and roofed — a canopy, a trellis, a roof. ʿArsh is a raised seat, a throne; ʿarsh Allāh is the Throne of Allah, the greatest of His creation.
extendedMeaning: Maʿrūshāt, 'trellised gardens', are among Allah's blessings (6:141). A town 'fallen down upon its roofs (ʿurūshihā)' describes utter ruin (2:259).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, mostly for the Throne: 'then He rose over the Throne (al-ʿarsh)' (7:54), 'Lord of the Great Throne' (9:129), and 'His Throne (ʿarshuhu) was upon the water' (11:7). It is also used for human thrones — the Queen of Sheba's (27:23).

primaryMeaning: Blindness — losing sight, and by extension losing insight, being unable to see the truth.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever turns from My remembrance … We will raise him blind (aʿmā) on the Day of Resurrection' (20:124). Surah 80 begins with the Prophet frowning when 'the blind man (al-aʿmā) came to him' (80:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. The deniers are 'deaf, dumb and blind (ʿumyun)' (2:18) — unable to take in guidance. 'It is not the eyes that go blind (taʿmā), but the hearts in the breasts' (22:46). 'Are the blind (al-aʿmā) and the seeing equal?' (6:50).

primaryMeaning: To divide into parts. Qisma is a share. Aqsama, 'to swear', is traced by al-Rāghib to qasāma — oaths divided among the relatives of a murdered person.
extendedMeaning: The deniers' claim of daughters for Allah is 'an unjust division (qismatun ḍīzā)' (53:22). Relatives present at the division (al-qisma) of inheritance should be given something (4:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, mostly for oaths: 'I swear (uqsimu) by the positions of the stars' (56:75), and the deniers 'swore by Allah their strongest oaths' (6:109). Allah divides provision: 'We have divided (qasamnā) among them their livelihood' (43:32).

primaryMeaning: To be enough, to meet a need so nothing more is required.
extendedMeaning: 'We are sufficient for you (kafaynāka) against the mockers' (15:95).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, most often as wa kafā bi-llāh, 'Allah is sufficient', ending a verse: 'Allah is sufficient as Reckoner' (4:6), 'as Witness' (4:79), 'as Disposer of affairs' (4:81). 'Allah will suffice you (fa-sa-yakfīkahum) against them' (2:137). 'Is not Allah sufficient (bi-kāfin) for His servant?' (39:36).

primaryMeaning: Open land — barr is the dry land, as opposed to the sea. From its wide openness comes birr, 'righteousness' — broad, generous goodness in faith and deeds; barr is one who is dutiful and kind.
extendedMeaning: Yahya was 'dutiful (barran) to his parents' (19:14). Believers may 'deal kindly (tabarrūhum) and justly' with those who do not fight them (60:8). Barr, 'land': 'the game of the sea is lawful for you, but the game of the land (al-barr) is forbidden while in iḥrām' (5:96).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. Birr is defined in 2:177: 'righteousness (al-birr) is not that you turn your faces east or west, but it is believing in Allah … giving wealth … establishing prayer'. 'You will not attain righteousness (al-birr) until you spend from what you love' (3:92). Al-abrār, 'the righteous', are in bliss (76:5).

primaryMeaning: A camel kneeling and settling firmly on the ground. Baraka, 'blessing', is lasting good that settles in a thing and increases; tabāraka, 'blessed is He', is the praise of Allah's abundant good.
extendedMeaning: The land around al-Aqṣā is 'which We blessed (bāraknā) around it' (17:1). Surah 67 opens, 'Blessed is He (tabāraka) in whose hand is the dominion'.
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. Tabāraka describes Allah: 'Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds' (7:54), 'Blessed is Allah, the best of creators' (23:14). Mubārak, 'blessed', describes the Quran (6:92), the House in Makkah (3:96) and the olive tree (24:35).

primaryMeaning: Three. Thulth is a third, and thālith is the third.
extendedMeaning: The people of the Cave stayed 'three hundred (thalātha mi'atin) years, and added nine' (18:25). The Prophet stood in prayer 'nearly two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it' (73:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. The waiting period of divorced women is 'three (thalāthata) menstrual cycles' (2:228). The Quran rejects the Trinity: 'Do not say "Three (thalāthatun)"; desist' (4:171), and 'they have disbelieved who say Allah is the third of three (thālithu thalāthatin)' (5:73). Thulth, 'a third', appears in the inheritance shares (4:11).

primaryMeaning: To resist and refuse to comply — to disobey. Maʿṣiya is disobedience, and ʿāṣī is one who disobeys.
extendedMeaning: Yahya was 'not a tyrant, nor disobedient (ʿaṣiyyā)' (19:14). The secret talk of hypocrites is of 'sin, aggression and disobedience (maʿṣiyat) to the Messenger' (58:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. 'Adam disobeyed (ʿaṣā) his Lord and erred' (20:121). The Israelites said, 'We hear and disobey (ʿaṣaynā)' (2:93). 'Whoever disobeys (yaʿṣi) Allah and His Messenger … will have a humiliating punishment' (4:14).

primaryMeaning: To stretch and extend — to lengthen something or add to it continuously. Madd is extension; madad and imdād are supply and reinforcement.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not extend (lā tamuddanna) your eyes towards what We have given some of them to enjoy' (15:88). The sea as ink, 'even if We brought the like of it as a supply (madadan)' (18:109).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. 'He spread out (madda) the earth' (13:3). Allah reinforces the believers: 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforces you (yumiddakum) with three thousand angels?' (3:124). Allah 'extends (yamudduhum)' the wrongdoers in their transgression (2:15).

primaryMeaning: To set something up, to raise it upright. Naṣb is setting up; nuṣub are stones set up for worship; naṣīb is one's appointed share; naṣab is toil — standing up to hard work.
extendedMeaning: 'When you are free, stand up (fa-nṣab) to worship' (94:7). 'Do not forget your share (naṣībaka) of the world' (28:77).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times, mostly as naṣīb, 'a share': 'for them is a share (naṣībun) of what they earned' (2:202). Al-anṣāb, 'stone altars', are 'defilement from the work of Satan' (5:90). Naṣab, 'fatigue', is borne in Allah's way and rewarded (9:120).

primaryMeaning: To hide something behind something else. Warā', 'behind', is what is hidden from view; it can mean what is past or what lies ahead, since both are out of sight. Wārā is to cover or conceal.
extendedMeaning: 'Before him (min warā'ihi) is Hell' (14:16). Ishaq was promised, 'and after (warā'i) Ishaq, Yaʿqub' (11:71).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times, mostly as warā'. Throwing the Book 'behind (warā'a) their backs' means ignoring it (2:101). Warā'ihim, 'before them', means what lies ahead: 'behind them is a barrier until the Day they are raised' (23:100). The crow showed Qabil 'how to hide (yuwārī) the body of his brother' (5:31).

primaryMeaning: To be wide and roomy — the opposite of narrowness. Saʿa is abundance and capacity; wusʿ is what one is able to bear; al-Wāsiʿ is the All-Encompassing.
extendedMeaning: 'My earth is spacious (wāsiʿatun), so worship Me' (29:56). 'Your Lord is vast (wāsiʿu) in forgiveness' (53:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. 'Allah is All-Encompassing (wāsiʿun), All-Knowing' (2:115). 'His Throne extends over (wasiʿa) the heavens and the earth' (2:255). 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity (wusʿahā)' (2:286).

primaryMeaning: To join and connect — to link one's instruction to another's action. Waṣṣā is to enjoin or charge someone with something; waṣiyya is a will or a solemn instruction.
extendedMeaning: Believers 'enjoin one another (tawāṣaw) to truth and enjoin one another to patience' (103:3), and 'to mercy' (90:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. Allah's commands: 'This He has enjoined on you (waṣṣākum), that you may reason' (6:151), and 'We have enjoined (waṣṣaynā) on man goodness to his parents' (29:8). Waṣiyya, 'a bequest', precedes inheritance: 'after any bequest (waṣiyyatin) he made or debt' (4:11).

primaryMeaning: To appear, to become plain. Badā is to show itself; abdā is to reveal. Bādiya, 'the open desert', is where everything is in plain view.
extendedMeaning: Women are told 'not to display (yubdīna) their adornment' except to those named (24:31). Yusuf spoke of his family coming 'from the desert (al-badw)' (12:100).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. On the Day of Judgment 'there will appear (badā) to them from Allah what they had not expected' (39:47). 'If you disclose (tubdū) your charities, it is good' (2:271). Allah knows 'what you reveal (tubdūna) and what you conceal' (2:33).

primaryMeaning: To be free, clear of something — free of a debt, a disease or blame. Al-Bāri' is the Creator who brings creation into being free of imperfection; bariyya is creation.
extendedMeaning: ʿĪsā healed 'the blind and the leper' — ubri'u, 'I heal', making them free of disease (3:49). The believers who do good 'are the best of creation (al-bariyya)' (98:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Barī', 'free of', declares a break: 'I am free (barī'un) of what you associate' (6:19), and barā'a, 'a declaration of disassociation', opens Surah 9 (9:1). Al-Bāri', 'the Maker', is a name of Allah (59:24), and Musa called his people to repent 'to your Maker (bāri'ikum)' (2:54).

primaryMeaning: Ḥaythu means 'where' or 'wherever' — a word of place.
extendedMeaning: 'He will provide for him from where (min ḥaythu) he does not expect' (65:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Adam and his wife were told, 'eat from it wherever (ḥaythu) you will' (2:35). 'Wherever (ḥaythu) you are, turn your faces towards it' — the Sacred Mosque (2:144). 'Allah knows best where (ḥaythu) to place His message' (6:124).

primaryMeaning: To be pure, clear of any mixture. Akhlaṣa is to make something pure for someone alone; ikhlāṣ is sincerity — doing a thing for Allah alone. Mukhlaṣ is one whom Allah has purified and chosen.
extendedMeaning: 'Is not pure (al-khāliṣ) religion for Allah alone?' (39:3). Musa was 'chosen (mukhlaṣan)' (19:51).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'Worship Allah, making the religion sincerely (mukhliṣan) His' (39:2). Satan cannot mislead 'Your chosen servants (al-mukhlaṣīn)' (15:40), among them Yusuf (12:24). Surah 112 is named Al-Ikhlāṣ, 'Sincerity'.

primaryMeaning: Evil, harm, wickedness — the opposite of khayr, 'good'. Sharar is a spark that flies out and burns.
extendedMeaning: The slander against ʿĀ'isha was not 'bad (sharran) for you; rather it is good for you' (24:11). Sharar, 'sparks', are thrown from Hell 'as huge as castles' (77:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'Perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad (sharrun) for you' (2:216). The last surahs seek refuge 'from the evil (sharri) of what He created' (113:2). 'The worst (sharra) of creatures with Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason' (8:22).

primaryMeaning: To pair — to add one to another so that it becomes two. Shafʿ is an even number; shafāʿa, 'intercession', is joining one's plea to another's to support them.
extendedMeaning: 'By the even (wal-shafʿ) and the odd' (89:3). 'Whoever intercedes (yashfaʿ) for a good cause will have a share of it' (4:85).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. On the Day of Judgment 'no intercession (shafāʿatun) will be accepted from it' (2:48), and 'who can intercede (yashfaʿu) with Him except by His permission?' (2:255). 'Intercession (al-shafāʿa) will not benefit except for whom the Most Merciful permits' (20:109).

primaryMeaning: To be clean and pure — the opposite of najas, 'impurity'. Ṭahāra is purity of body and of heart; ṭahhara is to purify; muṭahhar is purified.
extendedMeaning: The spouses of Paradise are 'purified (muṭahhara)' (2:25). Lut's people mocked the believers as 'people who keep themselves pure (yataṭahharūn)' (7:82). 'None touch it except the purified (al-muṭahharūn)' (56:79).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Allah wants 'to purify you (li-yuṭahhirakum)' through ablution (5:6), and 'loves those who purify themselves (al-mutaṭahhirīn)' (2:222). Ibrahim and Ismail were told, 'purify (ṭahhirā) My House' (2:125). Rain is 'pure water (mā'an ṭahūrā)' (25:48).

primaryMeaning: To overcome, to get the upper hand. Ghalaba is to defeat; ghālib is victorious.
extendedMeaning: Surah 30 opens, 'The Romans have been defeated (ghulibat) … but after their defeat they will overcome (sa-yaghlibūn)' (30:2–3). 'Allah is predominant (ghālibun) over His affair' (12:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'The party of Allah — they are the victorious (al-ghālibūn)' (5:56). 'How many a small group has overcome (ghalabat) a large group by Allah's permission' (2:249). 'If Allah helps you, none can overcome (ghāliba) you' (3:160).

primaryMeaning: To sit down, and to stay behind, remaining in place. Maqʿad is a seat or position; qawāʿid are foundations — what a structure sits on.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim and Ismail 'raised the foundations (al-qawāʿid) of the House' (2:127). The Prophet placed the believers 'in positions (maqāʿida) for battle' (3:121).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Believers remember Allah 'standing, sitting (quʿūdan) and on their sides' (3:191). Those who strive are not equal to 'those who sit (al-qāʿidīn)' at home (4:95). 'Do not sit (lā taqʿudū) with them' while they mock Allah's verses (4:140).

primaryMeaning: To stay, to remain somewhere for a while.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf 'remained (fa-labitha) in prison some years' (12:42).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times, often about how long someone stayed, and how short it seems: 'you will think you had remained (labithtum) only a little' (17:52). The man raised after a hundred years said, 'I have remained (labithtu) a day or part of a day' (2:259). The people of the Cave asked one another how long they had stayed (18:19).

primaryMeaning: To leave, to break off from something or someone. Hijra is leaving one's land for another — emigration; hajr is abandoning; muhājir is an emigrant.
extendedMeaning: 'Leave (fa-hjur) all impurity' (74:5). The Messenger will say, 'My people took this Quran as something abandoned (mahjūrā)' (25:30).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'Those who believed, emigrated (hājarū) and strove in the way of Allah — they hope for Allah's mercy' (2:218). Al-muhājirūn, 'the emigrants', and the Ansar are praised together (9:100). 'Whoever emigrates (yuhājir) in the way of Allah will find on earth many places of refuge' (4:100).

primaryMeaning: To turn something from its true direction, to overturn it. Ifk is a lie that turns the truth on its head; affāk is a habitual liar; al-mu'tafikāt are 'the overturned cities'.
extendedMeaning: Musa's staff 'swallowed what they falsified (ya'fikūn)' (7:117). Devils come down 'upon every sinful liar (affākin)' (26:222). Al-mu'tafikāt are the cities of Lut's people (69:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. Anna yu'fakūn, 'how are they turned away (from the truth)?', expresses wonder (5:75). Al-ifk, 'the slander', refers to the false accusation against ʿĀ'isha: 'those who came with the slander (bil-ifk) are a group among you' (24:11).

primaryMeaning: Female — softness and gentleness, the opposite of dhakar, 'male'. Unthā is a female; ināth are females.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever does righteousness, male or female (unthā), while a believer — We will give them a good life' (16:97).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'We created you from a male and a female (unthā)' (49:13). Maryam's mother said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female (unthā) … and the male is not like the female' (3:36). The Quran condemns calling angels or idols female (ināthan) (4:117; 53:21).

primaryMeaning: To walk quickly, to hurry towards something — and by extension to strive and work hard for it. Saʿy is effort; it is also the brisk walk between Safa and Marwa.
extendedMeaning: It also describes striving to cause harm: 'when he turns away, he strives (saʿā) in the land to cause corruption' (2:205). 'Hasten (fa-sʿaw) to the remembrance of Allah' when called to Friday prayer (62:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'Man will have only what he strives for (mā saʿā)' (53:39). A man came 'running (yasʿā)' from the far end of the city to warn Musa (28:20). Effort for the Hereafter is rewarded: 'their striving (saʿyuhum) will be appreciated' (17:19).

primaryMeaning: To turn something from one direction or state to another. Ṣarafa is to turn away; ṣarrafa is to turn something repeatedly — to present it in many ways; taṣrīf is varying and directing.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf prayed, 'unless You turn away (taṣrif) their plot from me' (12:33), and 'his Lord turned away (fa-ṣarafa) their plot from him' (12:34).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'See how We vary (nuṣarrifu) the signs' — presenting them in different ways (6:46), and 'We have diversified (ṣarrafnā) in this Quran' examples and warnings (17:41). Taṣrīf al-riyāḥ, 'the directing of the winds', is among His signs (2:164). 'How are you turned away (tuṣrafūn)?' (10:32).

primaryMeaning: ʿAsā means 'perhaps' or 'it may be' — expressing hope or expectation that something will happen.
extendedMeaning: 'Perhaps (ʿasā) Allah will put affection between you and those you are hostile to' (60:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'Perhaps (ʿasā) you dislike a thing and it is good for you' (2:216). Used of Allah, classical scholars note that ʿasā expresses something that will certainly happen: 'perhaps (ʿasā) your Lord will raise you to a praised station' (17:79).

primaryMeaning: To follow a trail step by step. Qaṣṣa is to relate a story — following events in order; qaṣaṣ is narrative; qiṣāṣ, 'retribution', is following up a deed with its exact equivalent.
extendedMeaning: Musa's mother told his sister, 'Follow him (quṣṣīhi)' (28:11); Musa and his servant 'went back following their tracks (qaṣaṣā)' (18:64). Surah 28 is Al-Qaṣaṣ, 'the Stories'.
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'We relate (naquṣṣu) to you the best of stories (aḥsan al-qaṣaṣ)' (12:3). 'Relate the stories (al-qaṣaṣ), that they may reflect' (7:176). 'In legal retribution (al-qiṣāṣ) there is life for you' (2:179).

primaryMeaning: To return and repent — hāda is classically explained as 'to turn back'. Alladhīna hādū, 'those who are Jewish', and al-yahūd, 'the Jews', are placed under this root, as is the name of the prophet Hūd.
extendedMeaning: Musa prayed, 'We have turned back (hudnā) to You' (7:156). Surah 11 is named Hūd.
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'Those who believed, and those who are Jewish (hādū), the Christians and the Sabians …' (2:62). 'The Jews (al-yahūd) and the Christians will not be pleased with you' (2:120). Hūd was sent to ʿĀd: 'O Hud (yā hūd), you have not brought us clear proof' (11:53).

primaryMeaning: To fold one thing over another, to double it. Ithnān is 'two'; mathnā is 'two by two'; thānī is 'second'; istathnā, 'to make an exception', is to fold something back out of a statement.
extendedMeaning: Al-mathānī, 'the oft-repeated', describes Al-Fātiḥa: 'We have given you seven of the oft-repeated' (15:87). The hypocrites 'fold up (yathnūna) their breasts' to hide (11:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. 'Marry those who please you of women, two (mathnā), three or four' (4:3). The Prophet in the cave was 'the second of two (thāniya ithnayn)' (9:40). 'Two (ithnatā) … twelve springs' gushed for the tribes (2:60).

primaryMeaning: To twist tightly, as rope is plaited. Jidāl, 'argument', is twisting words against an opponent to overcome them.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim 'argued with Us (yujādilunā)' for the people of Lut (11:74). Surah 58 is Al-Mujādila, 'she who disputes', about a woman pleading her case to the Prophet (58:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. 'Argue (jādilhum) with them in the way that is best' (16:125). 'Man is, more than anything, quarrelsome (jadalā)' (18:54). There is to be 'no disputing (jidāl) during Hajj' (2:197).

primaryMeaning: A host or army — a body of people gathered for a purpose. Jund are troops; junūd are hosts or armies.
extendedMeaning: Talut went out 'with the troops (bil-junūd)' (2:249).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. Pharaoh 'and his troops (junūduhu)' pursued the Israelites (10:90). 'To Allah belong the hosts (junūd) of the heavens and the earth' (48:4), and 'none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him' (74:31).

primaryMeaning: To know something through effort and skill — to come to know what was hidden. Adrā is to make someone know.
extendedMeaning: 'I do not know (adrī) whether what you are promised is near or far' (21:109).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times, often in wa mā adrāka, 'and what will make you know …?', which stresses that something is beyond ordinary knowing: 'And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?' (69:3). 'No soul knows (tadrī) what it will earn tomorrow, nor in what land it will die' (31:34).

primaryMeaning: To raise, to lift up — the opposite of lowering. Rafʿ is raising in place or in rank.
extendedMeaning: 'Good deeds raise it (yarfaʿuhu)' — the good word rising to Allah (35:10). Ibrahim and Ismail 'raised (yarfaʿu) the foundations of the House' (2:127).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. 'Allah is the one who raised (rafaʿa) the heavens without pillars you can see' (13:2). 'We raise (narfaʿu) in degrees whom We will' (6:83). 'We raised (rafaʿnā) the mountain above you' (2:63). Of ʿĪsā: 'Allah raised him (rafaʿahu) to Himself' (4:158).

primaryMeaning: To become, to come to a final state. Maṣīr is the destination — where a thing ends up.
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times, mostly as al-maṣīr, 'the destination': 'to You is the destination (al-maṣīr)' (2:285), and 'wretched is the destination' said of the Fire (2:126). 'To Allah all matters reach (taṣīru)' (42:53).

primaryMeaning: To fly. Ṭayr are birds; ṭā'ir is something that flies — and, because Arabs read omens from birds' flight, also one's fate or omen.
extendedMeaning: 'Your omen (ṭā'irukum) is with Allah' — the prophets' answer to people blaming them for misfortune (27:47). 'Every person's fate (ṭā'irahu) We have fastened to his neck' (17:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. Ibrahim was told, 'take four birds (al-ṭayr)' to see how the dead are raised (2:260). ʿĪsā made 'the shape of a bird (ṭayran)' by Allah's permission (3:49). The birds glorified Allah with Dawud (21:79).

primaryMeaning: To cover and overwhelm. Ghashiya is to come over something and cover it; ghishāwa is a covering over the eyes; al-ghāshiya is the Overwhelming — the Day of Judgment.
extendedMeaning: 'Has the story of the Overwhelming (al-ghāshiya) reached you?' (88:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. 'He covers (yughshī) the night with the day' (7:54). Slumber 'overcame (yaghshā) a group of you' at Uhud (3:154). The sea 'covered them (ghashiyahum)' — Pharaoh's army (20:78). 'On their eyes is a covering (ghishāwa)' (2:7).

primaryMeaning: To win through, to be saved — a desert (mafāza) was so called as a hopeful name, for one who crossed it had been saved. Fawz is triumph and success.
extendedMeaning: Those who believed, emigrated and strove 'are the successful (al-fā'izūn)' (9:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times, often in dhālika al-fawz al-ʿaẓīm, 'that is the great success' (4:13). 'Whoever is kept away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has succeeded (fāza)' (3:185). 'For the God-conscious is success (mafāzā)' (78:31).

primaryMeaning: Love and affection — warm attachment. Wadda is to love or to wish for something; mawadda is affection; al-Wadūd is the Most Loving.
extendedMeaning: 'He is the Forgiving, the Loving (al-Wadūd)' (85:14). Believers do not 'love (yuwāddūna) those who oppose Allah and His Messenger' (58:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 29 times. 'He placed between you affection (mawadda) and mercy' — between spouses (30:21). Many wish harm on the believers: 'they wish (waddū) you would suffer' (3:118). 'The Most Merciful will appoint for them affection (wuddā)' (19:96).

primaryMeaning: Abad is time without end — an unbounded future. Abadan means 'forever', or in negation 'never'.
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times, all as abadan. It describes eternity in Paradise — 'abiding therein forever (abadan)' (4:57) — and in the Fire (4:169). In negation it means 'never': 'they will never (abadan) wish for it' — death (2:95).

primaryMeaning: To be heavy — the opposite of khiffa, 'lightness'. Mithqāl is a weight or measure; thaqal is a burden; al-thaqalān, 'the two weighty ones', are humans and jinn.
extendedMeaning: 'Go forth, light or heavy (thiqālan)' (9:41). 'We will attend to you, O two weighty ones (al-thaqalān)' (55:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. Mithqāl dharra, 'an atom's weight', measures deeds: 'Allah does not wrong even an atom's weight' (4:40). 'Those whose scales are heavy (thaqulat) will be the successful' (7:8). The Quran is 'a weighty word (qawlan thaqīlā)' (73:5).

primaryMeaning: To return to a former state. Thawāb, 'reward', is what comes back to a person for their deed; thawb, 'garment', is classically explained as what the spun thread returns to; mathāba is a place people return to.
extendedMeaning: The Kaaba was made 'a place of return (mathābatan) for people' (2:125).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'Allah has with Him the best reward (ḥusn al-thawāb)' (3:195). 'Whoever wants the reward (thawāba) of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter' (4:134). 'Your garments (thiyābaka), purify them' (74:4).

primaryMeaning: To go around something on every side — to enclose it. Aḥāṭa is to encompass; muḥīṭ is one who surrounds and takes in everything; ḥā'iṭ is a wall.
extendedMeaning: 'Hell surely surrounds (la-muḥīṭatun) the disbelievers' (9:49). Al-Khiḍr asked Musa how he could be patient 'with what you have not encompassed (tuḥiṭ) in knowledge' (18:68).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'Allah encompasses (muḥīṭun) the disbelievers' (2:19). 'They encompass (yuḥīṭūna) nothing of His knowledge except what He wills' (2:255). 'Your Lord has encompassed (aḥāṭa) the people' (17:60).

primaryMeaning: To be empty, clear of anything else. Khalā is to be alone with someone, and to pass away — a time or people that has gone, leaving the place empty.
extendedMeaning: 'When the earth is stretched out, and casts out what is in it and becomes empty (takhallat)' (84:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'That was a community which has passed away (khalat)' (2:134). When the hypocrites 'are alone (khalaw) with their devils' they reveal their true views (2:14). 'Messengers had passed away (khalat) before him' (3:144).

primaryMeaning: To hope for something, to look forward to it. Rajā' is hope; it can also mean fear of what one expects. Arjā is to postpone.
extendedMeaning: Pharaoh's chiefs said, 'Postpone him (arjih) and his brother' (7:111).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'Those who believed, emigrated and strove — they hope (yarjūna) for the mercy of Allah' (2:218). 'Whoever hopes (yarjū) to meet his Lord, let him do righteous work' (18:110). Believers 'fear His punishment and hope (yarjūna) for His mercy' (17:57).

primaryMeaning: Seven. Sabʿūn is seventy. Sabuʿ, 'a beast of prey', shares the root.
extendedMeaning: 'We have given you seven (sabʿan) of the oft-repeated' — Al-Fātiḥa (15:87). Hell 'has seven gates' (15:44).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'He made them seven (sabʿa) heavens' (2:29). The king dreamt of 'seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones' (12:43). Musa chose 'seventy (sabʿīn) men' for the appointed meeting (7:155).

primaryMeaning: To split something apart. Shaqq is a crack; shiqāq is division and opposition — each side splitting off; mashaqqa is hardship, what splits one's strength.
extendedMeaning: 'The Day the heaven will split open (tashaqqaqu) with clouds' (25:25). 'The moon has split (inshaqqa)' (54:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'If they turn away, they are only in dissension (shiqāq)' (2:137). 'Whoever opposes (yushāqiqi) the Messenger after guidance has become clear' (4:115). Some stones 'split open (yashshaqqaqu) and water comes out' (2:74).

primaryMeaning: To make level and equal — to balance two sides. ʿAdl is justice, giving each its due; ʿadala bi- is to make something equal to another — to set up rivals to Allah; ʿadl is also an equivalent or ransom.
extendedMeaning: On the Day of Judgment 'no compensation (ʿadl) will be accepted' (2:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'Let a scribe write between you in justice (bil-ʿadl)' (2:282). 'Allah commands justice (bil-ʿadl) and good conduct' (16:90). 'If you fear you will not be just (taʿdilū), then marry only one' (4:3). The deniers 'set up equals (yaʿdilūna) to their Lord' (6:1).

primaryMeaning: To grow up and come into being. Ansha'a is to bring something into existence and raise it; nash'a is a creation or coming-into-being.
extendedMeaning: He 'produced (ansha'a) gardens, trellised and untrellised' (6:141).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. 'It is He who produced you (ansha'akum) from a single soul' (6:98). 'Travel in the land and see how He began creation, then Allah will produce the next creation (al-nash'a al-ākhira)' (29:20) — the resurrection. After each destroyed people, 'We raised (ansha'nā) another generation' (6:6).

primaryMeaning: Certainty — knowledge that has settled and leaves no doubt. Yaqīn is firm certainty; ayqana is to be sure.
extendedMeaning: 'This is the certain truth (ḥaqq al-yaqīn)' (56:95). The hoopoe brought Sulayman 'certain news (bi-naba'in yaqīn)' from Sheba (27:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 28 times. The God-conscious 'are certain (yūqinūn) of the Hereafter' (2:4). 'Worship your Lord until the certainty (al-yaqīn) comes to you' — death (15:99). 'They did not kill him for certain (yaqīnā)' — ʿĪsā (4:157).

primaryMeaning: A door or gate — a way in. Bāb is a door; abwāb are doors or gates.
extendedMeaning: Paradise and Hell both have gates that open for their people (39:71–73).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. The Israelites were told, 'enter the gate (al-bāb) bowing humbly' (2:58). Yaʿqub told his sons, 'do not enter by one gate (bābin), but enter by different gates' (12:67). 'We opened to them the gates (abwāba) of everything' — as a trial (6:44).

primaryMeaning: To go, to travel, to move along. Sayr is travelling; sayyara is to make something move.
extendedMeaning: On the Last Day 'the mountains will move away (tasīru)' (52:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times, often as a call to learn from history: 'Travel (sīrū) in the land and see how was the end of the deniers' (6:11), and 'have they not travelled (yasīrū) in the land?' (12:109). 'It is He who enables you to travel (yusayyirukum) on land and sea' (10:22).

primaryMeaning: A tree — plants whose branches intertwine. From branches crossing each other comes shajara bayna, 'a dispute arose between them'.
extendedMeaning: 'They will not believe until they make you judge in what disputes arise (shajara) between them' (4:65).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. Adam and his wife were told, 'do not approach this tree (al-shajara)' (2:35). 'A good word is like a good tree (ka-shajaratin ṭayyiba)' (14:24). The lamp is lit 'from a blessed olive tree' (24:35).

primaryMeaning: To wonder at something unusual. ʿAjab is wonder; aʿjaba is to please or impress — to make someone marvel.
extendedMeaning: 'A believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you (aʿjabatkum)' (2:221).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. 'Is it a wonder (ʿajaban) to people that We revealed to a man among them?' (10:2). Sarah said, 'This is an amazing thing (ʿajīb)' (11:72). 'Let not their wealth or children impress you (tuʿjibka)' (9:55).

primaryMeaning: Ten — and from it, mixing and living closely together. ʿAshīra is one's kin, the close group; maʿshar is a company; ʿāshara is to live with someone.
extendedMeaning: 'Live with them (ʿāshirūhunna) in kindness' — with wives (4:19). 'Twenty (ʿishrūn) patient among you will overcome two hundred' (8:65).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. 'Twelve (ithnatā ʿashrata) springs' gushed for the tribes (2:60). 'Warn your nearest kindred (ʿashīrataka)' (26:214). 'O company (yā maʿshar) of jinn and humans' (6:130).

primaryMeaning: To deceive — to lead someone on through false hopes while they are off guard. Ghurūr is delusion; al-gharūr is the deceiver, Satan.
extendedMeaning: 'O man, what has deceived you (gharraka) about your Lord, the Generous?' (82:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. 'Let not the life of this world deceive you (taghurrannakum), and let not the deceiver (al-gharūr) deceive you about Allah' (31:33). 'Satan promises them only delusion (ghurūrā)' (4:120).

primaryMeaning: The moon. Qamar is the moon; classically linked to qumra, a whitish colour.
extendedMeaning: 'By the moon (wal-qamar)!' (74:32). Ibrahim, seeing the moon rising, said, 'This is my Lord' — then turned from it when it set (6:77).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times, often with the sun as a sign and a measure of time: 'He made the sun a radiance and the moon (al-qamar) a light, and determined its phases' (10:5). 'The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split (inshaqqa al-qamar)' (54:1).

primaryMeaning: To settle in a place. Madīna is a town or city; madā'in are cities. Madyan, the people of Shuʿayb, is placed under this root in the corpus.
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. Al-madīna is used for Pharaoh's city (7:123), the city where Musa struck a man (28:15), and Madinah (9:101). Pharaoh sent 'gatherers into the cities (al-madā'in)' (7:111). 'To Madyan (madyana) their brother Shuʿayb' (7:85).

primaryMeaning: To hold on, to keep hold of something. Amsaka is to hold back or keep; istamsaka is to grasp firmly; musk is named from this root.
extendedMeaning: 'None holds them (yumsikuhunna) up but Allah' — birds in flight (16:79). Its seal is musk (misk) (83:26).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. 'Whoever rejects false gods and believes in Allah has grasped (istamsaka) the firmest handhold' (2:256). 'Allah holds (yumsiku) the heavens and the earth lest they cease' (35:41). Divorced wives are to be 'retained (fa-amsikūhunna) in kindness or released in kindness' (2:231).

primaryMeaning: To give generously, to bestow a favour — and to remind someone of a favour. Manna is grace; mann is also the heavenly food, manna; mamnūn is 'cut off', so ghayr mamnūn is 'never-ending'.
extendedMeaning: 'For them is a reward never-ending (ghayru mamnūn)' (41:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. 'Allah has conferred a favour (manna) on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger' (3:164). 'Do not cancel your charities with reminders (bil-mann) and hurt' (2:264). 'We sent down to you manna (al-mann) and quails' (2:57).

primaryMeaning: A heavy load. Wizr is a burden, and so a sin one carries; wazīr is a helper who carries part of another's load; wazar is a refuge.
extendedMeaning: 'Did We not remove from you your burden (wizrak), which weighed down your back?' (94:2–3).
quranUsage: Occurs 27 times. 'No bearer of burdens (wāziratun) will bear the burden (wizra) of another' (6:164). Musa asked, 'Appoint for me a helper (wazīran) from my family' (20:29). The deniers 'will carry their burdens (awzārahum) on their backs' (6:31).

primaryMeaning: A fire that blazes fiercely. Jaḥīm is the blazing Fire — a name of Hell.
quranUsage: Occurs 26 times, almost always as al-jaḥīm, 'the Hellfire': 'you will not be asked about the companions of the Hellfire (al-jaḥīm)' (2:119). 'The Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators' (26:91). 'Then drive him into the Hellfire (al-jaḥīm)' (69:31).

primaryMeaning: To be disgraced and humiliated — shamed before others. Khizy is disgrace; akhzā is to disgrace.
extendedMeaning: 'Our Lord, do not disgrace us (tukhzinā) on the Day of Resurrection' (3:194).
quranUsage: Occurs 26 times. 'There is disgrace (khizyun) in the life of this world' for those who believe in part of the Book (2:85). 'Disgrace (al-khizy) this Day is upon the disbelievers' (16:27). Lut pleaded, 'do not disgrace me (tukhzūni) concerning my guests' (11:78).

primaryMeaning: To fall short, to be unable. ʿAjz is inability; aʿjaza is to put beyond someone's power; ʿajūz is an old woman, whose strength has failed; muʿjiza, 'miracle', is what others cannot match.
extendedMeaning: Qabil said, 'Am I unable (a-ʿajaztu) to be like this crow?' (5:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 26 times, mostly as muʿjizīn, 'able to escape': 'you cannot escape (bi-muʿjizīn)' Allah (6:134). Sarah said, 'Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman (ʿajūzun)?' (11:72). Lut's wife was 'an old woman (ʿajūzan) among those who remained' (26:171).

primaryMeaning: To grow from the ground, as plants sprout. Nabāt is vegetation; anbata is to cause to grow.
extendedMeaning: Allah 'made Maryam grow a good growth (nabātan ḥasanā)' — raised her well (3:37). 'Allah caused you to grow (anbatakum) from the earth like plants' (71:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 26 times. 'We caused to grow (fa-anbatnā) with it gardens of beauty' (27:60), and 'We caused to grow in it (the earth) everything in balance' (15:19). The Israelites asked for 'what the earth grows (tunbitu)' — herbs and lentils (2:61).

primaryMeaning: To be light and easy — and from being made light of, to be lowly. Hawn is gentleness and ease; hūn is humiliation; ahāna is to humiliate; muhīn is humiliating.
extendedMeaning: 'The servants of the Most Merciful walk on the earth gently (hawnan)' (25:63).
quranUsage: Occurs 26 times, most often in ʿadhābun muhīn, 'a humiliating punishment' (2:90). 'Today you will be repaid with the punishment of humiliation (al-hūn)' (6:93). Allah told Zakariyya, 'It is easy (hayyinun) for Me' (19:9).

primaryMeaning: To put down, to set something in its place — and to lower. Waḍaʿa is to place or lay down; it is also used for giving birth; mawḍiʿ is a place.
extendedMeaning: 'The record will be placed (wuḍiʿa)' on the Day of Judgment (18:49). 'Did We not lift (waḍaʿnā) from you your burden?' (94:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 26 times. 'The first House set up (wuḍiʿa) for mankind was at Bakka' (3:96). Maryam's mother said, 'I have delivered her (waḍaʿtuhā), a female' (3:36). Some of the People of the Book 'distort words from their places (mawāḍiʿihi)' (4:46).

primaryMeaning: The name Ādam, the first human. Classical scholars link it to adīm, the surface of the earth — he was created from its soil — or to udma, a brownish colour.
extendedMeaning: 'The example of ʿĪsā with Allah is like that of Adam: He created him from dust' (3:59). Banū Ādam, 'children of Adam', addresses all mankind (7:26).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times, all as the name Ādam. Allah 'taught Adam the names of all things' (2:31), and the angels were told to prostrate to him (2:34). 'Adam received words from his Lord' and was forgiven (2:37).

primaryMeaning: To spread out, to stretch something wide. Basaṭa is to extend a hand or spread a carpet; basṭa is abundance.
extendedMeaning: Qabil was told, 'If you stretch (basaṭta) your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch mine against you' (5:28). Talut was given 'abundance (basṭa) in knowledge and body' (2:247).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times, mostly for provision: 'Allah extends provision (yabsuṭu al-rizq) for whom He wills and restricts it' (13:26). 'His hands are outstretched (mabsūṭatān); He spends as He wills' (5:64). 'Do not make your hand tied to your neck, nor extend it (tabsuṭhā) completely' (17:29).

primaryMeaning: The belly, and from it, the inside of anything — what is hidden within. Bāṭin is inward or hidden, the opposite of ẓāhir, 'outward'; biṭāna is a close confidant, like a lining.
extendedMeaning: 'He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward (al-Bāṭin)' (57:3). 'Do not take as confidants (biṭānatan) those other than yourselves' (3:118).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. Those who conceal what Allah revealed for gain 'eat nothing into their bellies (buṭūnihim) but fire' (2:174). Honey comes 'from their bellies (buṭūnihā)' — the bees (16:69). Believers avoid immoralities 'apparent and hidden (baṭana)' (6:151).

primaryMeaning: To separate two things, to mark a boundary. Ḥadd is a limit; ḥādda is to oppose — to set oneself on the other side of a boundary. Ḥadīd, 'iron', shares the root.
extendedMeaning: Those who 'oppose (yuḥāddūna) Allah and His Messenger' will be humbled (58:5). Surah 57 is Al-Ḥadīd, 'Iron'.
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. Ḥudūd Allāh, 'the limits of Allah', close the rulings of fasting and family law: 'These are the limits of Allah (ḥudūdu Allāh), so do not approach them' (2:187), and 'do not transgress them' (2:229). 'We sent down iron (al-ḥadīd), in which is great strength' (57:25).

primaryMeaning: To be present, to come to a place — the opposite of ghāba, 'to be absent'. Ḥāḍir is present; aḥḍara is to bring; muḥḍar is one brought forward.
extendedMeaning: 'Every soul will find what it did of good brought forward (muḥḍarā)' (3:30).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. 'When death comes to (ḥaḍara) one of you' (2:180; 2:133). On the Day of Judgment the deniers 'will be brought (muḥḍarūn)' to punishment (30:16). The trade 'present (ḥāḍiratan)' among you need not be written (2:282).

primaryMeaning: To turn and change from one state to another. Ḥawl is a year — a full turn of time — and 'around', what one turns about; taḥwīl is transferring; ḥīla is a stratagem to change a situation.
extendedMeaning: Mothers nurse their children 'two full years (ḥawlayn)' (2:233). The people of Paradise 'will not seek any transfer (ḥiwalā) from it' (18:108).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. 'When it lit up what was around him (ḥawlahu)' (2:17). The Quran was sent to warn 'the Mother of Towns and those around it (ḥawlahā)' (6:92). False gods cannot 'remove harm from you or transfer it (taḥwīlā)' (17:56).

primaryMeaning: To give water to drink — to people, animals or land. Saqā is to give drink; siqāya is providing water to pilgrims; istasqā is to pray for rain.
extendedMeaning: Musa 'asked for water (istasqā)' for his people, and twelve springs gushed forth (2:60). The people of the Fire are 'given to drink (yusqā) of festering water' (14:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. 'We give you to drink (nusqīkum) from what is in their bellies' — milk (16:66). Musa 'watered (fa-saqā) for them' the flocks of Shuʿayb's daughters (28:24). In Paradise the righteous 'will be given to drink (yusqawna) of a sealed pure wine' (83:25).

primaryMeaning: To buy or sell — exchanging one thing for another. Ishtarā is to buy, to take something in exchange; sharā can mean to sell.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf's buyers 'sold him (sharawhu) for a small price' (12:20). 'Among people is one who sells (yashrī) himself seeking the pleasure of Allah' (2:207).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times, often for exchanging guidance for gain: 'those who bought (ishtarawū) error in exchange for guidance' (2:16), and 'do not exchange (lā tashtarū) My verses for a small price' (2:41). 'Allah has bought (ishtarā) from the believers their lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise' (9:111).

primaryMeaning: To be exposed to fire, to burn in it or warm oneself by it. Ṣalā is to roast; iṣṭalā is to warm oneself at a fire.
extendedMeaning: 'He will burn (sa-yaṣlā) in a fire of blazing flame' — Abu Lahab (111:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times, mostly for burning in Hell: 'Hell, in which they will burn (yaṣlawnahā)' (14:29), and 'burn therein (iṣlawhā) today' (36:64). Musa went to the fire hoping 'you may warm yourselves (taṣṭalūn)' (27:7).

primaryMeaning: Something round that turns. Falak is the orbit of a heavenly body; fulk, 'ship', shares the root.
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times, mostly as al-fulk, 'the ship': Nuh was told, 'build the ship (al-fulk) under Our eyes' (11:37), and 'We saved him and those with him in the ship' (7:64). Ships sail by Allah's command (2:164). The sun and moon are 'each in an orbit (falakin), swimming' (21:33).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris notes that the root has two opposite senses: qisṭ is justice, a fair share, and aqsaṭa is to act justly; qasaṭa is to deviate from justice, and qāsiṭ is unjust.
extendedMeaning: 'We will set up the scales of justice (al-qisṭ) for the Day of Resurrection' (21:47).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. Allah is 'maintaining justice (qā'iman bil-qisṭ)' (3:18). 'Allah loves those who act justly (al-muqsiṭīn)' (5:42). 'O you who believe, be upholders of justice (bil-qisṭ)' (4:135). 'As for the unjust (al-qāsiṭūn), they will be fuel for Hell' (72:15).

primaryMeaning: The tongue — and from it, language and speech. Lisān is a tongue, a language, or what is said about someone.
extendedMeaning: 'We have made it easy in your tongue (bi-lisānika)' (19:97). Ibrahim prayed for 'a truthful mention (lisāna ṣidqin)' among later generations (26:84; 19:50). 'The diversity of your tongues (alsinatikum) and colours' is a sign (30:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. 'We sent no messenger except in the language (bi-lisāni) of his people' (14:4). Musa prayed, 'untie the knot from my tongue (lisānī)' (20:27) and said Harun was 'more eloquent than me in speech (lisānan)' (28:34). The Quran is 'in a clear Arabic tongue' (26:195).

primaryMeaning: To admonish — to remind someone of consequences in a way that softens the heart. Waʿẓ and mawʿiẓa are admonition.
extendedMeaning: Luqman said to his son 'while admonishing him (yaʿiẓuhu)': 'do not associate anything with Allah' (31:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. The Quran is 'an admonition (mawʿiẓatun) from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts' (10:57). 'Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition (al-mawʿiẓa al-ḥasana)' (16:125). After rulings: 'He admonishes you (yaʿiẓukum) with it' (2:231).

primaryMeaning: To give freely, without expecting anything in return. Hiba is a gift; al-Wahhāb is the Bestower, who gives abundantly.
extendedMeaning: 'He grants (yahabu) females to whom He wills, and grants males to whom He wills' (42:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 25 times. Prophets pray, 'grant me (hab lī) from Yourself good offspring' (3:38), and 'grant us (hab lanā) mercy from Yourself; You are the Bestower (al-Wahhāb)' (3:8). 'We bestowed on him (wa-wahabnā lahu) Ishaq and Yaʿqub' (6:84).

primaryMeaning: Harm or hurt of a lesser kind — annoyance, injury or insult. Adhā is harm; ādhā is to hurt someone.
extendedMeaning: Menstruation is described as 'a hurt (adhan)' (2:222). The pilgrim who has 'an ailment (adhan) of the head' may shave early with a ransom (2:196).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'Do not cancel your charities with reminders and hurt (al-adhā)' (2:264). Those who 'hurt (yu'dhūna) the Messenger of Allah' face punishment (9:61). The emigrants who 'were harmed (ūdhū) in My way' are promised reward (3:195).

primaryMeaning: Fruit — what a tree yields — and by extension any yield or result. Thamara is a fruit; athmara is to bear fruit.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim prayed for Makkah, 'provide its people with fruits (al-thamarāt)' (2:126).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. Rain brings forth 'fruits (al-thamarāt) as provision for you' (2:22). 'Look at its fruit (thamarihi) when it bears fruit and ripens' (6:99). Believers are tested 'with loss of wealth, lives and fruits (al-thamarāt)' (2:155).

primaryMeaning: Not knowing — and acting without knowledge or self-restraint. Jahl is ignorance; jāhil is one who acts foolishly; al-jāhiliyya is the age of ignorance before Islam.
extendedMeaning: 'The judgment of ignorance (al-jāhiliyya) is what they seek?' (5:50).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. Musa said, 'I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant (al-jāhilīn)' (2:67). Repentance is accepted from 'those who do wrong in ignorance (bi-jahāla), then repent soon after' (4:17). 'When the ignorant (al-jāhilūn) address them, they say, "Peace"' (25:63).

primaryMeaning: To be low and easy to handle — the opposite of ʿizz, 'might'. Dhull is humility or humiliation; dhalūl is tame, easy to ride; adhilla are the lowly.
extendedMeaning: Believers are 'humble (adhillatin) towards the believers, stern towards the disbelievers' (5:54). 'He made the earth tame (dhalūlan) for you' (67:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'Lower to them the wing of humility (al-dhull) out of mercy' — to parents (17:24). 'Humiliation (al-dhilla) was struck upon them' (2:61). 'You honour whom You will and humiliate (tudhillu) whom You will' (3:26).

primaryMeaning: The neck — and from it, watching: raising one's neck to look out. Raqīb is a watcher; raqaba is a neck, and so a person held in bondage; tarqqaba is to wait watchfully.
extendedMeaning: Musa 'left the city fearful, watchful (yataraqqabu)' (28:21). 'Wait watchfully (fa-rtaqib) for the Day the sky brings a visible smoke' (44:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. Freeing 'a believing slave (raqabatin)' is an expiation (4:92), and fī al-riqāb, 'for freeing slaves', is a use of charity (2:177). 'Allah is ever Watchful (raqīban) over you' (4:1).

primaryMeaning: To live long and to keep a place lived in. ʿUmr is a lifespan; ʿammara is to grant long life; ʿamara is to build up and inhabit; ʿumra is the visit to the House.
extendedMeaning: 'The mosques of Allah are only maintained (yaʿmuru) by those who believe in Allah' (9:18).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'One of them wishes he could be given a life (yuʿammaru) of a thousand years' (2:96). 'Whoever We grant long life (nuʿammirhu), We reverse him in creation' (36:68). 'Complete the Hajj and the ʿumra for Allah' (2:196).

primaryMeaning: Anger — the rising of the heart against something displeasing. Ghaḍab is wrath; ghaḍbān is angry.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever My anger (ghaḍabī) falls upon has fallen' (20:81). Yunus 'went off in anger (mughāḍiban)' (21:87).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. Al-Fātiḥa asks for a path 'not of those who have earned anger (al-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim)' (1:7). 'They returned with wrath (bi-ghaḍabin) from Allah' (2:61). Musa 'returned to his people angry (ghaḍbān), grieved' (7:150).

primaryMeaning: To split open, to break through — as dawn breaks the night or water bursts from the ground. Fajr is dawn; fajjara is to make water gush; fujūr is breaking through moral bounds — wickedness.
extendedMeaning: 'He inspired it with its wickedness (fujūrahā) and its piety' — the soul (91:8). 'The wicked (al-fujjār) will be in Hellfire' (82:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. The fast lasts 'until the white thread of dawn (al-fajr) becomes distinct' (2:187). 'We caused to gush forth (fajjarnā) a river between them' (18:33). Some stones 'split and rivers gush forth (yatafajjaru)' (2:74). 'By the dawn (wal-fajr)' (89:1).

primaryMeaning: To go beyond the proper limit, to be excessive. Fāḥisha is a deed that is grossly shameful; faḥshā' is indecency.
extendedMeaning: Believers 'avoid the major sins and immoralities (al-fawāḥish)' (42:37). 'Do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse; it is an immorality (fāḥishatan)' (17:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'Satan promises you poverty and commands you to indecency (al-faḥshā')' (2:268). 'Allah forbids indecency (al-faḥshā'), wrongdoing and oppression' (16:90). The God-conscious, 'when they commit an indecency (fāḥishatan) … remember Allah and seek forgiveness' (3:135).

primaryMeaning: Kāda means 'almost' or 'nearly' — something on the point of happening but not yet happening.
extendedMeaning: 'Its oil would almost (yakādu) glow even if no fire touched it' (24:35). 'Had We not strengthened you, you would almost (kidta) have inclined to them a little' (17:74).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'The lightning almost (yakādu) snatches away their sight' (2:20). 'They slaughtered it, though they almost did not (mā kādū)' (2:71). 'The heavens almost (takādu) rupture' at the claim that the Most Merciful has a son (19:90).

primaryMeaning: Illness — the body leaving its healthy state, and by extension a sickness of the heart. Maraḍ is disease; marīḍ is sick.
extendedMeaning: 'There is no blame on the sick (al-marīḍ)' for staying behind (24:61).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'In their hearts is a disease (maraḍun), so Allah increased their disease' (2:10) — doubt and hypocrisy. The sick (marīḍan) may make up missed fasts (2:184). Ibrahim said, 'When I am ill (mariḍtu), it is He who cures me' (26:80).

primaryMeaning: To fall and land — for something to come down and happen. Waqaʿa is to occur; wāqiʿ is what befalls; al-wāqiʿa, 'the Event', is the Day of Judgment.
extendedMeaning: The angels were told, 'fall down (fa-qaʿū) in prostration to him' (15:29). The mountain raised over the Israelites, 'they thought it would fall (wāqiʿun) upon them' (7:171).
quranUsage: Occurs 24 times. 'When the Event occurs (waqaʿati al-wāqiʿa)' (56:1). 'The judgment is sure to occur (la-wāqiʿun)' (51:6). Whoever emigrates and dies on the way, 'his reward has fallen upon (waqaʿa) Allah' (4:100).

primaryMeaning: Speed — moving fast. Sarīʿ is swift; asraʿ is swiftest; sāraʿa is to race towards something.
extendedMeaning: 'Let not those who hasten (yusāriʿūna) into disbelief grieve you' (3:176). On the Last Day the earth splits and people come out 'hurrying (sirāʿan)' (50:44).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. Allah is 'swift in account (sarīʿ al-ḥisāb)' (2:202) and 'the swiftest of reckoners (asraʿ al-ḥāsibīn)' (6:62). 'Hasten (sāriʿū) to forgiveness from your Lord' (3:133), and the righteous 'hasten (yusāriʿūna) to good deeds' (3:114).

primaryMeaning: To go beyond the right measure. Isrāf is excess — wasteful spending, or going too far in sin; musrif is one who exceeds all bounds.
extendedMeaning: 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves (asrafū), do not despair of the mercy of Allah' (39:53). Lut called his people 'a transgressing (musrifūn) people' (7:81).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. 'Eat and drink, but do not be excessive (lā tusrifū); He does not love the excessive (al-musrifīn)' (7:31; 6:141). The servants of the Most Merciful, 'when they spend, are neither extravagant (lam yusrifū) nor miserly' (25:67).

primaryMeaning: To release, to set free from a tie. Ṭalāq, 'divorce', is releasing the marriage bond; inṭalaqa is to set off — to be released on one's way.
extendedMeaning: Musa and al-Khiḍr 'set out (fa-nṭalaqā)' together (18:71). 'Proceed (inṭaliqū) to that which you used to deny' (77:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. 'Divorce (al-ṭalāq) is twice' (2:229). 'When you divorce (ṭallaqtum) women and they reach their term, retain them in kindness or release them in kindness' (2:231). Surah 65 is Al-Ṭalāq, 'Divorce'.

primaryMeaning: To sink under water, to drown. Aghraqa is to drown someone; gharaq is drowning.
extendedMeaning: 'If We will, We could drown them (nughriqhum)' — those at sea (36:43). When drowning overtook Pharaoh, he said, 'I believe' (10:90).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times, for the fate of Nuh's people and Pharaoh's army: 'We drowned (aghraqnā) the people of Pharaoh while you were looking' (2:50), and 'they will be drowned (mughraqūn)' — Nuh's people (11:37). 'Because of their sins they were drowned (ughriqū)' (71:25).

primaryMeaning: To put on, to wear — and to cover over. Libās is clothing; labasa is to confuse, to cover the truth with something else.
extendedMeaning: 'Those who believe and do not mix (yalbisū) their faith with wrongdoing — for them is security' (6:82). The garments of Paradise are silk (22:23).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. 'O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing (libāsan) to cover your nakedness, … but the clothing of piety is best' (7:26). Spouses 'are a garment (libās) for you and you are a garment for them' (2:187). 'Do not mix (lā talbisū) the truth with falsehood' (2:42).

primaryMeaning: To walk, to go on foot.
extendedMeaning: One of Shuʿayb's daughters 'came to him walking (tamshī) shyly' (28:25). 'Walk (imshū) in its paths and eat of His provision' (67:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. 'Do not walk (lā tamshi) on the earth arrogantly' (17:37). The messengers before 'ate food and walked (yamshūna) in the markets' (25:20). 'Is one who was dead and We gave him life and a light by which he walks (yamshī) among people like one in darkness?' (6:122).

primaryMeaning: To marry — to enter into the marriage contract. Nikāḥ is marriage; ankaḥa is to give someone in marriage.
extendedMeaning: 'Let those who cannot find the means to marry (nikāḥan) keep chaste until Allah enriches them' (24:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. 'Do not marry (lā tankiḥū) polytheist women until they believe' (2:221). 'Marry those who please you of women' (4:3). 'Do not resolve on the marriage contract (ʿuqdat al-nikāḥ) until the prescribed term ends' (2:235).

primaryMeaning: To weigh, to measure the heaviness of something. Wazn is weight; mīzān is a balance or scale — and by extension balance and justice.
extendedMeaning: The deniers' deeds are empty: 'We will not assign them any weight (waznan) on the Day of Resurrection' (18:105). Those who cheat 'give less when they measure or weigh (wazanūhum) for others' (83:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times. 'Give full measure and weight (al-mīzān) in justice' (6:152). 'Those whose scales (mawāzīnuhu) are heavy — they are the successful' (7:8). 'He raised the heaven and set up the balance (al-mīzān), so do not transgress in the balance' (55:7–8).

primaryMeaning: To be left alone, without the one who should support you. Yatīm is an orphan — a child who has lost their father.
extendedMeaning: 'As for the orphan, do not oppress him' (93:9). The wall al-Khiḍr rebuilt 'belonged to two orphan boys (yatīmayn)' (18:82).
quranUsage: Occurs 23 times, mostly urging care for orphans: 'kindness to parents, relatives and orphans (al-yatāmā)' (2:83), and 'do not approach the property of the orphan (al-yatīm) except in the best way' (6:152). 'Did He not find you an orphan (yatīman) and give you shelter?' (93:6).

primaryMeaning: To join together, to become familiar and at ease with something. Allafa is to unite hearts; īlāf is a familiar, settled custom. Alf, 'a thousand', shares the root.
extendedMeaning: Al-mu'allafa qulūbuhum, 'those whose hearts are to be reconciled', may receive charity (9:60). 'Allah drives the clouds, then joins them (yu'allifu) together' (24:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'He put affection (allafa) between their hearts' (8:63), and 'you were enemies and He united your hearts' (3:103). Surah 106 begins, 'For the familiarity (li-īlāfi) of Quraysh' (106:1). Alf, 'thousand': 'one of them wishes he could live a thousand (alfa) years' (2:96).

primaryMeaning: Dust, earth — fine soil. Turāb is dust; matraba is destitution, poverty that clings to the dust; atrāb are companions of equal age.
extendedMeaning: 'Or a needy person in misery (matrabatin)' (90:16). The companions of Paradise are 'loving, of equal age (atrāban)' (56:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. Man is created from dust: 'He created him from dust (turābin)' (3:59). The deniers ask, 'When we are dust (turāban), will we be raised?' (13:5). The show-off's charity is 'like a rock with dust (turābun) on it; heavy rain falls and leaves it bare' (2:264).

primaryMeaning: To be complete, with nothing missing. Tamma is to be finished; atamma is to complete or perfect something.
extendedMeaning: Mothers nurse 'two full years, for whoever wishes to complete (yutimma) the nursing' (2:233). 'Allah will complete (mutimmu) His light, though the disbelievers dislike it' (61:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'The word of your Lord has been fulfilled (tammat) in truth and justice' (6:115). 'Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed (atmamtu) My favour upon you' (5:3). 'Complete (atimmū) the Hajj and the ʿumra for Allah' (2:196).

primaryMeaning: To miss the mark. Khaṭa' is an unintended mistake; khaṭī'a is a sin, a deliberate missing of the right; khāṭi' is one who sins knowingly.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf's brothers admitted, 'we have been sinners (khāṭi'īn)' (12:91). The magicians hoped 'our Lord will forgive us our sins (khaṭāyānā)' (20:73).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or make a mistake (akhṭa'nā)' (2:286). Killing a believer 'by mistake (khaṭa'an)' requires expiation (4:92). The Israelites were told to say 'relieve us', so 'We will forgive your sins (khaṭāyākum)' (2:58).

primaryMeaning: Four. Rubuʿ is a quarter; arbaʿūn is forty; rubāʿ is 'four by four'.
extendedMeaning: 'Two, three or four (rubāʿa)' in marriage (4:3). Wives' inheritance is 'a quarter (al-rubuʿ)' (4:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. Those who swear off their wives wait 'four (arbaʿati) months' (2:226). Accusations of adultery require 'four (arbaʿati) witnesses' (24:4). 'We appointed with Musa forty (arbaʿīna) nights' (2:51).

primaryMeaning: To be clear and plain in speech. ʿArabī is Arabic — the clear, expressive tongue; aʿrāb are the desert Arabs, the bedouins; ʿurub are wives devoted and expressive in their love.
extendedMeaning: 'Had We made it a non-Arabic Quran, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained?"' (41:44). The companions of Paradise are 'devoted (ʿuruban), of equal age' (56:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'We sent it down as an Arabic (ʿarabiyyan) Quran so that you may understand' (12:2), 'in a clear Arabic tongue' (26:195). Al-aʿrāb, 'the bedouins', are addressed about their faith: 'The bedouins say, "We believe"' (49:14).

primaryMeaning: To go astray through ignorance or desire — to lose one's way. Ghayy is error, the opposite of rushd, 'right guidance'; aghwā is to lead astray.
extendedMeaning: 'Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred (ghawā)' (53:2). 'Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred (ghawā)' (20:121).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'The right way (al-rushd) has become distinct from error (al-ghayy)' (2:256). Iblis said, 'Because You have sent me astray (aghwaytanī), I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path' (7:16), and 'I will mislead them (la-ughwiyannahum) all' (15:39).

primaryMeaning: Joy — a gladness in the heart. Fariḥa is to rejoice; it can be praised joy at Allah's bounty or blameworthy exultation.
extendedMeaning: The martyrs are 'rejoicing (fariḥīna) in what Allah has given them of His bounty' (3:170).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'In the bounty of Allah and His mercy — in that let them rejoice (fal-yafraḥū)' (10:58). But proud exultation is condemned: 'Do not exult (lā tafraḥ); Allah does not love the exultant' (28:76). 'When We let people taste mercy, they rejoice (fariḥū) in it' (30:36).

primaryMeaning: To measure out, to determine. Tamannā is to wish — to picture something as one would want it; umniyya is a wish or fancy; manī is the fluid of life, from which a person is determined.
extendedMeaning: 'Was he not a drop of fluid emitted (yumnā)?' (75:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 22 times. 'Wish (fa-tamannawū) for death, if you are truthful' — to those who claimed the Hereafter was theirs alone (2:94). 'It is not by your wishes (amāniyyikum) nor the wishes of the People of the Book' (4:123). Satan 'arouses desires in them (yumannīhim)' (4:120).

primaryMeaning: A mark left behind, a trace. Athar is a trace or footprint; āthār are remains and effects; āthara is to prefer — to give something the leading place.
extendedMeaning: 'You prefer (tu'thirūna) the life of this world, while the Hereafter is better' (87:16–17). The Ansar 'give preference (yu'thirūna) over themselves, even when in need' (59:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'We sent following in their footsteps (āthārihim) ʿĪsā son of Maryam' (5:46). 'Look at the effects (āthāri) of the mercy of Allah — how He gives life to the earth after its death' (30:50). Yusuf's brothers said, 'Allah has preferred you (ātharaka) over us' (12:91).

primaryMeaning: To remain, to last on. Baqā' is continuance; bāqī is what remains; abqā is 'more lasting'; baqiyya is a remnant.
extendedMeaning: The Ark of the Covenant held 'a remnant (baqiyyatun) of what the family of Musa left' (2:248).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'The Hereafter is better and more lasting (abqā)' (87:17). 'Everyone on it will perish, and there will remain (yabqā) the Face of your Lord' (55:27). 'The enduring good deeds (al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt) are better with your Lord' (18:46).

primaryMeaning: Stone, and from its hardness, preventing and walling off. Ḥajar is a stone; ḥijr is something forbidden, fenced off; ḥajr is guardianship — a lap or protected place.
extendedMeaning: Stepdaughters 'in your guardianship (ḥujūrikum)' are forbidden in marriage (4:23). 'This livestock and crop is forbidden (ḥijr)' — a pagan claim (6:138). Al-Ḥijr is the land of Thamud and the title of Surah 15.
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'Fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones (al-ḥijāra)' (2:24). 'Strike the stone (al-ḥajar) with your staff' (2:60). Lut's people were struck with 'stones (ḥijāratan) of baked clay' (11:82).

primaryMeaning: To be on guard, to take care against something feared. Ḥadhar and ḥidhr are caution and precautions; ḥadhdhara is to warn.
extendedMeaning: 'Let those who oppose his command beware (fal-yaḥdhar)' (24:63). Some should study the religion 'to warn their people … that they may be cautious (yaḥdharūn)' (9:122).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'Allah warns you (yuḥadhdhirukum) of Himself' (3:28). 'Take your precautions (ḥidhrakum)' in battle (4:71). The people 'put their fingers in their ears … in fear (ḥadhara) of death' (2:19).

primaryMeaning: Forbearance — self-control that does not rush to anger or punishment. Ḥilm is forbearance and good sense; ḥalīm is the forbearing one; ḥulum is a dream, and the age of puberty, when dreams of maturity begin.
extendedMeaning: Children who 'reach puberty (al-ḥulum)' must ask permission to enter (24:59).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing (ḥalīm)' (2:225). Ibrahim was 'forbearing (la-ḥalīmun), tender-hearted' (11:75), and was given the good news of 'a forbearing boy (ghulāmin ḥalīm)' (37:101). The king's advisers called his dream 'confused dreams (aḍghāthu aḥlām)' (12:44).

primaryMeaning: Heat — something hot. Ḥamīm is boiling water, and also a close, devoted friend — one warm in care for you; yaḥmūm is black, hot smoke.
extendedMeaning: 'No devoted friend (ḥamīm) will ask about a friend' on that Day (70:10), and 'as if he were a devoted friend (waliyyun ḥamīm)' (41:34).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times, mostly as ḥamīm, 'boiling water', given to the people of the Fire: 'for them is a drink of boiling water (ḥamīm) and a painful punishment' (6:70), and 'they are given boiling water (ḥamīman) that tears their bowels' (47:15). They will be 'in scorching wind and boiling water, and a shade of black smoke (yaḥmūm)' (56:42–43).

primaryMeaning: A way that is followed smoothly, like water poured in a steady flow. Sunna is a set way or practice; sinn is a tooth; masnūn is shaped or smoothed.
extendedMeaning: Man was created 'from dry clay of altered black mud (ḥama'in masnūn)' (15:26). The law of retribution includes 'a tooth for a tooth (al-sinna bil-sinn)' (5:45).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. Sunnat Allāh, 'the way of Allah', is unchanging: 'you will not find in the way of Allah (li-sunnati Allāh) any change' (33:62), and 'such was Our way with those We sent before you' (17:77). 'Situations (sunan) have passed before you' (3:137).

primaryMeaning: To make something known and widely seen. Shahr, 'month', is marked by the new moon, which is seen and announced.
extendedMeaning: The wind of Sulayman went 'a month's (shahrun) journey in the morning and a month in the evening' (34:12). 'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months (shahr)' (97:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'The month (shahru) of Ramadan in which the Quran was sent down' (2:185). 'The number of months (al-shuhūr) with Allah is twelve' (9:36). The expiation is 'fasting two consecutive months (shahrayn)' (4:92).

primaryMeaning: Youth and vigour. Fatā is a young man, and also a servant or companion; aftā is to give a ruling — to explain a matter clearly, as one clarifies a new question; istaftā is to ask for a ruling.
extendedMeaning: 'They were youths (fityatun) who believed in their Lord' — the people of the Cave (18:13). Ibrahim was called 'a youth (fatan) called Ibrahim' (21:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'They ask you for a ruling (yastaftūnaka); say, Allah gives you a ruling (yuftīkum)' (4:176). The king said, 'Explain to me (aftūnī) my dream' (12:43). Musa said 'to his young servant (li-fatāhu)' (18:60).

primaryMeaning: To conceal something that ought to be made known — to hold it back and keep it hidden.
extendedMeaning: A believing man from Pharaoh's family was 'concealing (yaktumu) his faith' (40:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'Those who conceal (yaktumūna) what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance … are cursed by Allah' (2:159). 'Do not conceal (lā taktumū) testimony; whoever conceals it (yaktumhā), his heart is sinful' (2:283). Allah knows 'what you reveal and what you conceal (taktumūn)' (2:33).

primaryMeaning: To spread out, to unfold what was folded. Nashr is spreading; nushūr is resurrection — the dead being spread out again from their graves; intashara is to disperse.
extendedMeaning: 'Your Lord will spread out (yanshur) for you of His mercy' (18:16). 'He spreads (yanshuru) His mercy' through rain (42:28). 'When the pages are spread open (nushirat)' (81:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 21 times. 'Thus is the resurrection (al-nushūr)' — as dead land revives with rain (35:9). The false gods 'have no power over death, life or resurrection (nushūrā)' (25:3). After a meal, 'disperse (fa-ntashirū)' (33:53).

primaryMeaning: A group gathered around a shared cause or belief. Ḥizb is a party; aḥzāb are factions — including the confederate tribes that besieged Madinah.
extendedMeaning: When the believers saw 'the confederates (al-aḥzāb)', they said, 'This is what Allah promised us' (33:22). Surah 33 is Al-Aḥzāb.
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'The party of Allah (ḥizba Allāh) — they are the victorious' (5:56), set against 'the party of Satan (ḥizbu al-shayṭān)' (58:19). Communities 'split into sects, each faction (ḥizbin) rejoicing in what it has' (23:53).

primaryMeaning: To climb step by step, to move gradually. Daraja is a step or rank; istadraja is to lead someone on gradually, step by step, towards their end.
extendedMeaning: 'We will lead them on gradually (sa-nastadrijuhum) from where they do not know' (7:182). Allah is 'exalted above all degrees (rafīʿ al-darajāt)' (40:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'Those messengers — We raised some of them in degrees (darajātin)' (2:253). 'Allah has preferred those who strive … over those who sit, by a degree (darajatan)' (4:95). The believers 'will have the highest ranks (al-darajāt al-ʿulā)' (20:75).

primaryMeaning: To grow and increase, to swell. Ribā, 'usury', is increase charged on a loan; rabwa is raised ground; arbā is to make grow.
extendedMeaning: When rain falls on the earth, 'it stirs and swells (rabat)' (22:5). The flood 'carried a rising (rābiyan) foam' (13:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury (al-ribā)' (2:275). 'Allah destroys usury and gives increase (yurbī) for charities' (2:276). 'What you give in usury to increase (li-yarbuwa) through people's wealth does not increase with Allah' (30:39).

primaryMeaning: A year — a full turning of time; the plural sinīn is often used for hard years of drought. Sanā is also a flash of light.
extendedMeaning: 'We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine (bil-sinīn)' (7:130). 'The flash (sanā) of its lightning almost takes away the sight' (24:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. Yusuf 'remained in prison some years (biḍʿa sinīn)' (12:42). 'One of them wishes to be given life of a thousand years (sanatin)' (2:96). The Israelites wandered 'forty years (sanatan)' (5:26). The moon's phases let you 'know the number of years (al-sinīn)' (10:5).

primaryMeaning: To make something with skill, to craft it. Ṣunʿ is a work of craftsmanship; ṣanʿa is a craft; iṣṭanaʿa is to make something for oneself — to train and prepare it.
extendedMeaning: 'We taught him the making (ṣanʿata) of coats of mail' — Dawud (21:80). Allah told Musa, 'I chose you for Myself (iṣṭanaʿtuka)' (20:41), 'so that you might be raised under My eye (li-tuṣnaʿa)' (20:39).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'The work (ṣunʿa) of Allah, who perfected all things' (27:88). 'Allah is aware of what they do (yaṣnaʿūn)' (24:30). The losers are those who 'think they are doing well in work (ṣunʿan)' (18:104). Nuh was told, 'build (iṣnaʿ) the ship under Our eyes' (11:37).

primaryMeaning: To split open, to break through — and to bring into being for the first time, splitting open nothingness. Fāṭir is the Originator; fiṭra is the original nature a person is created with; fiṭr is breaking a fast.
extendedMeaning: 'The heavens almost break apart (yatafaṭṭarna)' at the claim of a son (19:90). 'When the sky breaks open (infaṭarat)' (82:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'Originator (fāṭir) of the heavens and the earth' (6:14). Ibrahim said, 'I have turned my face to Him who originated (faṭara) the heavens and the earth' (6:79). 'The fiṭra of Allah on which He originated (faṭara) people' (30:30).

primaryMeaning: To understand deeply — to grasp the meaning behind the words. Fiqh is deep understanding; tafaqqaha is to gain understanding of the religion.
extendedMeaning: Musa prayed, 'untie the knot from my tongue, so that they may understand (yafqahū) my speech' (20:28). Creation glorifies Allah, 'but you do not understand (tafqahūna) their glorification' (17:44).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times, mostly lā yafqahūna, 'they do not understand': 'What is wrong with these people that they hardly understand (yafqahūna) any speech?' (4:78). 'They have hearts with which they do not understand (lā yafqahūna)' (7:179). A group should go forth 'to gain understanding (li-yatafaqqahū) in the religion' (9:122).

primaryMeaning: To uncover, to remove what covers something. Kashafa is to lay bare or lift away — especially to remove a hardship.
extendedMeaning: 'The Day the shin will be uncovered (yukshafu)' (68:42). The Queen of Sheba 'uncovered (kashafat) her shins' thinking the glass floor was water (27:44).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times, mostly for lifting affliction: 'If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it (kāshifa) but He' (6:17). Ayyub's prayer was answered, 'so We removed (fa-kashafnā) what afflicted him' (21:84). 'Who answers the distressed when he calls and removes (yakshifu) the evil?' (27:62).

primaryMeaning: To play — to do something without serious purpose. Laʿib is play and amusement.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf's brothers asked, 'Send him with us tomorrow to enjoy himself and play (yalʿab)' (12:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'The life of this world is only play (laʿibun) and amusement' (6:32). 'We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play (lāʿibīn)' (21:16). Some 'take your religion in ridicule and play (laʿiban)' (5:57).

primaryMeaning: To draw out milk from an udder by stroking — and from drawing out, doubt and dispute: pulling at a matter to raise questions. Mirya is doubt; imtarā is to doubt; mārā is to argue.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not argue (tumāri) about them except with an obvious argument' — the people of the Cave (18:22). 'Will you dispute (a-fa-tumārūnahu) with him about what he saw?' (53:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters (al-mumtarīn)' (2:147). 'Do not be in doubt (miryatin) about it' (11:17). 'Then you still doubt (tamtarūn)' — the resurrection (6:2).

primaryMeaning: The date palm. Nakhl and nakhīl are date palms; nakhla is a single palm tree.
extendedMeaning: ʿĀd were blown down 'as if they were trunks of uprooted palm trees (nakhlin)' (54:20). Pharaoh threatened to crucify the magicians 'on the trunks of palm trees' (20:71).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times, often among Allah's blessings: 'gardens of grapevines and date palms (al-nakhl)' (6:141), and 'date palms with clusters of dates hanging low' (6:99). Maryam was told, 'Shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree (al-nakhla)' (19:25).

primaryMeaning: To pull out, to draw something away forcefully. Nazaʿa is to remove or strip away; tanāzaʿa is to pull against each other — to dispute.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not dispute (lā tanāzaʿū) with one another, or you will lose courage' (8:46). 'By those who pull out (al-nāziʿāt) violently' — the angels taking souls (79:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. 'We will remove (nazaʿnā) whatever ill feeling is in their breasts' — in Paradise (7:43). 'You take away (tanziʿu) dominion from whom You will' (3:26). Musa 'drew out (nazaʿa) his hand, and it was white' (7:108).

primaryMeaning: To blow, to breathe into something.
extendedMeaning: 'Dhu al-Qarnayn said, "Blow (unfukhū)" until he made it like fire' — the iron barrier (18:96).
quranUsage: Occurs 20 times. On the Last Day 'the trumpet will be blown (nufikha)' (18:99; 23:101). Allah 'breathed (nafakhtu) into him of My spirit' — Adam (15:29), and 'We breathed (nafakhnā) into her of Our spirit' — Maryam (21:91). ʿĪsā 'breathed into' the clay bird and it became a bird (3:49).
