primaryMeaning: A land or settlement — a place where people live and settle. Balad is a town or land; bilād are lands; balda is a single town.
extendedMeaning: 'Let not the movement of the disbelievers through the land (al-bilād) deceive you' (3:196). 'The good land (al-balad) brings forth its vegetation by its Lord's permission' (7:58).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times. 'I swear by this city (al-balad)' — Makkah (90:1). Ibrahim prayed, 'My Lord, make this a secure city (baladan āminan)' (2:126). Rain revives 'a dead land (baldatan mayta)' (25:49).

primaryMeaning: The price of something — its worth in exchange. Thaman is a price; thamāniya is eight and thumun an eighth, which share the root.
extendedMeaning: The Throne of your Lord 'will be carried that Day by eight (thamāniya)' (69:17). Wives inherit 'an eighth (al-thumun)' when there are children (4:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times. Thamanan qalīlan, 'a small price', is condemned as what people sell Allah's signs for (2:41). 'They sold him for a cheap price (bi-thamanin bakhs)' — Yusuf (12:20). 'Eight (thamāniya) pairs' of livestock (6:143).

primaryMeaning: To be on the right course — sound judgment and right guidance. Rushd is maturity and right direction; rashīd is one rightly guided; murshid is a guide.
extendedMeaning: 'So that they may be rightly guided (yarshudūn)' (2:186). Musa asked al-Khiḍr to teach him 'of what you have been taught of right guidance (rushdā)' (18:66).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times. 'The right way (al-rushd) has become clear from error' (2:256). The youths of the Cave prayed, 'prepare for us right guidance (rashadan) in our affair' (18:10). Orphans receive their property 'if you perceive in them sound judgment (rushdan)' (4:6).

primaryMeaning: To kindle and stir up a fire. Saʿīr is a blazing fire — a name of Hell; suʿur is madness, a burning of the mind.
extendedMeaning: Thamud said, 'We would then be in error and madness (suʿur)' (54:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times, mostly as al-saʿīr, 'the Blaze': 'they will burn in a Blaze (saʿīran)' (4:10), and 'a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze (al-saʿīr)' (42:7). 'When Hell is set ablaze (suʿʿirat)' (81:12).

primaryMeaning: To give something a form or shape. Ṣūra is a form or image; ṣawwara is to fashion; al-Muṣawwir is the Fashioner. Ṣūr is the horn or trumpet sounded on the Last Day.
extendedMeaning: 'In whatever form (ṣūratin) He willed, He assembled you' (82:8). Al-Muṣawwir, 'the Fashioner', is a name of Allah (59:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times. 'It is He who shapes you (yuṣawwirukum) in the wombs as He wills' (3:6). 'He formed you (ṣawwarakum) and made your forms (ṣuwarakum) good' (40:64). 'The Day the trumpet (al-ṣūr) is blown' (6:73).

primaryMeaning: To come up and appear — as the sun rises over the horizon. Ṭulūʿ is rising; iṭṭalaʿa is to look over something and learn of it; ṭalʿ is the spathe of the palm, the first thing to emerge.
extendedMeaning: 'Peace it is until the rising (maṭlaʿ) of the dawn' (97:5). 'Date palms with layered spathes (ṭalʿun naḍīd)' (50:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times. 'Glorify with the praise of your Lord before the rising (ṭulūʿ) of the sun' (20:130). The sun, 'when it rose (ṭalaʿat)', inclined away from the Cave (18:17). 'You will not cease to discover (taṭṭaliʿu) deceit from them' (5:13).

primaryMeaning: To go away and disappear — as the sun sets. Ghurūb is sunset; maghrib is the west, where the sun goes down; gharīb is a stranger, far from home.
extendedMeaning: 'I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests (al-maghārib)' (70:40). Gharābīb, 'intensely black', describes some mountain streaks (35:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times. 'To Allah belongs the east and the west (al-maghrib); wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah' (2:115). Righteousness is not turning 'towards the east or the west (al-maghrib)' (2:177). Dhu al-Qarnayn found the sun 'setting (taghrubu) in a murky spring' (18:86).

primaryMeaning: Fruit — and from it, delight and pleasant enjoyment. Fākiha is fruit; fakih is one who enjoys himself.
extendedMeaning: Pharaoh's people had lived in 'comfort in which they delighted (fākihīn)' (44:27). The people of Paradise are 'busy, enjoying themselves (fākihūn)' (36:55).
quranUsage: Occurs 19 times, mostly for the fruits of Paradise: 'they will have fruit (fākihatun) and whatever they ask for' (36:57), and 'fruit of whatever they choose' (56:20). On earth, 'in them are many fruits (fawākihu)' (23:19).

primaryMeaning: To be firm and fixed in place. Thabata is to stand firm; thabbata is to make firm; tathbīt is steadiness.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah erases what He wills and confirms (yuthbitu)' (13:39). 'When you meet a company, stand firm (fa-thbutū)' (8:45).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. 'Our Lord, make firm (thabbit) our feet' (2:250). 'Allah keeps firm (yuthabbitu) those who believe with the firm word in this life and the Hereafter' (14:27). 'If you help Allah, He will help you and make firm (yuthabbit) your feet' (47:7).

primaryMeaning: To be fortified, protected and hard to reach. Ḥiṣn is a fortress; iḥṣān is protecting oneself — through chastity or marriage; muḥṣana is a chaste woman or a married one.
extendedMeaning: Dawud was taught to make coats of mail 'to protect you (li-tuḥṣinakum) from your violence' (21:80).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times, mostly in family law: al-muḥṣanāt, 'chaste women' or 'married women', appear in the rules of marriage (4:24–25). Maryam is praised as one 'who guarded (aḥṣanat) her chastity' (21:91). The Jewish tribe thought 'their fortresses (ḥuṣūnuhum) would protect them from Allah' (59:2).

primaryMeaning: To dispute, to be an adversary in an argument. Khaṣm is an opponent; khiṣām is quarrelling; ikhtaṣama is to dispute with one another.
extendedMeaning: 'You were not with them when they were disputing (yakhtaṣimūn)' — over Maryam's guardianship (3:44). The people of the Fire 'quarrel (takhāṣumu)' among themselves (38:64).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. The man who pleases with his speech is 'the fiercest of opponents (aladdu al-khiṣām)' (2:204). Man, created from a drop, 'is a clear opponent (khaṣīmun mubīn)' (16:4). 'These are two opponents (khaṣmān) who dispute about their Lord' (22:19).

primaryMeaning: To move slowly across the ground, to creep. Dābba is any creature that moves on the earth.
extendedMeaning: Sulayman's death was revealed only when 'a creature of the earth (dābbatu al-arḍ)' gnawed his staff (34:14). 'We will bring forth for them a creature (dābbatan) from the earth' — a sign of the Hour (27:82).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. 'There is no creature (dābbatin) on earth but that its provision is upon Allah' (11:6). 'Allah created every creature (dābbatin) from water' (24:45). 'The worst creatures (al-dawābb) with Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason' (8:22).

primaryMeaning: The head — the top of the body, and by extension the chief or principal of something. Ra's al-māl is capital, the principal sum.
extendedMeaning: On the Day of Judgment the wrongdoers are 'raising their heads (ru'ūsihim), their gaze not returning to them' (14:43). Boiling water 'poured over their heads (ru'ūsihim)' (22:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. In ablution, 'wipe over your heads (bi-ru'ūsikum)' (5:6), and pilgrims 'do not shave your heads (ru'ūsakum)' until the offering arrives (2:196). Those who give up usury 'may have your capital (ru'ūsu amwālikum)' (2:279).

primaryMeaning: To cut a notch — to mark something off as fixed. Faraḍa is to ordain, to make obligatory; farīḍa is an obligation or an appointed share.
extendedMeaning: 'He who made the Quran binding on you (faraḍa) will bring you back to a place of return' (28:85). The dower 'you have specified (faraḍtum)' (2:237).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. Shares of inheritance are 'an obligation (farīḍatan) from Allah' (4:11), and charity goes to its recipients as 'an obligation from Allah' (9:60). 'Whoever undertakes (faraḍa) Hajj in them' (2:197). 'A surah which We sent down and made obligatory (faraḍnāhā)' (24:1).

primaryMeaning: To think something over, to turn it in the mind. Tafakkur is reflection — working one's thought through a matter to reach its meaning.
extendedMeaning: Of the denier who schemed against the Quran: 'He thought (fakkara) and deliberated' (74:18). 'Stand for Allah in pairs and individually, then reflect (tatafakkarū)' (34:46).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times, always as a verb, and mostly in the phrase 'for a people who reflect (yatafakkarūn)' (7:176). The people of understanding 'reflect (yatafakkarūna) on the creation of the heavens and the earth' (3:191). 'Thus Allah makes clear the verses, that you may reflect (tatafakkarūn)' (2:219).

primaryMeaning: Ladun means 'from with' or 'from the presence of' — something coming directly from someone's own side.
extendedMeaning: The Quran's verses were 'perfected, then explained in detail from One (min ladun) Wise and Aware' (11:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times, often for what comes directly from Allah: 'grant us from Yourself (min ladunka) mercy' (3:8), and 'We would have given them from Ourselves (min ladunnā) a great reward' (4:67). Al-Khiḍr was taught 'knowledge from Us (min ladunnā)' (18:65).

primaryMeaning: To have a firm place — to be set firmly and given power. Makkana is to establish someone in a land; makīn is firmly established and secure.
extendedMeaning: 'We wished to … establish them (numakkina) in the land' — the oppressed Israelites (28:6). Those who, 'if We establish them (makkannāhum) in the land, establish prayer' (22:41).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. 'We had established them (makkannāhum) on the earth as We have not established you' (6:6). 'Thus We established (makkannā) Yusuf in the land' (12:21). The drop of fluid is placed 'in a firm lodging (qarārin makīn)' (23:13).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two branches: dictating — amlalla is to dictate words to a writer — and milla, a religion or way that is followed.
extendedMeaning: 'Who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim except one who makes a fool of himself?' (2:130).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times, mostly as millat Ibrāhīm, 'the religion of Ibrahim': 'Rather, the religion (millata) of Ibrahim, the upright' (2:135). Prophets' peoples demanded they 'return to our religion (millatinā)' (7:88). The debtor 'should dictate (wal-yumlil)' the terms to the scribe (2:282).

primaryMeaning: To move away quickly — to flee, or to set out together. Nafara is to march forth; nufūr is aversion, turning away; nafar is a band of people.
extendedMeaning: 'A company (nafarun) of the jinn listened' (72:1). 'I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men (nafaran)' (18:34).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. 'Go forth (infirū) in groups or all together' (4:71), and 'if you do not go forth (tanfirū), He will punish you' (9:39). The Quran 'increases them only in aversion (nufūrā)' (17:41).

primaryMeaning: To come back to something again and again. Anāba is to turn back to Allah in repentance and devotion; munīb is one who constantly turns to Him.
extendedMeaning: 'Turning (munībīna) to Him, and fear Him' (30:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 18 times. 'In that is a sign for every servant who turns back (munīb)' (34:9). 'He guides to Himself whoever turns back (anāba)' (13:27). 'Turn back (wa-anībū) to your Lord and submit to Him' (39:54). Shuʿayb said, 'Upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn back (unību)' (11:88).

primaryMeaning: To return, to come back. Awwāb is one who returns to Allah often; ma'āb is the place of return — the final destination.
extendedMeaning: Hell 'is a place of return (ma'āban) for the transgressors' (78:22). The mountains 'repeated praises (awwibī) with him' — Dawud (34:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. Dawud was 'one who constantly turned back (awwābun)' (38:17). 'For them is blessedness and a good place of return (ḥusnu ma'āb)' (13:29). 'He is ever forgiving to those who often turn back (lil-awwābīn)' (17:25).

primaryMeaning: To return to a place and settle there. Bawwa'a is to settle someone in a home; tabawwa'a is to take up a dwelling; bā'a bi- is to come back carrying something — to incur it.
extendedMeaning: 'We showed Ibrahim the site (bawwa'nā) of the House' (22:26). Yusuf was 'settled in the land to live (yatabawwa'u) wherever he wished' (12:56).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. The Israelites 'returned with (bā'ū) wrath from Allah' (2:61). 'We will surely settle them (la-nubawwi'annahum) in this world in a good place' — the emigrants (16:41). 'We settled (bawwa'nā) the Children of Israel in a good place' (10:93).

primaryMeaning: Stillness and lowliness — the humbling of the voice and gaze. Khushūʿ is humble submission felt in the heart and seen in the body; dry, lifeless earth is called khāshiʿa.
extendedMeaning: 'You see the earth humble (khāshiʿatan); when We send down rain on it, it stirs' (41:39). 'Had We sent down this Quran on a mountain, you would have seen it humbled (khāshiʿan)' (59:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. 'The believers have succeeded, those who are humble (khāshiʿūn) in their prayer' (23:2). 'Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts humble themselves (takhshaʿa) at the remembrance of Allah?' (57:16). Voices 'will be humbled (khashaʿat)' before the Most Merciful (20:108).

primaryMeaning: To be light — the opposite of heaviness. Khaffafa is to lighten; istakhaffa is to treat something as light.
extendedMeaning: Pharaoh 'made fools of (fa-stakhaffa) his people, and they obeyed him' (43:54). 'Let not those who lack certainty unsettle you (yastakhiffannaka)' (30:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. 'Allah wishes to lighten (yukhaffifa) for you; man was created weak' (4:28). For the deniers 'the punishment will not be lightened (yukhaffafu)' (2:86). 'Those whose scales are light (khaffat) have lost themselves' (7:9).

primaryMeaning: To wait and watch for something to happen. Tarabbaṣa is to wait expectantly — for good, for a set period, or for misfortune to befall another.
extendedMeaning: The hypocrites 'wait (yatarabbaṣūna) to see what befalls you' (4:141), and 'you waited (tarabbaṣtum), doubted and were deceived' (57:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. Divorced women 'wait (yatarabbaṣna) by themselves for three periods' (2:228). 'Wait (fa-tarabbaṣū) until Allah brings His command' (9:24). 'Say: wait (tarabbaṣū); I too am waiting with you' (52:31).

primaryMeaning: To claim — to assert something, usually without proof. Zaʿm is a claim; zaʿīm is one who guarantees, standing surety for his word.
extendedMeaning: 'I am responsible (zaʿīmun) for it' — a camel-load for whoever finds the king's cup (12:72).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times, mostly for false claims: 'Where are your partners whom you used to claim (tazʿumūn)?' (6:22). 'Those who disbelieve claim (zaʿama) that they will never be raised' (64:7). 'This is for Allah, by their claim (bi-zaʿmihim)' (6:136).

primaryMeaning: To rise and climb up. Sūr is a city wall; sūra, a chapter of the Quran, is classically explained as a stage or degree — or a section walled off by itself; siwār is a bracelet, encircling the wrist.
extendedMeaning: The two disputants 'climbed over the wall (tasawwarū) of the prayer chamber' to reach Dawud (38:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. Sūra means a chapter: 'produce a surah (bi-sūratin) like it' (2:23), and 'bring ten surahs (suwarin) like it' (11:13). 'A wall (bi-sūrin) with a gate will be put between them' (57:13). The people of Paradise wear 'bracelets (asāwira) of gold' (18:31).

primaryMeaning: To drive forward, to herd from behind. Sāqa is to drive; sūq is a market, where goods are driven to; sāq is the shin or stem, the part that carries things along.
extendedMeaning: 'The Day the shin (sāq) will be uncovered' (68:42). The crop 'stands firm on its stem (sūqihi)' (48:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. 'Those who disbelieved will be driven (sīqa) to Hell in groups' (39:71), and the God-conscious to Paradise (39:73). 'We will drive (nasūqu) the criminals to Hell, thirsty' (19:86). The messengers 'ate food and walked in the markets (al-aswāq)' (25:7).

primaryMeaning: To rise and shine — as the sun comes up. Sharq is the east; mashriq is the place of sunrise; ishrāq is sunrise; ashraqa is to shine.
extendedMeaning: The mountains glorified with Dawud 'in the evening and at sunrise (al-ishrāq)' (38:18). 'The earth will shine (ashraqat) with the light of its Lord' (39:69).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. 'To Allah belong the east (al-mashriq) and the west' (2:115). Righteousness is not facing 'the east or the west' (2:177). 'Lord of the heavens and the earth … and Lord of the points of sunrise (al-mashāriq)' (37:5).

primaryMeaning: To be pure and clear, free of any mixture. Ṣafā is purity; iṣṭafā is to choose the best, the purest part; ṣafwān is a smooth, bare rock.
extendedMeaning: Charity spoiled by showing off is 'like a smooth rock (ṣafwānin) with dust on it' (2:264). Paradise has 'rivers of purified (muṣaffan) honey' (47:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times, mostly for Allah choosing: 'Allah has chosen (iṣṭafā) for you this religion' (2:132), and 'Allah chooses (yaṣṭafī) messengers from angels and from people' (22:75). Maryam was told, 'Allah has chosen you (iṣṭafāki) and purified you' (3:42).

primaryMeaning: To take refuge — to go to someone for protection. ʿĀdha is to seek refuge; istaʿādha is to ask for protection; maʿādh Allāh means 'Allah forbid'.
extendedMeaning: The last two surahs begin 'Say: I seek refuge (aʿūdhu) in the Lord of the daybreak' (113:1) and 'the Lord of mankind' (114:1). 'My Lord, I seek refuge (aʿūdhu) in You from the promptings of the devils' (23:97–98).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. 'If an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, seek refuge (fa-staʿidh) in Allah' (7:200). Musa said, 'I seek refuge (aʿūdhu) in Allah from being among the ignorant' (2:67). Yusuf answered the seduction, 'I seek refuge in Allah (maʿādha Allāh)' (12:23).

primaryMeaning: To hold back and keep from — to prevent something from being reached or given. Manaʿa is to prevent or withhold; mannāʿ is one who always withholds.
extendedMeaning: 'Every stubborn disbeliever, forbidder of good (mannāʿin lil-khayr)' (50:25).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. 'Who is more unjust than one who prevents (manaʿa) the mosques of Allah from His name being mentioned?' (2:114). Allah asked Iblis, 'What prevented you (manaʿaka) from prostrating?' (7:12). Those who pray carelessly also 'withhold (yamnaʿūna) small kindnesses' (107:7).

primaryMeaning: To resent something and hold it against someone — and so to punish in return. Intiqām is retribution; naqama is to resent.
extendedMeaning: 'Do you resent us (tanqimūna) except that we believe in Allah?' (5:59).
quranUsage: Occurs 17 times. Allah is 'Almighty, Owner of Retribution (dhū intiqām)' (3:4). 'We took retribution (fa-ntaqamnā) from them and drowned them' (7:136). Pharaoh's magicians said, 'You resent us (tanqimu) only because we believed in the signs of our Lord' (7:126).

primaryMeaning: To be open and plain — to speak aloud or appear openly. Jahr is loudness or openness; jahratan is 'openly, plainly'.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly (tajharū) to him' (49:2). Allah knows 'your secret and what you make public (jahrakum)' (6:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. The Israelites demanded, 'Show us Allah openly (jahratan)' (2:55). 'Allah does not love the public mention (al-jahr) of evil, except by one who has been wronged' (4:148). 'Do not be loud (lā tajhar) in your prayer, nor too quiet' (17:110).

primaryMeaning: To come to nothing — classically, of an animal that swells from bad pasture and dies. Ḥabiṭa is for deeds to be lost and worthless; aḥbaṭa is to make them void.
extendedMeaning: 'If you associate partners, your deeds will surely become worthless (la-yaḥbaṭanna)' (39:65).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. Those who turn from their religion and die disbelieving — 'their deeds have become worthless (ḥabiṭat) in this world and the Hereafter' (2:217). 'Do not raise your voices above the Prophet's … lest your deeds become worthless (taḥbaṭa)' (49:2).

primaryMeaning: Bad and foul — the opposite of ṭayyib, 'good'. Khabīth describes what is impure in food, speech, deeds or character.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah will separate the bad (al-khabīth) from the good' (8:37). 'Evil women are for evil men (al-khabīthāt lil-khabīthīn)' (24:26).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. 'Do not aim at the bad (al-khabītha) of it to spend from' (2:267). The Prophet 'forbids them the impure things (al-khabā'ith)' (7:157). 'A bad word is like a bad tree (shajaratin khabītha), uprooted from the earth' (14:26).

primaryMeaning: To betray a trust — to fail someone who relied on you. Khiyāna is betrayal; khā'in is a traitor; ikhtāna is to deceive oneself.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not be an advocate for the deceitful (lil-khā'inīn)' (4:105). 'He knows the treachery (khā'inata) of the eyes' (40:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. 'O you who believe, do not betray (lā takhūnū) Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts' (8:27). 'Allah does not love the treacherous (al-khā'inīn)' (8:58). 'Allah knew that you used to deceive yourselves (takhtānūna)' — in the nights of fasting (2:187).

primaryMeaning: A line or row — writing set down in lines. Saṭara is to write; masṭūr is inscribed; asāṭīr are tales that have been written down; muṣayṭir is one who has control over something.
extendedMeaning: 'You are not a controller (bi-muṣayṭir) over them' (88:22). 'Every matter, small and great, is written down (mustaṭar)' (54:53).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. Asāṭīr al-awwalīn, 'tales of the former peoples', is the deniers' dismissal of the Quran (6:25). 'By the pen and what they write (yasṭurūn)' (68:1). 'That is inscribed (masṭūrā) in the Book' (17:58).

primaryMeaning: To make ready and have at hand. Aʿtada is to prepare; ʿatīd is ready and present.
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times, mostly aʿtadnā, 'We have prepared': 'for them We have prepared (aʿtadnā) a painful punishment' (4:18). Each word is recorded by 'an observer, ready (ʿatīd)' (50:18). The wife of al-ʿAzīz 'prepared (aʿtadat) for them a banquet' (12:31).

primaryMeaning: To appear openly, to become known. Aʿlana is to declare or make public; ʿalāniya is openness, the opposite of sirr, 'secret'.
extendedMeaning: 'Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we declare (nuʿlinu)' (14:38).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. Allah knows 'what they conceal and what they declare (yuʿlinūn)' (2:77). Those who spend 'secretly and openly (ʿalāniyatan)' have their reward (2:274). Nuh said, 'I called them publicly (aʿlantu) and confided in them privately' (71:9).

primaryMeaning: The early morning, from dawn to sunrise. Ghudūw is morning; ghadā is to set out early; ghadan is 'tomorrow' — the coming morning.
extendedMeaning: 'Never say of anything, I will do that tomorrow (ghadan)' without 'if Allah wills' (18:23). The owners of the garden 'went early (ghadaw), determined' (68:25).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. 'Remember your Lord … in the mornings (bil-ghuduw) and the evenings' (7:205). 'Do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning (bil-ghadāt) and evening' (6:52). 'Let every soul look to what it has sent ahead for tomorrow (li-ghadin)' (59:18).

primaryMeaning: To get into something and fix there. Ghill is a hidden grudge in the heart; ghull is a collar or shackle round the neck; ghalla is to take from the spoils secretly — to defraud.
extendedMeaning: The Prophet relieves people 'of their burdens and the shackles (al-aghlāl) upon them' (7:157). 'Let not your hand be chained (maghlūlatan) to your neck' (17:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. 'We will remove whatever grudge (ghillin) is in their breasts' (7:43). The deniers will have 'shackles (al-aghlāl) on their necks' (13:5). 'It is not for a prophet to defraud (yaghulla)' (3:161).

primaryMeaning: The heart — classically linked to fa'ada, 'to roast', the heart being the place of burning feeling. Fu'ād is the heart as the seat of feeling and inner perception.
extendedMeaning: 'We relate to you the stories of the messengers to make firm your heart (fu'ādaka)' (11:120). Ibrahim prayed, 'make the hearts (af'idatan) of people incline towards them' (14:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. Allah gave people 'hearing, sight and hearts (al-af'ida)' (16:78), and all three will be questioned (17:36). 'The heart (al-fu'ād) did not lie about what it saw' (53:11). 'The heart of Musa's mother became empty' (28:10).

primaryMeaning: To measure out grain and the like by volume. Kayl is measure; mikyāl is a measuring vessel; iktāla is to receive by measure.
extendedMeaning: 'Woe to those who give less, who, when they take a measure (iktālū) from people, take in full' (83:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times, mostly in commands of fair dealing: 'give full measure (al-kayla) and weight in justice' (6:152), and 'do not decrease the measure (al-mikyāla) and weight' (11:84). Yusuf told his brothers, 'if you do not bring him, there will be no measure (kayla) for you from me' (12:60).

primaryMeaning: The core, the innermost and best part of a thing. Lubb is the kernel — and the mind or understanding, the core of a person.
extendedMeaning: 'None will take heed except people of understanding (ulū al-albāb)' (2:269).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times, all as ulū al-albāb, 'people of understanding' — those with minds that see to the core: 'In the creation of the heavens and the earth … are signs for people of understanding (ulī al-albāb)' (3:190). 'In retribution there is life for you, O people of understanding' (2:179).

primaryMeaning: To be distracted by something pleasant — to be turned from what matters. Lahw is amusement or distraction; alhā is to divert someone.
extendedMeaning: 'Competition for more has diverted you (alhākum)' (102:1). 'Leave them to eat and enjoy, and let hope divert them (yulhihim)' (15:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. 'The life of this world is only play and amusement (lahwun)' (6:32). 'Let not your wealth or children divert you (tulhikum) from the remembrance of Allah' (63:9). 'Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts (tulhīhim) from remembering Allah' (24:37).

primaryMeaning: To smooth and spread out, to make a place ready and comfortable. Mahd is a cradle or bed; mihād is a resting place; mahhada is to prepare the way.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever does good — they are preparing (yamhadūn) for themselves' (30:44). 'I spread out (mahhadtu) for him everything' (74:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 16 times. 'He who made the earth a bed (mahdan) for you' (20:53). ʿĪsā 'will speak to people in the cradle (al-mahd)' (3:46). Hell is called 'an evil resting place (bi'sa al-mihād)' (2:206).

primaryMeaning: To begin, to do something for the first time. Bada'a and abda'a are to start or originate; al-Mubdi' is the One who begins creation.
extendedMeaning: 'As We began (bada'nā) the first creation, We will repeat it' (21:104). Yusuf 'began (fa-bada'a) with their bags before his brother's bag' (12:76).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. 'He begins creation (yabda'u al-khalq) then repeats it' (10:4). 'Do they not see how Allah begins (yubdi'u) creation, then repeats it?' (29:19). 'He began (bada'a) the creation of man from clay' (32:7).

primaryMeaning: To sell or trade — an exchange agreed between two parties. Bayʿ is trade; bāyaʿa is to pledge allegiance, sealing a covenant with a handclasp as in a sale; biyaʿ are churches.
extendedMeaning: 'Rejoice in the bargain (bi-bayʿikum) you have made' (9:111). 'Monasteries, churches (biyaʿun), synagogues and mosques' would have been destroyed without Allah's defence (22:40).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. 'Allah has permitted trade (al-bayʿ) and forbidden usury' (2:275). 'Before a Day comes in which there is no bargaining (bayʿun), no friendship and no intercession' (2:254). 'Those who pledge allegiance to you (yubāyiʿūnaka) are pledging allegiance to Allah' (48:10).

primaryMeaning: A narrow place — a thicket too dense to pass through. Ḥaraj is tightness, difficulty, or a sense of guilt that constricts.
extendedMeaning: Allah makes the breast of the one He leaves astray 'tight and constricted (ḍayyiqan ḥarajan)' (6:125). 'They will not believe until … they find in themselves no discomfort (ḥarajan)' (4:65).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. 'He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty (ḥarajin)' (22:78), and 'Allah does not want to place on you any difficulty' (5:6). 'Let there be in your breast no discomfort (ḥarajun) from it' (7:2). 'There is no blame (ḥarajun) on the blind, the lame or the sick' (24:61).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two senses: freedom — what is pure and free of fault — and heat. Ḥurr is free; taḥrīr is freeing; ḥarīr, 'silk', is the finest, purest cloth; ḥarr is heat.
extendedMeaning: 'The free (al-ḥurr) for the free' in retribution (2:178). ʿImran's wife dedicated her child 'devoted (muḥarraran)' — freed for Allah's service (3:35).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. 'Freeing (taḥrīru) a believing slave' is an expiation (4:92; 5:89). In Paradise 'their garments will be silk (ḥarīrun)' (22:23). 'Do not go out in the heat (al-ḥarr); the fire of Hell is hotter' (9:81).

primaryMeaning: To mount and ride — to get on top of something that carries you. Rakiba is to ride; rakb is a company of riders; rikāb are camels; rukba is the knee, bent as one rides.
extendedMeaning: 'You will surely ride (la-tarkabunna) stage after stage' (84:19). At Badr 'the caravan (al-rakb) was below you' (8:42). Nuh called, 'Ride (irkabū) in it; in the name of Allah is its course' (11:41).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. 'We created for them the like of it in which they ride (yarkabūn)' — the ship (36:42). 'He made for you ships and livestock on which you ride (tarkabūn)' (43:12). 'If you fear, pray on foot or riding (rukbānan)' (2:239).

primaryMeaning: To go in pursuit of something — to seek it or drive it. Sāma is to impose something hard on someone; sīmā is a distinguishing mark; musawwam is branded or marked; asāma is to let livestock graze.
extendedMeaning: Lut's people were struck with stones 'marked (musawwamatan) from your Lord' (11:83). 'From it trees grow on which you pasture your cattle (tusīmūna)' (16:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. Pharaoh's people were 'afflicting you (yasūmūnakum) with the worst torment' (2:49). The poor who do not beg: 'you will recognise them by their mark (bi-sīmāhum)' (2:273). 'Their mark (sīmāhum) is on their faces from the trace of prostration' (48:29).

primaryMeaning: Doubt — being unsure between two sides without settling on either. Shakk is doubt.
extendedMeaning: 'If you are in doubt (shakkin) about what We have revealed to you, ask those who read the Scripture before you' (10:94).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times, almost always as shakk, 'doubt': 'those who differed over it are in doubt (shakkin) about it' — ʿĪsā's death (4:157). The prophets asked, 'Is there any doubt (shakkun) about Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth?' (14:10).

primaryMeaning: To be closed up and solid, without any gap. Ṣamam is deafness — the ear stopped up; aṣamm is deaf; ṣamma is to become deaf.
extendedMeaning: The servants of the Most Merciful, reminded of His verses, 'do not fall upon them deaf (ṣumman) and blind' (25:73).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times, mostly for refusing to hear the truth: 'Deaf (ṣummun), dumb and blind — they will not return' (2:18). 'The worst creatures with Allah are the deaf (al-ṣumm) and dumb who do not reason' (8:22). 'Can you make the deaf (al-ṣumm) hear, even though they do not reason?' (10:42).

primaryMeaning: The palm of the hand — and from it, holding back, as one raises a palm to stop. Kaffa is to restrain; kāffatan is 'all together', as if gathered in one hand.
extendedMeaning: Those who call on false gods are like one 'who stretches out his palms (kaffayhi) to water to reach his mouth' (13:14). 'He withheld (kaffa) the hands of people from you' (48:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. 'Enter into Islam completely (kāffatan)' (2:208). 'We sent you only to all mankind (kāffatan)' (34:28). 'Perhaps Allah will restrain (yakuffa) the might of the disbelievers' (4:84).

primaryMeaning: To pass the hand over something, to wipe it. Masaḥa is to wipe; al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah', is classically explained as the one anointed — wiped with blessing — or the one who wiped the sick and healed them.
extendedMeaning: 'They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah son of Maryam' (9:31). Sulayman 'began to pass (masḥan) his hand over their legs and necks' — his horses (38:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times. Al-Masīḥ is ʿĪsā's title: 'the Messiah (al-masīḥ), ʿĪsā son of Maryam' (3:45). In ablution, 'wipe over (wa-msaḥū) your heads' (5:6), and in dry ablution, 'wipe your faces and hands' (4:43).

primaryMeaning: Rain. Maṭar is rain, but in the Quran it is almost always rain of punishment; amṭara is to rain down.
extendedMeaning: It also appears as ordinary rain: 'there is no blame on you if you are troubled by rain (maṭarin)' when setting down arms (4:102).
quranUsage: Occurs 15 times, mostly for punishment: 'We rained upon them a rain (maṭaran) — see how was the end of the criminals' (7:84). 'Evil was the rain (maṭaru) of those who were warned' (26:173). ʿĀd saw the cloud and said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain (mumṭirunā)' — but it was a punishing wind (46:24).

primaryMeaning: To stay in a place and settle there for good. Mathwā is a lasting abode; thāwī is a dweller.
extendedMeaning: Al-ʿAzīz told his wife, 'Make his stay (mathwāhu) comfortable' — Yusuf (12:21). 'Allah knows your movement and your resting place (mathwākum)' (47:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times, mostly for the final abode: 'Wretched is the abode (mathwā) of the wrongdoers' (3:151), and 'Is there not in Hell an abode (mathwan) for the disbelievers?' (29:68). 'The Fire is your abode (mathwākum)' (6:128).

primaryMeaning: To plough and till the ground so that it yields. Ḥarth is tilled land and its crop — and by extension whatever a person works for.
extendedMeaning: The owners of the garden said, 'Go early to your crop (ḥarthikum)' (68:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. The cow the Israelites were told to slaughter was 'not trained to plough the earth or water the field (al-ḥarth)' (2:71). 'Your wives are a tilth (ḥarthun) for you' (2:223). 'Whoever desires the harvest (ḥartha) of the Hereafter, We increase it for him' (42:20).

primaryMeaning: To throw stones, to stone. Rajm is stoning; rajīm is one driven off with stones — outcast; rajman bil-ghayb is a guess thrown at the unseen.
extendedMeaning: The youths of the Cave feared their people 'will stone you (yarjumūkum)' (18:20). Of the number of the youths: 'guessing at the unseen (rajman bil-ghayb)' (18:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. Al-shayṭān al-rajīm, 'Satan the outcast': 'I seek refuge for her in You from Satan the outcast (al-rajīm)' (3:36), and 'get out, for you are outcast (rajīm)' (15:34). The lamps of the sky were made 'missiles (rujūman) against the devils' (67:5).

primaryMeaning: To be firmly fixed, to anchor. Rasā is to stand firm; rawāsī are firm mountains; mursā is the time or place a ship comes to anchor.
extendedMeaning: 'In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage (mursāhā)' — Nuh's ship (11:41). The jinn made for Sulayman 'cauldrons fixed in place (rāsiyāt)' (34:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times, mostly as rawāsī, 'firm mountains': 'He spread the earth and placed in it firm mountains (rawāsiya) and rivers' (13:3). 'The mountains He set firm (arsāhā)' (79:32). They ask about the Hour, 'when is its arrival (mursāhā)?' (7:187).

primaryMeaning: To sow and cultivate. Zarʿ is a sown crop; zurūʿ are fields of crops.
extendedMeaning: Believers are 'like a crop (ka-zarʿin) that sends out its shoot' (48:29). The garden owner had 'between them crops (zarʿan)' (18:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'Have you seen what you sow? Is it you who make it grow (tazraʿūnahu), or are We the grower?' (56:64). Ibrahim settled his family 'in a valley without cultivation (ghayri dhī zarʿin)' (14:37). Among Allah's gifts are 'crops (al-zarʿa) of varied taste' (6:141).

primaryMeaning: A row, a line — things set side by side in order. Ṣaff is a rank; ṣāffāt are those ranged in rows, or birds with wings spread out.
extendedMeaning: 'Do you not see that the birds with wings spread (ṣāffātin) glorify Him?' (24:41). In Paradise: 'cushions lined up (maṣfūfa)' (88:15).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. People will be 'presented before your Lord in rows (ṣaffan)' (18:48), and angels will stand 'in rows (ṣaffan)' (89:22). 'Allah loves those who fight in His way in a row (ṣaffan), as if they were a solid structure' (61:4). 'By those lined up in rows (al-ṣāffāti)' (37:1).

primaryMeaning: To hold back, to abstain. Ṣawm and ṣiyām are fasting — abstaining from food, drink and relations from dawn to sunset; ṣawm can also be abstaining from speech.
extendedMeaning: Maryam said, 'I have vowed a fast (ṣawman) to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak to anyone today' (19:26).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'Fasting (al-ṣiyām) has been prescribed for you as it was for those before you' (2:183). A fast of three days is an expiation (2:196). 'Men who fast and women who fast (al-ṣā'imāt)' are among those promised forgiveness (33:35).

primaryMeaning: Dimness of sight, especially at nightfall. ʿAshiyy is the late afternoon and evening, when light fades; ʿishā' is nightfall; ʿashā is to turn a blind eye.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever turns a blind eye (yaʿshu) to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign him a devil' (43:36).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times, often for times of remembrance: 'glorify Him morning and evening (ʿashiyyā)' (19:11), and 'in the evening (bil-ʿashiyy) and the early morning' (3:41). Yusuf's brothers 'came to their father at nightfall (ʿishā'an), weeping' (12:16).

primaryMeaning: To give, to hand something over. ʿAṭā' is a gift; aʿṭā is to give.
extendedMeaning: 'Your Lord will give you (yuʿṭīka), and you will be satisfied' (93:5). 'We have given you (aʿṭaynāka) abundance' (108:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'Our Lord is He who gave (aʿṭā) each thing its form, then guided it' (20:50). 'Each We extend — these and those — from the gift (ʿaṭā') of your Lord, and the gift of your Lord is not restricted' (17:20). Paradise is 'a gift (ʿaṭā'an) uninterrupted' (11:108).

primaryMeaning: The vertebrae of the back — faqīr is classically one whose back is broken by need. Faqr is poverty; fuqarā' are the poor.
extendedMeaning: Musa prayed, 'My Lord, I am in need (faqīr) of whatever good You send down to me' (28:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'O mankind, you are the ones in need (al-fuqarā') of Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient' (35:15). Charity is 'for the poor (lil-fuqarā') who are restrained in the way of Allah' (2:273). 'Satan promises you poverty (al-faqr)' (2:268).

primaryMeaning: To blame, to reproach. Lawm is blame; malūm is blameworthy; lawwāma is one who blames often — the self-reproaching soul.
extendedMeaning: Yunus was swallowed 'while he was blameworthy (mulīm)' (37:142). Believers strive 'not fearing the blame (lawmata) of a critic' (5:54).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'I swear by the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwāma)' (75:2). Satan will say, 'Do not blame me (talūmūnī), blame yourselves (lūmū)' (14:22). Those who guard their chastity except with spouses 'are not to be blamed (malūmīn)' (23:6).

primaryMeaning: To describe — to set out the qualities of something. In the Quran it most often means to attribute, especially falsely, to Allah.
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'Exalted is He above what they describe (yaṣifūn)' (6:100). Yaʿqub said, 'Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe (taṣifūn)' (12:18). 'Do not say, about what your tongues falsely describe (taṣifu), "This is lawful and this is forbidden"' (16:116).

primaryMeaning: To enter and pass into something. Walaja is to go in; awlaja is to make something enter another; walīja is a close insider, one taken into confidence.
extendedMeaning: Believers did not take 'besides Allah … any intimate (walījatan)' (9:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 14 times. 'You make the night enter (tūliju) the day and the day enter the night' (3:27). Allah 'knows what enters (yaliju) the earth and what comes out of it' (34:2). The deniers will not enter Paradise 'until a camel passes (yalija) through the eye of a needle' (7:40).

primaryMeaning: To refuse firmly — to decline something and hold back from it.
extendedMeaning: 'Let no witness refuse (lā ya'ba) when called' (2:282). The heavens, earth and mountains 'refused (fa-abayna) to bear' the trust (33:72).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. The angels prostrated 'except Iblis; he refused (abā) and was arrogant' (2:34). 'Most people refuse (fa-abā) anything but disbelief' (17:89). 'Allah refuses (ya'bā) except to perfect His light' (9:32).

primaryMeaning: To come upon someone suddenly, without warning. Baghtatan is 'suddenly' or 'unexpectedly'.
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, all as baghtatan, mostly about the Hour or punishment: 'until the Hour comes to them suddenly (baghtatan)' (6:31), and 'We seized them suddenly (baghtatan) while they did not perceive' (7:95). 'It will not come to you except suddenly' (7:187).

primaryMeaning: Skin, and from its toughness, endurance and firmness. Jild is skin; jalada is to flog — to strike the skin; jalad is steadfast endurance.
extendedMeaning: 'Flog (fa-jlidū) each of them a hundred lashes (jalda)' (24:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. The skins of the people of the Fire are renewed: 'every time their skins (julūduhum) are roasted through, We replace them' (4:56). On the Day of Judgment their skins will testify against them (41:20–21). At the Quran's recitation 'the skins (julūd) of those who fear their Lord shiver' (39:23).

primaryMeaning: Ibn Fāris gives two senses: nearness — jār is a neighbour, and ajāra is to give someone the protection a neighbour owes — and swerving from the path, jawr, injustice.
extendedMeaning: If a polytheist 'seeks your protection (istajāraka), protect him (fa-ajirhu) so he may hear the word of Allah' (9:6). On the earth 'are neighbouring (mutajāwirāt) tracts' (13:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. Kindness is due to 'the near neighbour and the distant neighbour (al-jār)' (4:36). Allah 'protects (yujīru), and none can protect against Him' (23:88). 'No one can protect me (yujīranī) from Allah' (72:22).

primaryMeaning: To swear an oath. Ḥalafa is to swear; ḥallāf is one who swears often.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not obey every habitual swearer (ḥallāfin), worthless' (68:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, mostly for the hypocrites' oaths: 'they come to you swearing (yaḥlifūna) by Allah, "We intended only good"' (4:62), and 'they swear (yaḥlifūna) by Allah that they are of you, but they are not' (9:56). Broken oaths need expiation: 'that is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn (ḥalaftum)' (5:89).

primaryMeaning: To turn back, to go round; and intense whiteness. Ḥāra is to return; ḥāwara is to talk back and forth — to converse; ḥawāriyyūn are the disciples of ʿĪsā, classically linked to the pure white of their garments or hearts; ḥūr are companions with eyes whose white is striking.
extendedMeaning: 'He thought he would never return (yaḥūra)' — to his Lord (84:14). 'Allah has heard your conversation (taḥāwurakumā)' (58:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'The disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn) said, "We are the helpers of Allah"' (3:52). The garden owner said to his companion 'while conversing with him (yuḥāwiruhu)' (18:34). In Paradise are ḥūr ʿīn, 'fair companions with beautiful eyes' (44:54).

primaryMeaning: To store up and keep safe. Khazīna is a treasury; khazā'in are treasures; khazana are keepers or guards.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf said, 'Put me over the storehouses (khazā'in) of the land' (12:55). 'You are not the storers (bi-khāzinīn) of it' — rainwater (15:22).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'I do not say to you that I have the treasures (khazā'inu) of Allah' (6:50). 'There is nothing but that its treasuries (khazā'inuhu) are with Us' (15:21). The keepers (khazanatuhā) of Paradise and Hell greet or question those who arrive (39:71–73).

primaryMeaning: A gap between two things, and what passes through it. Khilāl is 'in the midst of'; khalīl is an intimate friend, whose love passes through every part of the heart; khulla is close friendship.
extendedMeaning: 'Close friends (al-akhillā') that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-conscious' (43:67).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend (khalīlan)' (4:125). The Day will come 'with no bargaining, no friendship (khulla), and no intercession' (2:254). Rain comes 'out of their midst (khilālihi)' — the clouds (24:43).

primaryMeaning: The most tender kind of mercy — gentle compassion. Ra'fa is kindness; ra'ūf is full of kindness.
extendedMeaning: 'Let not pity (ra'fatun) for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah' (24:2). Allah placed 'compassion (ra'fatan) and mercy' in the hearts of ʿĪsā's followers (57:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, mostly as ra'ūf, describing Allah — 'Allah is, to the people, Kind (la-ra'ūfun) and Merciful' (2:143) — and the Prophet: 'to the believers he is kind (ra'ūfun) and merciful' (9:128).

primaryMeaning: To bow the head and back — to bend low. Rukūʿ is bowing in prayer; rākiʿ is one who bows.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim and Ismail were told to purify the House 'for those who bow and prostrate (al-rukkaʿ al-sujūd)' (2:125). Dawud 'fell down bowing (rākiʿan) and turned in repentance' (38:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Establish prayer, give zakah, and bow (warkaʿū) with those who bow (al-rākiʿīn)' (2:43). 'O you who believe, bow (irkaʿū) and prostrate' (22:77). Maryam was told, 'bow (warkaʿī) with those who bow' (3:43).

primaryMeaning: Desire — a strong longing of the self for something. Shahwa is appetite or lust; ishtahā is to desire; shahawāt are the objects of desire.
extendedMeaning: 'There will be in it whatever souls desire (tashtahīhi) and eyes delight in' (43:71). Those who follow desires 'want you to deviate greatly' (4:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Beautified for people is the love of desires (al-shahawāt) — women, sons, heaped-up gold and silver' (3:14). Lut's people came to men 'with desire (shahwatan) instead of women' (7:81). In Paradise 'you will have whatever your souls desire (tashtahī)' (41:31).

primaryMeaning: To be small — in size, age or standing. Ṣaghīr is small; ṣāghir is one made small — humbled and disgraced.
extendedMeaning: The jizya is paid 'while they are humbled (ṣāghirūn)' (9:29). The book 'leaves nothing small (ṣaghīratan) or great but it has recorded it' (18:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Do not be weary of writing it, small (ṣaghīran) or large' — the debt (2:282). 'Every matter, small (ṣaghīrin) and great, is recorded' (54:53). Iblis was told, 'Get out, you are of the disgraced (al-ṣāghirīn)' (7:13).

primaryMeaning: To shout, to cry out loudly. Ṣayḥa is a shout — the mighty blast that destroyed some peoples, and the blast of the resurrection.
extendedMeaning: The hypocrites 'think every shout (ṣayḥatin) is against them' (63:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, mostly for punishment: 'the blast (al-ṣayḥa) seized those who had wronged' — Thamud (11:67). 'It was only one blast (ṣayḥatan), and they were extinguished' (36:29). 'The Day they hear the blast (al-ṣayḥa) in truth — that is the Day of coming out' (50:42).

primaryMeaning: To be narrow, tight — the opposite of wide. Ḍāqa is to be straitened; ḍayq is distress; ḍayyiq is constricted.
extendedMeaning: When the angels came to Lut, 'he was distressed for them and felt straitened (ḍāqa)' (11:77). 'We know that your breast is straitened (yaḍīqu) by what they say' (15:97).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. At Hunayn 'the earth, with all its breadth, was straitened (ḍāqat) for you' (9:25). The one Allah leaves astray has his breast 'tight and constricted (ḍayyiqan ḥarajan)' (6:125). 'Do not be in distress (ḍayqin) over what they plot' (16:127).

primaryMeaning: To become still and settled after disturbance. Iṭma'anna is to be at rest, reassured; ṭuma'nīna is tranquillity; muṭma'inn is one whose heart is at peace.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah made it only as good news for you, and so that your hearts would be reassured (li-taṭma'inna) by it' (3:126). Those 'satisfied (iṭma'annū) with the life of this world' do not hope to meet Allah (10:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'In the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest (taṭma'innu)' (13:28). Ibrahim asked to see how the dead are raised 'so that my heart may be reassured (li-yaṭma'inna)' (2:260). 'O soul at peace (al-muṭma'inna)' (89:27).

primaryMeaning: To hold back and protect — to keep someone from harm. ʿĀṣim is a protector; iʿtaṣama is to hold on for protection.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf said of the seduction, 'he refused (fa-staʿṣama)' (12:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Hold firmly (iʿtaṣimū) to the rope of Allah all together' (3:103). Nuh's son said, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me (yaʿṣimunī) from the water', and Nuh answered, 'There is no protector (ʿāṣima) today from the command of Allah' (11:43). 'Allah will protect you (yaʿṣimuka) from the people' (5:67).

primaryMeaning: To be thick and coarse — the opposite of fine and gentle. Ghilẓa is harshness; ghalīẓ is thick, heavy or severe.
extendedMeaning: 'Strive against the disbelievers and hypocrites, and be stern (wa-ughluẓ) with them' (9:73). Hell's angels are 'stern (ghilāẓun) and severe' (66:6).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Had you been harsh and hard-hearted (ghalīẓa al-qalb), they would have scattered from around you' (3:159). Marriage is 'a firm covenant (mīthāqan ghalīẓā)' (4:21). 'We saved them from a harsh (ghalīẓ) punishment' (11:58).

primaryMeaning: A boy — a young male from birth to youth, full of growing strength. Ghulām is a boy or youth; ghilmān are youths who serve.
extendedMeaning: 'Youths (ghilmānun) of theirs will circulate among them' in Paradise (52:24). The traveller who found Yusuf in the well cried, 'This is a boy (ghulām)!' (12:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, often in news of a son: Zakariyya asked, 'How will I have a boy (ghulāmun) when I am old?' (3:40). The angels gave Ibrahim 'good news of a knowing boy (bi-ghulāmin ʿalīm)' (15:53). Al-Khiḍr killed a boy (ghulāman) whose parents were believers (18:74, 18:80).

primaryMeaning: To ransom — to give something in place of another to free them. Fidya is a ransom or compensation; fadā is to redeem.
extendedMeaning: 'The criminal will wish he could be ransomed (yaftadī) from the punishment of that Day by his children' (70:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. Those unable to fast pay 'a ransom (fidyatun): feeding a poor person' (2:184). 'We ransomed him (fadaynāhu) with a great sacrifice' — Ibrahim's son (37:107). The deniers 'would offer it as ransom (la-ftadaw)' if they owned the earth twice over (13:18).

primaryMeaning: The mouth. Fam is a mouth; afwāh are mouths — often used for what is said only with the lips.
extendedMeaning: 'They want to put out the light of Allah with their mouths (bi-afwāhihim)' (9:32). The false caller is like one who stretches his hands to water 'to reach his mouth (fāhu)' (13:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, often for empty words: 'They say with their mouths (bi-afwāhihim) what is not in their hearts' (3:167). 'Hatred has appeared from their mouths (afwāhihim)' (3:118). 'You uttered with your mouths (bi-afwāhikum) what you had no knowledge of' (24:15).

primaryMeaning: To cut — to cut off a piece of something. Qarḍ, 'a loan', is a portion of one's wealth cut off and given, to be returned later.
extendedMeaning: The sun 'passes them on the left (taqriḍuhum)' — the people of the Cave (18:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan (qarḍan ḥasanā), so He may multiply it for him many times?' (2:245). 'Lend (aqriḍū) Allah a goodly loan' (73:20). 'If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you' (64:17).

primaryMeaning: Devoted, constant obedience — standing long in worship and humility. Qunūt is devotion; qānit is devoutly obedient.
extendedMeaning: 'Is one who is devout (qānitun) through the hours of the night, prostrating and standing …' (39:9). Ibrahim was 'a nation, devoutly obedient (qānitan) to Allah' (16:120).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'All are devoutly obedient (qānitūn) to Him' (2:116). 'Stand before Allah devoutly obedient (qānitīn)' (2:238). Maryam was told, 'be devoutly obedient (uqnutī) to your Lord' (3:43).

primaryMeaning: To appear, to come out — a star appears in the sky, and a plant comes up from the ground. Najm is a star; nujūm are stars; najm is also a plant without a stem.
extendedMeaning: 'The star and the tree (wal-najm wal-shajar) prostrate' (55:6) — najm here is classically explained as the stemless plant. Ibrahim 'took a look at the stars (al-nujūm)' (37:88).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'By the star (wal-najm) when it descends' (53:1). The stars are for guidance: 'by the stars (bil-najm) they are guided' (16:16), and 'the sun, the moon and the stars (al-nujūm) subjected by His command' (7:54). 'When the stars (al-nujūm) are obliterated' (77:8).

primaryMeaning: To be sincere and pure — the way pure honey is free of wax. Nuṣḥ is sincere counsel, wishing good for someone; nāṣiḥ is a sincere adviser.
extendedMeaning: Tawbatan naṣūḥā, 'sincere repentance', is urged in 66:8. Musa's sister asked, 'Shall I guide you to a household … who will be sincere (nāṣiḥūn) to him?' (28:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times, often in the prophets' words: 'I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you sincerely (anṣaḥu)' (7:62), and 'I am a trustworthy adviser (nāṣiḥun) to you' (7:68). Satan deceived Adam, swearing, 'I am a sincere adviser (al-nāṣiḥīn) to you' (7:21).

primaryMeaning: A fixed time — a limit set for something. Waqt is time; mīqāt is an appointed time or place; mawqūt is set at fixed times.
extendedMeaning: The new moons are 'markers of time (mawāqītu) for people and for Hajj' (2:189). Satan was given respite 'until the Day of the time (al-waqt) well-known' (15:38).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'Prayer is prescribed for the believers at fixed times (mawqūtā)' (4:103). Musa came 'to Our appointed time (li-mīqātinā)' (7:143). 'The Day of Decision is their appointed time (mīqātuhum), all of them' (44:40).

primaryMeaning: To lose hope — to despair of something. Ya's is despair; ya'ūs is one who despairs.
extendedMeaning: 'When evil touches him, he is in despair (ya'ūsā)' (17:83).
quranUsage: Occurs 13 times. 'None despairs (yay'asu) of the relief of Allah except the disbelieving people' (12:87). 'Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah … have despaired (ya'isū) of My mercy' (29:23). 'Today the disbelievers have despaired (ya'isa) of your religion' (5:3).

primaryMeaning: To hold back what should be given — stinginess, the opposite of generosity. Bukhl is miserliness.
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Let not those who withhold (yabkhalūna) what Allah has given them of His bounty think it good for them' (3:180). 'Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess (bil-bukhl) on people' (4:37). 'Whoever withholds (yabkhal) is only withholding from himself' (47:38).

primaryMeaning: The start of something — being first or early. Bukra is early morning; ibkār is the time from dawn to mid-morning; bikr is a virgin, one untouched, at the start.
extendedMeaning: The companions of Paradise were made 'virgins (abkāran)' (56:36).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, mostly for times of glorification: 'glorify Him morning (bukratan) and evening' (19:11), and 'glorify in the evening and the morning (al-ibkār)' (3:41). The cow of the Israelites was 'neither old nor young (bikr)' (2:68).

primaryMeaning: Whiteness. Abyaḍ is white; ibyaḍḍa is to turn white; bayḍ are eggs.
extendedMeaning: The fast lasts 'until the white thread (al-khayṭ al-abyaḍ) becomes distinct from the black thread of dawn' (2:187). The maidens of Paradise are 'as if they were sheltered eggs (bayḍun)' (37:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. Musa's hand 'came out white (bayḍā'), without harm' (20:22). 'The Day some faces will turn white (tabyaḍḍu) and some faces black' (3:106). Yaʿqub's eyes 'became white (ibyaḍḍat) from grief' (12:84).

primaryMeaning: To gather and collect — as water is gathered into a cistern. Ijtabā is to choose — to gather someone to oneself, selecting them.
extendedMeaning: Fruits of every kind 'are brought (yujbā) to it' — the sanctuary of Makkah (28:57).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, mostly for Allah choosing His prophets: 'Thus will your Lord choose you (yajtabīka)' — Yusuf (12:6). 'He chose him (ijtabāhu) and guided him to a straight path' — Ibrahim (16:121). 'Allah chooses (yajtabī) of His messengers whom He wills' (3:179).

primaryMeaning: To deny something while knowing it is true — refusal against one's own knowledge.
extendedMeaning: 'None rejects (yajḥadu) Our signs except the disbelievers' (29:47).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'They do not deny you, but the wrongdoers reject (yajḥadūna) the signs of Allah' (6:33). Pharaoh's people 'rejected them (jaḥadū), while their souls were convinced of them' (27:14). ʿĀd 'rejected (jaḥadū) the signs of their Lord' (11:59).

primaryMeaning: To uncover, to lay bare — and to be worn out. Ḥasra is intense regret, when the truth is laid bare and one sees what was lost; ḥasīr is exhausted.
extendedMeaning: Look again at the sky: 'your sight will return to you humbled and exhausted (ḥasīr)' (67:4). Yawm al-ḥasra, 'the Day of Regret', is a name of the Day of Judgment (19:39).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Alas, our regret (yā ḥasratanā) over what we neglected' (6:31). 'Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets (ḥasarātin) upon them' (2:167). 'Alas for mankind (yā ḥasratan ʿalā al-ʿibād)' (36:30).

primaryMeaning: To incline, to turn away from something towards another. Ḥanīf is one who has turned away from false worship and inclined towards the true faith — upright.
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, mostly describing Ibrahim: 'the religion of Ibrahim, the upright (ḥanīfan); he was not of the polytheists' (2:135). 'Set your face to the religion, inclining to truth (ḥanīfan)' (30:30). Believers are to be 'upright (ḥunafā') for Allah, not associating anything with Him' (22:31).

primaryMeaning: To fall down, with a sound — as water falls or a person drops to the ground. Kharra is to fall prostrate.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever associates with Allah — it is as if he had fallen (kharra) from the sky' (22:31). Yusuf's family 'fell down (kharrū) before him in prostration' (12:100).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Musa fell down (kharra) unconscious' when the mountain crumbled (7:143). When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited, the prophets 'fall down (kharrū) in prostration, weeping' (19:58). The people of knowledge 'fall upon their faces (yakhirrūna) in prostration' (17:107).

primaryMeaning: To speak to someone directly. Khāṭaba is to address; khiṭāb is speech; khiṭba is a marriage proposal; khaṭb is a weighty matter that calls for words.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim asked the angels, 'What is your business (khaṭbukum)?' (15:57). There is no blame in hinting at 'a proposal of marriage (khiṭbat)' to widows (2:235).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. Nuh was told, 'Do not address Me (tukhāṭibnī) concerning those who did wrong' (11:37). 'When the ignorant address them (khāṭabahum), they say, "Peace"' (25:63). Dawud was given 'wisdom and decisive speech (faṣl al-khiṭāb)' (38:20).

primaryMeaning: To wade into water — and by extension to plunge into talk, especially idle or mocking talk.
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'When you see those who engage (yakhūḍūna) in mocking Our verses, turn away from them' (6:68). The hypocrites said, 'We were only conversing and playing (nakhūḍu)' (9:65). The people of the Fire say, 'We used to indulge in vain talk with those who indulged (al-khā'iḍīn)' (74:45).

primaryMeaning: To reach something that is ahead, to catch up with it. Adraka is to overtake or grasp; darak is a level going down; tadāraka is to reach someone in time.
extendedMeaning: 'The hypocrites will be in the lowest level (al-darak al-asfal) of the Fire' (4:145). 'Had not a favour from his Lord reached him (tadārakahu)' — Yunus (68:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Vision cannot grasp Him (lā tudrikuhu), but He grasps all vision' (6:103). 'Wherever you are, death will overtake you (yudrikkum)' (4:78). 'It is not for the sun to overtake (tudrika) the moon' (36:40).

primaryMeaning: Fear joined with watchfulness and caution. Rahba is awe; ruhbān are monks, who renounce the world out of fear of Allah; rahbāniyya is monasticism.
extendedMeaning: 'They took their scholars and monks (ruhbānahum) as lords besides Allah' (9:31). 'Monasticism (rahbāniyya) they invented; We did not prescribe it for them' (57:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Fear Me alone (fa-rhabūni)' (2:40). The prophets 'called on Us in hope and fear (rahaban)' (21:90). 'Among them are priests and monks (ruhbān), and they are not arrogant' (5:82).

primaryMeaning: To confine, to shut someone in. Sijn is a prison; sajana is to imprison. Sijjīn is the register of the wicked, classically explained as a place of deep confinement.
extendedMeaning: 'The record of the wicked is in Sijjīn. And what will make you know what Sijjīn is?' (83:7–8).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, mostly in the story of Yusuf: the wife of al-ʿAzīz said, 'he will surely be imprisoned (la-yusjananna)' (12:32), and Yusuf answered, 'My Lord, prison (al-sijn) is dearer to me than what they invite me to' (12:33). 'O my two companions of the prison (al-sijn)' (12:39).

primaryMeaning: To uncover, to lay open. Safar, 'a journey', uncovers the traveller's character and brings him out into open country; asfara is for dawn to break; safara are scribes, who make things plain in writing; asfār are large books.
extendedMeaning: 'Some faces that Day will be bright (musfira)' (80:38). Those who carried the Torah but did not act on it are 'like a donkey carrying books (asfārā)' (62:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Whoever is ill or on a journey (safarin), then an equal number of other days' (2:184). Musa said, 'We have met fatigue on this journey of ours (safarinā)' (18:62). The pages of revelation are 'in the hands of scribes (safaratin), noble and righteous' (80:15–16).

primaryMeaning: To go along a path — and to thread something through, as a string passes through beads. Salaka is to travel or to insert; maslak is a way.
extendedMeaning: 'Thus We have inserted it (salaknāhu) into the hearts of the criminals' (26:200). The bee is told, 'follow (fa-slukī) the ways of your Lord' (16:69).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'He threaded (salaka) for you roads in it' — the earth (20:53). Musa was told, 'Insert (usluk) your hand into your garment' (28:32). The people of the Fire are asked, 'What led you (salakakum) into Saqar?' (74:42).

primaryMeaning: To be like something, to resemble it. Shibh is a likeness; tashābaha is for things to look alike; mutashābih is similar — or ambiguous, open to more than one meaning; shubbiha is to be made to appear like another.
extendedMeaning: The Israelites said, 'Cows look alike (tashābaha) to us' (2:70). 'Their hearts are alike (tashābahat)' — the deniers of every age (2:118).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. The fruits of Paradise are 'given to them in resemblance (mutashābihan)' (2:25). Some verses are muḥkamāt, precise, and others mutashābihāt, 'open to interpretation' (3:7). Of ʿĪsā: 'they did not kill him or crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum)' (4:157).

primaryMeaning: Hardship and misery — the opposite of saʿāda, 'happiness'. Shaqā' is wretchedness; shaqiyy is one who is wretched and deprived of good.
extendedMeaning: Zakariyya prayed, 'I have never been unhappy (shaqiyyan) in my prayer to You, my Lord' (19:4). 'The most wretched one (al-ashqā) will avoid it' — the reminder (87:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. On the Day of Judgment 'among them will be the wretched (shaqiyyun) and the happy' (11:105). 'Whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor suffer (yashqā)' (20:123). The people of the Fire will say, 'Our wretchedness (shiqwatunā) overcame us' (23:106).

primaryMeaning: The left side, and the north wind that comes from the left of one facing east. From covering on all sides comes ishtamala, 'to contain, to include'.
extendedMeaning: Aṣḥāb al-shimāl, 'the companions of the left', are the damned (56:41). 'What the wombs of the two females contain (ishtamalat)' (6:143).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. The sun passed the Cave 'on the left (dhāta al-shimāl)' (18:17). 'As for him who is given his record in his left hand (bi-shimālihi), he will say, "I wish I had not been given my record"' (69:25). Iblis vowed to come at people 'from their right and their left (shamā'ilihim)' (7:17).

primaryMeaning: To follow and support; and to spread about. Shīʿa is a party of followers who support someone; shiyaʿ are sects; shāʿa is for news to spread.
extendedMeaning: 'Those who love that immorality should spread (tashīʿa) among the believers' face a painful punishment (24:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Those who divided their religion and became sects (shiyaʿan)' (6:159). Musa found two men fighting, 'one of his own party (shīʿatihi)' (28:15). 'Among his party (shīʿatihi) was Ibrahim' — following Nuh's way (37:83).

primaryMeaning: To long for something and hope to get it — strong desire, praised when it is hope in Allah and blamed when it is greed. Ṭamaʿ is hope or craving.
extendedMeaning: 'Then he desires (yaṭmaʿu) that I should add more' — the denier (74:15). 'Do you hope (a-fa-taṭmaʿūna) that they will believe you?' (2:75).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Call on Him in fear and hope (ṭamaʿan)' (7:56). The magicians said, 'We hope (naṭmaʿu) that our Lord will forgive us our sins' (26:51). The Prophet's wives are told not to speak softly 'lest he in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire (fa-yaṭmaʿa)' (33:32).

primaryMeaning: Clay — earth mixed with water. Ṭīn is clay or mud.
extendedMeaning: 'We created man from an extract of clay (ṭīn)' (23:12). Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, light a fire on the clay (al-ṭīn) for me' — to make bricks (28:38).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, mostly for the creation of man: 'It is He who created you from clay (ṭīnin)' (6:2). Iblis refused to prostrate, saying, 'You created me from fire and created him from clay (ṭīnan)' (17:61; 7:12). ʿĪsā made 'from clay (al-ṭīn) the shape of a bird' (3:49).

primaryMeaning: To wipe out the trace of a fault — to offer an excuse. ʿUdhr is an excuse; iʿtadhara is to apologise; maʿdhira is justification.
extendedMeaning: 'Man will be a witness against himself, even if he presents his excuses (maʿādhīrahu)' (75:15). Those who warned the Sabbath-breakers said, 'To be absolved (maʿdhiratan) before your Lord' (7:164).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Make no excuse (lā taʿtadhirū); you have disbelieved after your belief' (9:66). 'That Day their excuses (maʿdhiratuhum) will not benefit those who wronged' (30:57). Musa said, 'You have received from me an excuse (ʿudhran)' (18:76).

primaryMeaning: Difficulty and hardship — the opposite of yusr, 'ease'. ʿUsr is hardship; ʿasīr is hard; ʿusra is a time of difficulty.
extendedMeaning: 'That Day will be a hard (ʿasīrun) Day for the disbelievers' (74:9–10). Musa asked, 'Do not impose on me difficulty (ʿusran)' (18:73).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'With hardship (al-ʿusr) comes ease' (94:5–6). 'Allah will bring about ease after hardship (ʿusrin)' (65:7). 'If the debtor is in difficulty (ʿusratin), then give him time until ease' (2:280).

primaryMeaning: A staff or stick — a length of wood to lean on or strike with. ʿAṣā is a staff; ʿiṣiyy are staffs.
extendedMeaning: Musa said, 'It is my staff (ʿaṣāya); I lean on it and beat leaves with it for my sheep' (20:18). The magicians threw 'their ropes and their staffs (ʿiṣiyyuhum)' (20:66).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, mostly for the staff of Musa: 'Strike the stone with your staff (bi-ʿaṣāka)' (2:60). 'He threw his staff (ʿaṣāhu), and it was a serpent, manifest' (7:107). 'Throw your staff (ʿaṣāka)', and it swallowed what the magicians had faked (7:117).

primaryMeaning: To help, to support. Ista'āna is to ask for help; taʿāwana is to help one another; mustaʿān is the one whose help is sought.
extendedMeaning: Yaʿqub said, 'Allah is the One whose help is sought (al-mustaʿān)' (12:18). The cow was 'of middle age (ʿawānun)' (2:68).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. Iyyāka nastaʿīn, 'You alone we ask for help' (1:5). 'Seek help (istaʿīnū) through patience and prayer' (2:45). 'Help one another (taʿāwanū) in righteousness and piety, and do not help one another in sin' (5:2).

primaryMeaning: To cover and shelter, to keep something hidden and safe. Akinna are coverings; kinn is a shelter; maknūn is well guarded or concealed; akanna is to hide within.
extendedMeaning: The companions of Paradise are 'like pearls well guarded (al-lu'lu' al-maknūn)' (56:23). 'He made for you shelters (aknānan) in the mountains' (16:81).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'We have placed over their hearts coverings (akinnatan) lest they understand it' (6:25). 'Your Lord knows what their breasts conceal (tukinnu)' (27:74). The Quran is 'in a well-guarded Book (kitābin maknūn)' (56:78).

primaryMeaning: Flesh, meat. Laḥm is flesh; it joins bone together, and the root is also used for things joined firmly.
extendedMeaning: 'Would one of you like to eat the flesh (laḥma) of his dead brother?' — about backbiting (49:12). 'Their meat and their blood do not reach Allah, but your piety does' (22:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. Forbidden foods include 'the flesh (laḥma) of swine' (2:173). The man raised after a hundred years was shown bones clothed 'with flesh (laḥman)' (2:259), and 'We clothed the bones with flesh' (23:14). In Paradise 'meat (laḥmi) of fowl, whatever they desire' (56:21).

primaryMeaning: To throw something aside, to cast it away as worthless. Nabadha is to discard; intabadha is to withdraw to one side.
extendedMeaning: 'He will surely be thrown (la-yunbadhanna) into the Crusher' (104:4). Maryam 'withdrew (intabadhat) from her family to a place towards the east' (19:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'Whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside (nabadhahu)' (2:100). 'A party of them threw (nabadha) the Book of Allah behind their backs' (2:101). 'We seized him and his soldiers and threw them (fa-nabadhnāhum) into the sea' (28:40).

primaryMeaning: A small amount of liquid, a drop. Nuṭfa is a drop of fluid — the drop from which a person is created.
extendedMeaning: 'Was he not a drop (nuṭfatan) of fluid emitted?' (75:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times, always as nuṭfa, in the stages of creation: 'He created man from a drop (nuṭfatin), then he is a clear opponent' (16:4). 'We placed him as a drop (nuṭfatan) in a firm lodging, then We made the drop a clinging clot' (23:13–14).

primaryMeaning: To speak clearly — to put thought into words. Naṭaqa is to speak; manṭiq is speech or language; anṭaqa is to make speak.
extendedMeaning: Sulayman said, 'We have been taught the language (manṭiq) of birds' (27:16). The skins will say, 'Allah, who made everything speak, made us speak (anṭaqanā)' (41:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. Ibrahim said of the idols, 'Ask them, if they can speak (yanṭiqūn)' (21:63). 'We have a record which speaks (yanṭiqu) the truth' (23:62). 'He does not speak (yanṭiqu) from desire; it is only a revelation revealed' (53:3–4).

primaryMeaning: To attain, to get hold of what one seeks. Nāla is to reach or obtain; nayl is gain.
extendedMeaning: 'They planned what they could not attain (yanālū)' (9:74).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'You will never attain (tanālū) righteousness until you spend from what you love' (3:92). 'My covenant does not reach (yanālu) the wrongdoers' (2:124). 'Their meat and blood do not reach (yanāla) Allah, but piety from you reaches Him' (22:37).

primaryMeaning: A valley — ground where water flows. Wādī is a valley; diya is blood money, paid to the family of one who was killed.
extendedMeaning: Killing a believer by mistake requires 'blood money (diyatun) paid to his family' (4:92).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. 'You are in the sacred valley (bil-wādi al-muqaddas), Ṭuwā' (20:12). The ants spoke 'when they came to the valley (wādi) of the ants' (27:18). The poets 'wander in every valley (wādin)' (26:225).

primaryMeaning: To join one thing to another, to connect — and to arrive, to reach. Waṣala is to join or reach; waṣṣala is to make continuous.
extendedMeaning: The angels told Lut, 'they will never reach you (yaṣilū)' (11:81).
quranUsage: Occurs 12 times. The wrongdoers 'cut what Allah commanded to be joined (yūṣala)' (2:27), while the believers 'join what Allah commanded to be joined' (13:21). 'We have made the word continuous (waṣṣalnā) for them' — sending revelation in succession (28:51).

primaryMeaning: To make strong, to support. Ayyada is to strengthen someone; ayd is strength and power.
extendedMeaning: 'Remember Our servant Dawud, the possessor of strength (dhā al-ayd)' (38:17). 'The heaven We built with strength (bi-aydin)' (51:47).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'We supported him (ayyadnāhu) with the Holy Spirit' — ʿĪsā (2:87). 'Allah supports (yu'ayyidu) with His help whom He wills' (3:13). 'He supported him (ayyadahu) with soldiers you did not see' — in the cave (9:40).

primaryMeaning: Beauty — and gathering things into a whole. Jamāl is beauty; jamīl is beautiful or gracious; jumla is a whole taken together; jamal is a camel.
extendedMeaning: The deniers will not enter Paradise 'until a camel (al-jamal) passes through the eye of a needle' (7:40). 'Release them in a gracious release (sarāḥan jamīlā)' (33:28).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. Yaʿqub said, 'So patience is beautiful (ṣabrun jamīl)' (12:18). 'Forgive with gracious forgiveness (al-ṣafḥ al-jamīl)' (15:85). The deniers asked, 'Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once (jumlatan)?' (25:32).

primaryMeaning: War and fighting. Ḥarb is war; ḥāraba is to wage war. Miḥrāb, a private chamber for prayer, is classically explained as a place of struggle against Satan, or the most honoured part of a house.
extendedMeaning: 'Be informed of a war (ḥarb) from Allah and His Messenger' — to those who persist in usury (2:279). The jinn made for Sulayman 'elevated chambers (maḥārīb) and statues' (34:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'The recompense of those who wage war (yuḥāribūna) against Allah and His Messenger' is set out in 5:33. 'Whenever they kindle the fire of war (lil-ḥarb), Allah puts it out' (5:64). Zakariyya found provision with Maryam 'whenever he entered upon her in the prayer chamber (al-miḥrāb)' (3:37).

primaryMeaning: Pebbles — and counting, since pebbles were used to count. Aḥṣā is to count or take full account of something.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah has enumerated it (aḥṣāhu), while they forgot it' (58:6). 'Keep count (wa-aḥṣū) of the waiting period' (65:1).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'If you tried to count (tuḥṣūhā) the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them' (14:34). 'Everything We have enumerated (aḥṣaynāhu) in a clear register' (36:12). The book 'leaves nothing small or great but it has enumerated it (aḥṣāhā)' (18:49).

primaryMeaning: To suckle at the breast. Raḍāʿa is nursing; arḍaʿa is to nurse a child; murḍiʿa is a nursing mother.
extendedMeaning: 'We had forbidden to him the wet nurses (al-marāḍiʿ) before' — Musa (28:12). On the Day of Judgment 'every nursing mother (murḍiʿatin) will forget what she nursed' (22:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'Mothers shall nurse (yurḍiʿna) their children two full years' (2:233), and a wet nurse may be sought (tastarḍiʿū) (2:233). Foster-mothers and foster-sisters 'through nursing (al-raḍāʿa)' are forbidden in marriage (4:23).

primaryMeaning: To write — and a thick piece of iron. Zabūr is a written book — the scripture given to Dawud; zubur are books; zubar are pieces, large chunks.
extendedMeaning: 'Bring me sheets (zubar) of iron' — Dhu al-Qarnayn's barrier (18:96). Communities 'split their affair among them into sects (zuburan)' (23:53).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'We gave Dawud the Zabūr (zabūran)' (4:163). Earlier messengers came 'with clear proofs and scriptures (al-zubur)' (3:184). 'Everything they did is in the records (al-zubur)' (54:52).

primaryMeaning: A rope that connects one thing to another — and so any means or cause that leads to something. Sabab is a means; asbāb are ties and ways; sabba is to insult.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not insult (lā tasubbū) those they call on besides Allah, lest they insult Allah' (6:108). Pharaoh said, 'Build me a tower, that I may reach the ways (al-asbāb)' (40:36).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'We gave Dhu al-Qarnayn of everything a means (sababan)' (18:84), 'so he followed a way (sababan)' (18:85). On the Day of Judgment 'the ties (al-asbāb) between them will be cut' (2:166).

primaryMeaning: To drag along the ground. Saḥāb, 'clouds', are classically named for the way they drag across the sky.
extendedMeaning: The people of the Fire 'will be dragged (yusḥabūna) through boiling water' (40:71–72).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. 'The clouds (al-saḥāb) held between heaven and earth' are among His signs (2:164). 'He sends the winds … until they carry heavy clouds (saḥāban)' (7:57). The mountains 'pass as the clouds pass (marra al-saḥāb)' (27:88).

primaryMeaning: Lightness and lack of judgment — foolishness. Safah is folly; safīh is one who is foolish or cannot manage his affairs.
extendedMeaning: If the debtor is 'of limited understanding (safīhan)', his guardian dictates (2:282). 'Do not give the foolish (al-sufahā') your wealth' (4:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. The hypocrites said, 'Should we believe as the fools (al-sufahā') believe?' — 'it is they who are the fools' (2:13). 'Who turns away from the religion of Ibrahim except one who makes a fool of himself (safiha)?' (2:130). Hud's people said, 'We see you in foolishness (safāha)' (7:66).

primaryMeaning: Tender concern mixed with fear — caring about someone and fearing for them. Ishfāq is anxious care; shafaq is the reddish glow after sunset, soft and fading.
extendedMeaning: 'I swear by the twilight glow (bil-shafaq)' (84:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. The angels 'are fearful (mushfiqūn) out of awe of Him' (21:28). The criminals will be 'fearful (mushfiqīn) of what is in it' — their record (18:49). The heavens, earth and mountains 'feared (ashfaqna)' the trust (33:72).

primaryMeaning: A deafening blast that strikes someone down. Ṣāʿiqa is a thunderbolt; ṣaʿiqa is to be struck senseless or dead.
extendedMeaning: When the trumpet is blown, 'whoever is in the heavens and the earth will fall dead (ṣaʿiqa)' (39:68).
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times. The Israelites demanded to see Allah, 'so the thunderbolt (al-ṣāʿiqa) seized you while you looked on' (2:55). 'I warn you of a thunderbolt (ṣāʿiqatan) like that of ʿĀd and Thamud' (41:13). Musa 'fell down unconscious (ṣaʿiqan)' (7:143).

primaryMeaning: To stamp, to seal — as a seal is pressed into wax. Ṭabaʿa is to seal; ṭabʿ is a seal, and also one's nature, stamped in from creation.
quranUsage: Occurs 11 times, always for sealing hearts: 'Allah has set a seal (ṭabaʿa) on them because of their disbelief' (4:155). 'Thus Allah seals (yaṭbaʿu) the hearts of the disbelievers' (7:101). Their hearts 'were sealed (ṭubiʿa), so they do not understand' (9:87).

primaryMeaning: The edge or end of something — and the eyelid, the edge of the eye, and so a glance. Ṭarf is a blink or gaze; aṭrāf are extremities or borders.
