extendedMeaning: Yusuf said, 'Plant for seven years as usual (da'aban)' (12:47).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Like the way (ka-da'bi) of the people of Pharaoh and those before them' (3:11; 8:52). 'He subjected the sun and the moon, both constantly pursuing (dā'ibayn) their courses' (14:33).

primaryMeaning: To wear away something by repeated use — a trail effaced by feet. Darasa is to study, going over a text again and again; dirāsa is study.
extendedMeaning: 'Have you a book in which you study (tadrusūn)?' (68:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Be devoted to the Lord, because you teach the Book and because you study it (tadrusūn)' (3:79). They inherited the Book 'and studied (darasū) what was in it' (7:169). The deniers would say, 'You have studied (darasta)' — accusing the Prophet of copying (6:105).

primaryMeaning: To create and spread out, to multiply. Dhara'a is to bring into being and scatter across the earth.
extendedMeaning: 'What He produced (dhara'a) for you in the earth of varying colours' (16:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'It is He who multiplied you (dhara'akum) in the earth, and to Him you will be gathered' (23:79). 'He multiplies you (yadhra'ukum) thereby; there is nothing like Him' (42:11). 'We have created (dhara'nā) for Hell many of the jinn and mankind' (7:179).

primaryMeaning: To fall, to go down — and so to perish. Taraddā is to tumble to one's ruin; ardā is to destroy; mutaraddiya is an animal killed by a fall.
extendedMeaning: Forbidden is 'that which has a fatal fall (al-mutaraddiya)' (5:3). 'Let not one who does not believe in it avert you, lest you perish (fa-tardā)' (20:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'His wealth will not avail him when he falls (taraddā)' (92:11). The believer in Paradise will tell his old companion, 'You almost ruined me (la-turdīni)' (37:56). 'That assumption of yours … has ruined you (ardākum)' (41:23).

primaryMeaning: To watch and lie in wait. Raṣad is a watch or guard; marṣad and mirṣād are a place of lookout or ambush.
extendedMeaning: The jinn said, 'Whoever listens now will find a burning flame lying in wait (raṣadā)' (72:9). A mosque was taken 'as a station (irṣādan) for whoever had fought Allah' (9:107).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Sit in wait for them at every place of ambush (marṣadin)' (9:5). 'Your Lord is ever watchful (la-bil-mirṣād)' (89:14). 'Hell has been lying in wait (mirṣādā)' (78:21).

primaryMeaning: To drive away with a shout. Zajra is a single cry; izdujira is to be driven off; muzdajar is a deterrent.
extendedMeaning: 'By those who drive strongly (fal-zājirāti zajrā)' — the angels (37:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. The resurrection 'will be only a single cry (zajratun)' (37:19; 79:13). 'There has come to them of news that in which there is deterrence (muzdajarun)' (54:4). Nuh 'was called mad and was repelled (wa-zdujira)' (54:9).

primaryMeaning: To shake violently and repeatedly. Zalzala and zilzāl are a great convulsion; zulzila is to be shaken.
extendedMeaning: Those before 'were touched by poverty and hardship and were shaken (zulzilū)' (2:214).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'When the earth is shaken with its earthquake (zilzālahā)' (99:1). 'The convulsion (zalzala) of the Hour is a terrible thing' (22:1). The believers 'were shaken (zulzilū) with a severe shaking' — at the trench (33:11).

primaryMeaning: To turn aside, to incline away. Zūr, 'falsehood', is speech turned away from the truth; zāra, 'to visit', is to turn aside to someone; tazāwara is to incline away.
extendedMeaning: 'Until you visited (zurtum) the graves' (102:2). The sun 'inclined away (tazāwaru) from their cave' (18:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Avoid false speech (qawl al-zūr)' (22:30). The servants of the Most Merciful 'do not witness falsehood (al-zūr)' (25:72). The deniers said of the Quran, 'a lie and falsehood (zūran)' (25:4).

primaryMeaning: To block a gap, to close it off — and to be on target, straight and right. Sadd is a barrier; sadīd is right and sound.
extendedMeaning: Guardians of orphans should 'speak words of appropriate justice (sadīdā)' (4:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice (qawlan sadīdā)' (33:70). 'We have put before them a barrier (saddan) and behind them a barrier' (36:9). Dhu al-Qarnayn built 'a barrier (saddan)' between the two mountains (18:94).

primaryMeaning: To heal, to cure. Shifā' is healing — restoring health.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim said, 'When I am ill, it is He who cures me (yashfīni)' (26:80).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. The Quran is 'a healing (shifā'un) for what is in the breasts' (10:57), and 'We send down of the Quran what is healing and mercy for the believers' (17:82). Honey is 'a healing (shifā'un) for people' (16:69).

primaryMeaning: To bind tightly — and to persist, holding firmly to something. Aṣarra is to persist; ṣirr is bitter frost; ṣarra is a loud cry.
extendedMeaning: Spending of the deniers is like 'a wind in which is frost (ṣirrun)' (3:117). Sarah 'came forward with a cry (ṣarratin)' (51:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. The God-conscious 'do not persist (lam yuṣirrū) in what they did while they know' (3:135). The companions of the left 'persisted (yuṣirrūn) in the great sin' (56:46). Nuh's people 'persisted (aṣarrū) and were arrogant with great arrogance' (71:7).

primaryMeaning: To hunt — to catch wild game. Ṣayd is hunting or the game caught.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, all in the rulings of hunting for pilgrims: 'Do not kill game (al-ṣayd) while you are in iḥrām' (5:95). 'Lawful to you is the game of the sea (ṣaydu al-baḥr)' (5:96). 'When you have left iḥrām, then hunt (fa-ṣṭādū)' (5:2).

primaryMeaning: Light that shines out. Ḍaw' and ḍiyā' are light — a light that shines by itself; aḍā'a is to light up.
extendedMeaning: 'Which god other than Allah could bring you light (bi-ḍiyā')?' (28:71). The Torah was 'a criterion and a light (ḍiyā'an)' (21:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'It is He who made the sun a shining light (ḍiyā'an) and the moon a light (nūran)' (10:5). 'When it lit up (aḍā'at) what was around him' (2:17). 'Its oil would almost glow (yuḍī'u) even if no fire touched it' (24:35).

primaryMeaning: To turn aside to someone as a guest. Ḍayf is a guest; ḍayyafa is to offer hospitality.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Has the story of Ibrahim's honoured guests (ḍayf) reached you?' (51:24). Lut said, 'Do not disgrace me concerning my guests (ḍayfī)' (11:78). The people of the town 'refused to offer them hospitality (yuḍayyifūhumā)' — Musa and al-Khiḍr (18:77).

primaryMeaning: To be bound to something one cannot escape — a debt that clings. Maghram is a debt or loss; ghārim is one in debt; gharām is lasting and inseparable.
extendedMeaning: Farmers would say, 'We are laden with debt (la-mughramūn)' if the crop failed (56:66).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. Charity is for, among others, 'those in debt (al-ghārimīn)' (9:60). 'Do you ask them for payment, so they are burdened with debt (maghramin)?' (52:40). 'Its punishment is ever inseparable (gharāman)' — Hell (25:65).

primaryMeaning: To boast, to take pride in one's qualities over others. Fakhūr is a boaster; tafākhur is mutual boasting; fakhkhār is baked pottery.
extendedMeaning: 'He created man from clay like pottery (kal-fakhkhār)' (55:14).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Allah does not love every conceited, boastful one (fakhūr)' (31:18; 57:23). 'The life of this world is only play, amusement, adornment and boasting (tafākhur) among you' (57:20).

primaryMeaning: To spread out flat. Firāsh is a bed or resting place; furush are couches; farāsh are moths, which spread out in swarms; farsh are small animals low to the ground.
extendedMeaning: 'Reclining on couches (furush) lined with brocade' (55:54). Livestock 'for carrying and for meat (farshan)' (6:142).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Who made for you the earth a resting place (firāshan)' (2:22). 'The earth We spread out (farashnāhā), and how excellent are the spreaders' (51:48). People will be 'like scattered moths (kal-farāsh)' (101:4).

primaryMeaning: To be empty, free of something — and to pour out until empty. Faragha is to finish; afragha is to pour; fārigh is empty.
extendedMeaning: 'We will attend (sa-nafrughu) to you, O two weighty ones' (55:31). Dhu al-Qarnayn said, 'Bring me molten copper that I may pour (ufrigh) over it' (18:96).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Our Lord, pour upon us (afrigh) patience' (2:250; 7:126). 'When you have finished (faraghta), then stand up for worship' (94:7). 'The heart of Musa's mother became empty (fārighan)' (28:10).

primaryMeaning: Sudden fright that makes one start. Fazaʿ is terror; faziʿa is to be terrified.
extendedMeaning: When the two disputants came to Dawud, 'he was alarmed (fa-faziʿa) by them' (38:22). 'When fear is removed (fuzziʿa) from their hearts' (34:23).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'The Day the trumpet is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and the earth will be terrified (fa-faziʿa)' (27:87). 'The greatest terror (al-fazaʿ al-akbar) will not grieve them' (21:103). The righteous 'will be safe from the terror (fazaʿin) of that Day' (27:89).

primaryMeaning: To head straight for something — the direct, balanced way. Qaṣd is the straight path; iqtaṣada is to be moderate, keeping to the middle.
extendedMeaning: Among the believers 'some are moderate (muqtaṣidun)' (35:32). 'Had it been a near gain and a moderate (qāṣidan) journey, they would have followed you' (9:42).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Upon Allah is the direction (qaṣdu) of the way' (16:9). Luqman said, 'Be moderate (iqṣid) in your walking' (31:19). Among the People of the Book 'is a moderate (muqtaṣida) community' (5:66).

primaryMeaning: A shirt — a garment worn on the body.
extendedMeaning: Yusuf said, 'Take this shirt of mine (bi-qamīṣī) and cast it over my father's face; he will regain his sight' (12:93).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, all in the story of Yusuf. His brothers brought 'his shirt (qamīṣihi) with false blood' (12:18). The wife of al-ʿAzīz 'tore his shirt (qamīṣahu) from behind' (12:25), and 'if his shirt is torn from behind, she has lied' (12:27).

primaryMeaning: To lose all hope — the deepest despair. Qunūṭ is despair; qāniṭ is one who has given up hope.
extendedMeaning: 'When evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing (qanūṭ)' (41:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Do not despair (lā taqnaṭū) of the mercy of Allah; Allah forgives all sins' (39:53). Ibrahim said, 'Who despairs (yaqnaṭu) of the mercy of his Lord except those astray?' (15:56). 'It is He who sends down rain after they had despaired (qanaṭū)' (42:28).

primaryMeaning: A cup — especially one full of drink. Ka's is a cup or its contents.
extendedMeaning: 'And a full cup (ka'san dihāqā)' (78:34).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, all for the cups of Paradise: 'a cup (ka'sin) whose mixture is camphor' (76:5), 'a cup from a flowing spring' (37:45). 'They will exchange a cup (ka'san) in which there is no idle talk or sin' (52:23).

primaryMeaning: To return, to turn back again — as a horseman wheels round to charge again. Karra is a return; karratayn is 'twice more'.
extendedMeaning: 'Then return your sight twice again (karratayn)' (67:4). 'That would then be a losing return (karratun)' (79:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, mostly in the wish for a return to this world: 'If only we had a return (karratan), we would disown them' (2:167), and 'if I had another turn (karratan), I would be of the good-doers' (39:58).

primaryMeaning: To hold something in and close it off — as a waterskin is tied shut. Kaẓm is restraining anger or grief; kaẓīm is one who suppresses sorrow.
extendedMeaning: Yunus 'called out while he was distressed (makẓūm)' (68:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. The God-conscious are 'those who restrain (al-kāẓimīn) anger and pardon people' (3:134). Yaʿqub, grieving for Yusuf, 'was suppressing (kaẓīm) his grief' (12:84). When told of a daughter, 'his face becomes dark, and he suppresses (kaẓīm) grief' (16:58).

primaryMeaning: A dog. Kalb is a dog; mukallib is one who trains hunting animals.
extendedMeaning: The one who followed his desire 'is like the dog (al-kalb): if you chase it, it pants; if you leave it, it pants' (7:176).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. The dog of the people of the Cave was 'stretching its forelegs at the entrance' (18:18), and people disputed the number, 'the fourth of them their dog (kalbuhum)' (18:22). Game caught by 'trained animals (mukallibīn)' is lawful (5:4).

primaryMeaning: A cave — a large hollow in a mountain.
extendedMeaning: Surah 18 is named Al-Kahf, 'the Cave'.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, all for the cave of the sleepers in Surah 18: 'Do you think the companions of the Cave (al-kahf) and the inscription were a wonder among Our signs?' (18:9). 'They stayed in their cave (kahfihim) three hundred years' (18:25).

primaryMeaning: Pearls. Lu'lu' is a pearl.
extendedMeaning: 'When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls (lu'lu'an manthūrā)' (76:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, all for Paradise and the sea. The people of Paradise wear 'bracelets of gold and pearls (lu'lu'an)' (22:23). Youths serving them are 'like pearls well protected (lu'lu'un maknūn)' (52:24). 'From both of them come forth pearls (al-lu'lu') and coral' (55:22).

primaryMeaning: To turn aside from the straight line. Laḥd is the niche cut into the side of a grave; alḥada is to deviate — from the truth, or in Allah's names; multaḥad is a place to turn aside to, a refuge.
extendedMeaning: 'You will never find besides Him a refuge (multaḥadan)' (18:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Leave those who deviate (yulḥidūna) concerning His names' (7:180). 'The tongue of the one they point to (yulḥidūna ilayhi) is foreign' — answering the claim that a man taught the Prophet (16:103). 'Those who deviate (yulḥidūna) in Our verses are not hidden from Us' (41:40).

primaryMeaning: To catch up with someone, to join them. Laḥiqa is to reach; alḥaqa is to join one to another.
extendedMeaning: The martyrs rejoice over 'those who have not yet joined them (lam yalḥaqū)' (3:170).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. Yusuf prayed, 'Cause me to die a Muslim and join me (alḥiqnī) with the righteous' (12:101). 'Those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join (alḥaqnā) with them their descendants' (52:21).

primaryMeaning: A flat board or tablet. Lawḥ is a tablet; alwāḥ are tablets or planks; lawwāḥa is one that scorches the skin, changing its colour.
extendedMeaning: Nuh's ship was 'made of planks (alwāḥin) and nails' (54:13). Saqar is 'scorching (lawwāḥatun) the skin' (74:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'We wrote for him on the tablets (al-alwāḥ) of everything an instruction' — Musa (7:145), and he 'threw down the tablets' in anger (7:150). The Quran is 'in a preserved Tablet (lawḥin maḥfūẓ)' (85:22).

primaryMeaning: To let something loose to move freely — as animals are let out to pasture — and so to mix. Maraja is to release; mārij is a flame that flickers freely; marīj is confused; marjān is coral.
extendedMeaning: The deniers 'are in a confused (marīj) state' (50:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'He released (maraja) the two seas meeting side by side' (55:19; 25:53). The jinn were created 'from a smokeless flame of fire (mārijin min nār)' (55:15). 'From both of them come forth pearls and coral (al-marjān)' (55:22).

primaryMeaning: The strongest dislike — hatred directed at something shameful. Maqt is intense loathing.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Great is hatred (maqtan) with Allah that you say what you do not do' (61:3). The deniers will be told, 'Allah's hatred (la-maqtu) was greater than your hatred of yourselves' (40:10). Marrying fathers' former wives 'was an immorality and hateful (maqtan)' (4:22).

primaryMeaning: To act slowly, without hurry — to give time. Mahhala and amhala are to grant respite; muhl is molten metal or dregs of oil, flowing slowly.
extendedMeaning: The tree of Zaqqum is 'like murky oil (kal-muhl), boiling in the bellies' (44:45). 'The Day the sky will be like molten brass (kal-muhl)' (70:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'Give respite (fa-mahhil) to the disbelievers; leave them awhile (amhilhum)' (86:17). 'Leave Me with the deniers … and give them a little respite (mahhilhum)' (73:11). The drink of the Fire is 'like molten brass (kal-muhl) that scalds the faces' (18:29).

primaryMeaning: To lean, to incline to one side. Māla is to incline; mayl is inclination — or a sudden swerve to attack.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, all in Surah 4. 'Those who follow desires want you to deviate (tamīlū) greatly' (4:27). With more than one wife, 'do not incline (tamīlū) completely' (4:129). The disbelievers wish you would neglect your arms 'so they could come down on you in a single assault (maylatan)' (4:102).

primaryMeaning: A peer set up as an equal — one who stands against another as a match. Nidd is a rival; andād are rivals claimed as equals to Allah.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times, always as andād. 'Do not set up rivals (andādan) to Allah while you know' (2:22). 'Among people are those who take besides Allah rivals (andādan), loving them as they should love Allah' (2:165).

primaryMeaning: To prod and stir up — to provoke discord between people. Nazgh is an evil prompting; nazagha is to sow dissension.
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. 'If an evil suggestion (nazghun) comes to you from Satan, seek refuge in Allah' (7:200; 41:36). 'Satan sows discord (yanzaghu) among them' (17:53). Yusuf said, 'after Satan had caused discord (nazagha) between me and my brothers' (12:100).

primaryMeaning: To tread, to step firmly on the ground. Waṭi'a is to set foot on; mawṭi' is a place stepped on; wāṭa'a is to match or adjust.
extendedMeaning: The deniers adjusted the sacred months 'to adjust (li-yuwāṭi'ū) the number' (9:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 6 times. The believers do not 'take a step (mawṭi'an) that enrages the disbelievers' without its being recorded (9:120). 'He caused you to inherit … a land you had not trodden (taṭa'ūhā)' (33:27). 'Rising at night is more effective (ashaddu waṭ'an)' (73:6).

primaryMeaning: Arā'ik are couches — raised seats furnished with cushions under a canopy.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, all for the couches of Paradise: 'reclining therein on adorned couches (al-arā'ik)' (18:31), and 'on adorned couches, observing' (83:23).

primaryMeaning: Grief mixed with anger — deep sorrow at a loss. Asaf is grief; āsafa is to provoke to anger.
extendedMeaning: 'When they angered Us (āsafūnā), We took retribution from them' (43:55).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Yaʿqub said, 'Oh, my grief (yā asafā) over Yusuf!' (12:84). Musa returned to his people 'angry and grieved (asifan)' (7:150; 20:86). 'Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief (asafan) over them' (18:6).

primaryMeaning: Coolness — the opposite of heat. Bard is coolness; bārid is cool; barad is hail.
extendedMeaning: 'He sends down from the sky mountains of hail (baradin)' (24:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We said, O fire, be coolness (bardan) and safety upon Ibrahim' (21:69). The people of the Fire 'will not taste therein any coolness (bardan) or drink' (78:24). Ayyub was told, 'This is a cool (bāridun) bath and drink' (38:42).

primaryMeaning: Hatred — the opposite of love. Baghḍā' is intense hatred.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim told his people, 'there has appeared between us enmity and hatred forever' (60:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We caused among them enmity and hatred (al-baghḍā') until the Day of Resurrection' (5:14; 5:64). 'Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred between you through wine and gambling' (5:91). 'Hatred (al-baghḍā') has appeared from their mouths' (3:118).

primaryMeaning: To be struck silent by despair — confounded and hopeless, with no argument left. Ablasa is to despair; mublis is one left speechless in hopelessness.
extendedMeaning: Many scholars link Iblīs to this root — the one who despaired of Allah's mercy.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We seized them suddenly, and they were in despair (mublisūn)' (6:44). 'The Day the Hour comes, the criminals will be in despair (yublisu)' (30:12). The punishment 'will not be lightened for them, and they will be in despair therein' (43:75).

primaryMeaning: To be ruined and perish — land left barren and uncultivated. Būr are a ruined people; bawār is destruction; bāra is to come to nothing.
extendedMeaning: Believers 'hope for a trade that will never perish (lan tabūra)' (35:29).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'They were a people ruined (būran)' (25:18). Those who exchanged Allah's favour for disbelief 'led their people into the home of destruction (al-bawār)' (14:28). 'The plotting of those will perish (yabūru)' (35:10).

primaryMeaning: Ruin and destruction — to be doomed, cut off from all good. Thubūr is perdition; mathbūr is one destroyed.
extendedMeaning: 'He will call for destruction (thubūrā)' — the one given his record behind his back (84:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. In the Fire, 'they will call out for destruction (thubūran)' (25:13), and be told, 'Do not call today for one destruction, but call for many' (25:14). Musa told Pharaoh, 'I think you, O Pharaoh, are destroyed (mathbūrā)' (17:102).

primaryMeaning: To rise and stir up — to set something in motion. Athāra is to raise dust, stir clouds, or turn up soil.
extendedMeaning: Earlier peoples 'ploughed (athārū) the earth and built it up more than these have' (30:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Allah sends the winds, so they stir up (fa-tuthīru) clouds' (30:48; 35:9). The cow was 'not trained to plough (tuthīru) the earth' (2:71). The chargers 'stir up (fa-atharna) dust' (100:4).

primaryMeaning: To fall and lie flat on the ground, as a bird or animal crouches down. Jāthim is one fallen prone, lifeless.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, always as jāthimīn, for destroyed peoples: 'the earthquake seized them, and they became in their home fallen prone (jāthimīn)' — Thamud (7:78), and the people of Shuʿayb (7:91).

primaryMeaning: To become clear and exposed — to come out into the open. Tajallā is to appear; jallā is to reveal; jalā' is exile, being driven out into the open.
extendedMeaning: 'Had Allah not decreed exile (al-jalā') for them' (59:3). 'By the day when it appears (tajallā)' (92:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'When his Lord appeared (tajallā) to the mountain, He made it crumble' (7:143). 'None will reveal it (yujallīhā) at its time except He' — the Hour (7:187). 'By the day when it displays it (jallāhā)' (91:3).

primaryMeaning: To pass through and beyond something. Jāwaza is to cross; tajāwaza is to pass over — to overlook.
extendedMeaning: 'When they had passed beyond (jāwazā)' — Musa and his servant (18:62).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We took the Children of Israel across (jāwaznā) the sea' (7:138; 10:90). Talut 'crossed it (jāwazahu)' — the river (2:249). 'We will overlook (natajāwazu) their misdeeds' (46:16).

primaryMeaning: Hunger — an empty belly.
extendedMeaning: Adam was told, 'You will not be hungry (tajūʿa) in it, nor naked' (20:118). The food of the Fire 'neither nourishes nor avails against hunger (jūʿin)' (88:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We will test you with something of fear and hunger (al-jūʿ)' (2:155). Allah 'fed them against hunger (jūʿin)' — Quraysh (106:4). A town that denied Allah's blessings was made to taste 'the garment of hunger (al-jūʿ) and fear' (16:112).

primaryMeaning: Eager, intense desire to get something or keep it. Ḥirṣ is avid longing; ḥarīṣ is one deeply concerned for something.
extendedMeaning: 'You will never be able to be just between wives, even if you desire it (ḥaraṣtum)' (4:129).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The Prophet is 'deeply concerned (ḥarīṣun) for you' (9:128). 'Most of the people will not believe, however much you desire it (ḥaraṣta)' (12:103). Some are 'the most greedy (aḥraṣa) of people for life' (2:96).

primaryMeaning: Envy — resenting another's blessing and wishing it removed. Ḥasad is envy; ḥāsid is an envier.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'From the evil of an envier (ḥāsidin) when he envies (ḥasada)' (113:5). Many of the People of the Book wish to turn you back 'out of envy (ḥasadan) from themselves' (2:109). 'Or do they envy (yaḥsudūna) people for what Allah has given them?' (4:54).

primaryMeaning: Pebbles, small stones — and anything thrown into a fire as fuel. Ḥāṣib is a storm of stones; ḥaṣab is fuel.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Do you feel secure that He will not send against you a storm of stones (ḥāṣiban)?' (17:68). 'Among them were those on whom We sent a storm of stones (ḥāṣiban)' (29:40). 'You and what you worship besides Allah are the firewood (ḥaṣab) of Hell' (21:98).

primaryMeaning: A fish — including a very large one. Ḥūt is a fish; ḥītān are fish.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not be like the companion of the fish (al-ḥūt)' — Yunus (68:48).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'The fish (al-ḥūt) swallowed him while he was blameworthy' — Yunus (37:142). Musa and his servant 'forgot their fish (ḥūtahumā)' (18:61). 'Their fish (ḥītānuhum) came to them on the day of their Sabbath' (7:163).

primaryMeaning: To turn aside and flee from something. Maḥīṣ is a place of escape.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, always 'no escape (maḥīṣ)': 'Whether we are impatient or patient, there is for us no escape (maḥīṣin)' (14:21). 'Their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape (maḥīṣan) from it' (4:121).

primaryMeaning: To deceive — to conceal one's real intent in order to mislead. Khadaʿa is to trick; khādaʿa is to try to deceive.
extendedMeaning: 'If they intend to deceive you (yakhdaʿūka), Allah is sufficient for you' (8:62).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'They seek to deceive (yukhādiʿūna) Allah and those who believe, but they deceive only themselves' (2:9). 'The hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them (khādiʿuhum)' — repaying their deceit (4:142).

primaryMeaning: To estimate by guessing — as one guesses the yield of dates on a palm. Kharaṣa is to conjecture; kharrāṣ is a liar who speaks from guesswork.
extendedMeaning: 'They have no knowledge of that; they only guess (yakhruṣūn)' (43:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'They follow only assumption, and they only guess (yakhruṣūn)' (6:116; 10:66). 'Cursed are the liars (al-kharrāṣūn)' (51:10).

primaryMeaning: A step — the distance between the feet in walking. Khuṭuwāt are footsteps.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, always in 'the footsteps of Satan (khuṭuwāt al-shayṭān)': 'do not follow the footsteps of Satan; he is to you a clear enemy' (2:168; 2:208). 'Whoever follows the footsteps of Satan — he commands immorality and wrongdoing' (24:21).

primaryMeaning: Khinzīr is the pig, swine.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, mostly in the list of forbidden foods: 'He has forbidden you carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine (al-khinzīr)' (2:173; 5:3; 16:115). Some were made 'apes and swine (al-khanāzīr)' (5:60).

primaryMeaning: To be empty and to fall in — a house that collapses because nothing is left inside it. Khāwiya is fallen in, empty, ruined.
extendedMeaning: The garden owner found his garden 'fallen down on its trellises (khāwiyatun)' (18:42).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, for ruined places: 'a town fallen down on its roofs (khāwiyatun ʿalā ʿurūshihā)' (2:259; 22:45). 'Those are their houses, fallen in ruin (khāwiyatan)' (27:52). ʿĀd lay 'like trunks of hollow (khāwiya) palm trees' (69:7).

primaryMeaning: To fail to get what one hoped for — disappointment. Khāba is to fail; khā'ib is disappointed.
extendedMeaning: 'He has failed (khāba) who carries wrongdoing' (20:111).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'He has failed (khāba) who corrupts it' — the soul (91:10). 'Whoever invents a lie has failed' (20:61). 'Every stubborn tyrant was disappointed (khāba)' (14:15).

primaryMeaning: To push away, to ward off. Dara'a is to repel; iddāra'a is to push the blame onto one another — to dispute.
extendedMeaning: The wife's testimony 'averts (yadra'u) the punishment from her' (24:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The righteous 'repel (yadra'ūna) evil with good' (13:22; 28:54). The Israelites 'disputed (fa-ddāra'tum) over it' — the slain man (2:72). 'Then avert (fa-dra'ū) death from yourselves' (3:168).

primaryMeaning: Oil, grease — and from its smoothness, being soft and compromising. Duhn is oil; dihān is murky oil; adhana is to go soft on one's principles.
extendedMeaning: 'When the sky is split and becomes rose-red, like murky oil (kal-dihān)' (55:37).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'They wish that you would compromise (tudhinu), so they would compromise' (68:9). 'Is it this statement that you take lightly (mudhinūn)?' (56:81). 'A tree that grows from Mount Sinai, producing oil (bil-duhn)' (23:20).

primaryMeaning: The arm from elbow to fingertip — and a measure of that length. Dhirāʿ is a forearm or cubit; ḍāqa dharʿan is to be at a loss, one's reach too short.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Their dog was 'stretching its forelegs (dhirāʿayhi) at the entrance' (18:18). 'Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits (dhirāʿan), insert him' (69:32). When the angels came, Lut 'felt straitened (ḍāqa bihim dharʿan)' for them (11:77).

primaryMeaning: To blame, to find fault. Dhamma is to censure; madhmūm is blameworthy. Dhimma is a covenant or pledge — the protection owed, whose breaking brings blame.
extendedMeaning: Yunus 'would have been thrown onto the barren shore while he was blamed (madhmūm)' (68:49).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Whoever wants only this world 'will burn in Hell, disgraced (madhmūman)' (17:18). 'Do not set up another god with Allah, lest you sit disgraced (madhmūman)' (17:22). The deniers 'do not observe towards a believer any tie or covenant (dhimmatan)' (9:10).

primaryMeaning: To tie, to fasten firmly. Rabaṭa is to bind; ribāṭ is tethering horses ready for defence; rābaṭa is to stay steadfast at one's post.
extendedMeaning: Musa's mother would have revealed him 'had We not strengthened (rabaṭnā) her heart' (28:10). Rain was sent 'to strengthen (li-yarbiṭa) your hearts' (8:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Be patient, outlast in patience, and be steadfast (rābiṭū)' (3:200). 'We made firm (rabaṭnā) their hearts' — the youths of the Cave (18:14). 'Prepare against them … tethered (ribāṭ) horses' (8:60).

primaryMeaning: Terror — a fear that fills the heart. Ruʿb is dread.
extendedMeaning: 'If you had looked at them, you would have been filled with terror (ruʿban)' — the youths of the Cave (18:18).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, mostly for terror cast into the enemy's hearts: 'We will cast terror (al-ruʿb) into the hearts of those who disbelieve' (3:151), and 'I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved' (8:12).

primaryMeaning: Gentleness and ease — and the elbow, on which one leans. Rifq is kindness; rafīq is a companion who is gentle with you; mirfaq is an elbow, or what makes things easy; murtafaq is a place to rest.
extendedMeaning: Hell is 'an evil resting place (murtafaqan)', and Paradise 'an excellent resting place' (18:29, 18:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Excellent are they as companions (rafīqan)' — the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous (4:69). The youths hoped 'your Lord will prepare for you ease (mirfaqan) in your affair' (18:16). In ablution, 'wash your hands up to the elbows (al-marāfiq)' (5:6).

primaryMeaning: To go out and vanish — as a soul leaves the body. Zahaqa is to perish; zahūq is bound to vanish.
extendedMeaning: Allah intends 'that their souls should depart (tazhaqa) while they are disbelievers' (9:55).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished (zahaqa); falsehood is ever bound to vanish (zahūqan)' (17:81). 'We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and it vanishes (zāhiqun)' (21:18).

primaryMeaning: A branch from one root — a line of descent. Asbāṭ are the tribes descended from Yaʿqub's sons.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We believe in Allah … and what was revealed to Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaʿqub and the tribes (al-asbāṭ)' (2:136; 3:84). 'We divided them into twelve tribes (asbāṭan)' (7:160).

primaryMeaning: Six. Sudus is a sixth; sādis is sixth.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. In inheritance, 'each parent has a sixth (al-sudus)' (4:11). The people of the Cave: 'five, the sixth of them (sādisuhum) their dog' (18:22). 'No five confer but He is the sixth (sādisuhum)' (58:7).

primaryMeaning: An ear of grain — the spike that holds the seeds. Sunbula is an ear; sanābil are ears.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Spending in Allah's way is 'like a grain that grows seven ears (sanābila), in each ear (sunbulatin) a hundred grains' (2:261). The king saw 'seven green ears (sunbulātin) and others dry' (12:43), and Yusuf said, 'leave it in its ears (sunbulihi)' (12:47).

primaryMeaning: To be scattered and separated. Shattā is various, diverse; ashtāt are separate groups.
extendedMeaning: 'We brought forth pairs of various (shattā) plants' (20:53). 'No blame on you to eat together or separately (ashtātan)' (24:61).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Your striving is surely diverse (la-shattā)' (92:4). 'That Day people will come out in scattered groups (ashtātan) to be shown their deeds' (99:6). 'You think them united, but their hearts are divided (shattā)' (59:14).

primaryMeaning: Greed together with stinginess — tightly holding what one has while craving more. Shuḥḥ is avarice; ashiḥḥa are the miserly.
extendedMeaning: The hypocrites were 'miserly (ashiḥḥatan) towards you' (33:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Whoever is protected from the stinginess (shuḥḥa) of his soul — they are the successful' (59:9; 64:16). 'Souls are prone to greed (al-shuḥḥ)' (4:128).

primaryMeaning: To open up and lay out — to widen. Sharaḥa al-ṣadr is to open someone's breast — to make it at ease and receptive.
extendedMeaning: 'Is one whose breast Allah has opened (sharaḥa) to Islam, so he is upon a light from his Lord …?' (39:22). But 'whoever opens (sharaḥa) his breast to disbelief' faces wrath (16:106).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Whoever Allah wants to guide, He opens (yashraḥ) his breast to Islam' (6:125). Musa prayed, 'My Lord, expand (ishraḥ) for me my breast' (20:25). 'Did We not expand (nashraḥ) for you your breast?' (94:1).

primaryMeaning: A way down to water — a path that leads straight to the source. Sharīʿa is a clear way laid down; shirʿa is a law; sharaʿa is to ordain.
extendedMeaning: 'Do they have partners who have ordained (sharaʿū) for them of religion what Allah did not permit?' (42:21). Fish came 'visibly (shurraʿan)' on the Sabbath (7:163).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'He has ordained (sharaʿa) for you of religion what He enjoined on Nuh' (42:13). 'For each of you We prescribed a law (shirʿatan) and a way' (5:48). 'We put you on an ordained way (sharīʿatin) of the matter, so follow it' (45:18).

primaryMeaning: Half of something — and the direction or side one faces. Shaṭr is a direction.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, all in the verses changing the direction of prayer: 'Turn your face towards (shaṭra) the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces towards it (shaṭrahu)' (2:144; 2:150).

primaryMeaning: A flame, a blazing light — and bright white, like fire against the night. Shihāb is a flaming torch or shooting star; shuhub are flames.
extendedMeaning: Musa told his family, 'I will bring you a burning torch (bi-shihābin)' (27:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, mostly for flames that strike the devils who eavesdrop: 'he is pursued by a clear burning flame (shihābun mubīn)' (15:18; 37:10). The jinn said, 'We found the sky filled with strong guards and flames (shuhuban)' (72:8).

primaryMeaning: To pour down. Ṣabba is to pour; ṣabb is pouring abundantly.
extendedMeaning: 'Boiling water will be poured (yuṣabbu) over their heads' (22:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We poured down (ṣababnā) water in abundance (ṣabban)' (80:25). 'Pour (ṣubbū) over his head the punishment of boiling water' (44:48). 'Your Lord poured (fa-ṣabba) on them a scourge of punishment' (89:13).

primaryMeaning: To split something open, to crack it. Ṣadaʿa is to split, and to proclaim openly — splitting the silence; taṣaddaʿa is to split apart; ṣudāʿ is a headache that splits the head.
extendedMeaning: The drink of Paradise gives 'no headache (lā yuṣaddaʿūn)' (56:19). 'That Day they will be divided (yaṣṣaddaʿūn)' (30:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Proclaim openly (fa-ṣdaʿ) what you are commanded' (15:94). 'Had We sent down this Quran on a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, splitting apart (mutaṣaddiʿan)' (59:21). 'By the earth which cracks open (dhāt al-ṣadʿ)' (86:12).

primaryMeaning: To turn aside, to veer away from something. Ṣadafa is to turn away; ṣadafān are two facing cliffs, each turning towards the other.
extendedMeaning: Dhu al-Qarnayn filled the gap 'between the two cliffs (al-ṣadafayn)' (18:96).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'See how We vary the signs, then they turn away (yaṣdifūn)' (6:46). 'Who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah and turns away (ṣadafa) from them?' (6:157).

primaryMeaning: To cry out loudly — for help or in distress. Ṣarīkh is a cry, or one who answers it; istaṣrakha is to call for help; muṣrikh is a helper.
extendedMeaning: 'If We will, We drown them, and there is no responder to their cry (ṣarīkha)' (36:43).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'They will cry out (yaṣṭarikhūn) therein: Our Lord, remove us' (35:37). Satan will say, 'I cannot be your helper (bi-muṣrikhikum), nor can you be mine' (14:22). The man from Musa's people 'cried out to him for help (yastaṣrikhuhu)' (28:18).

primaryMeaning: Yellow. Aṣfar is yellow; ṣafrā' is bright yellow; iṣfarra is to turn yellow, as plants do when they dry.
extendedMeaning: Sparks of Hell are 'as if they were yellow (ṣufrun) camels' (77:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'A yellow (ṣafrā') cow, bright in colour' (2:69). Crops 'grow dry and you see them turn yellow (muṣfarran), then they become debris' (39:21; 57:20).

primaryMeaning: An idol — a carved image worshipped besides Allah. Ṣanam is an idol; aṣnām are idols.
extendedMeaning: The Israelites passed 'a people devoted to their idols (aṣnāmin)' and asked for a god like them (7:138).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Ibrahim asked his father, 'Do you take idols (aṣnāman) as gods?' (6:74), and prayed, 'Keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols (al-aṣnām)' (14:35). 'By Allah, I will plan against your idols (aṣnāmakum)' (21:57).

primaryMeaning: To drive away, to chase off. Ṭarada is to expel; ṭārid is one who drives away.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Do not drive away (lā taṭrudi) those who call on their Lord morning and evening' (6:52). Nuh said, 'I am not going to drive away (bi-ṭāridi) those who believe' (11:29), and 'who would help me against Allah if I drove them away (ṭaradtuhum)?' (11:30).

primaryMeaning: To wipe out and efface — so that no trace or mark remains. Ṭamasa is to obliterate or blind.
extendedMeaning: 'We blinded (fa-ṭamasnā) their eyes' — the people of Lut (54:37). 'If We willed, We could have obliterated (la-ṭamasnā) their eyes' (36:66).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'When the stars are obliterated (ṭumisat)' (77:8). 'Believe … before We efface (naṭmisa) faces' (4:47). Musa prayed, 'Our Lord, obliterate (iṭmis) their wealth' (10:88).

primaryMeaning: To fold up, to roll something together. Ṭawā is to fold; maṭwiyy is folded up. Ṭuwā is the name of the sacred valley.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'The Day We will fold up (naṭwī) the heaven like the folding (ka-ṭayyi) of a scroll for records' (21:104). 'The heavens will be folded (maṭwiyyātun) in His right hand' (39:67). 'You are in the sacred valley, Ṭuwā (ṭuwan)' (20:12).

primaryMeaning: The step of a doorway — and reproach, going back over what was done. Istaʿtaba is to seek to make amends, to ask to be restored to favour.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, always for the deniers who will not be allowed to make amends: 'they will not be asked to make amends (yustaʿtabūn)' (16:84; 30:57; 45:35). 'If they ask for favour (yastaʿtibū), they will not be of those favoured' (41:24).

primaryMeaning: To spread corruption — to go about causing disorder. ʿAthā is to act wickedly.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, always in 'do not act wickedly (lā taʿthaw) in the land, spreading corruption' (2:60). It is said to the Israelites, to ʿĀd, to Thamud and to Madyan (7:74; 11:85; 26:183; 29:36).

primaryMeaning: To bind tightly around something. ʿUṣba is a band of people bound together; ʿaṣīb is a day that grips with distress.
extendedMeaning: Qarun's keys would burden 'a company (bil-ʿuṣba) of strong men' (28:76).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Yusuf's brothers said, 'we are a band (ʿuṣba)' (12:8; 12:14). 'Those who brought the slander are a group (ʿuṣbatun) among you' (24:11). Lut said, 'This is a distressful (ʿaṣībun) day' (11:77).

primaryMeaning: To press and squeeze out. ʿAṣara is to press grapes or olives; muʿṣirāt are rain clouds pressing out rain; ʿaṣr is time pressing on — and the late afternoon.
extendedMeaning: A garden struck by 'a whirlwind (iʿṣārun) with fire' (2:266).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'By time (wal-ʿaṣr), man is in loss' (103:1–2). Yusuf's companion said, 'I saw myself pressing (aʿṣiru) wine' (12:36), and a year will come 'in which they will press (yaʿṣirūn)' (12:49). 'We sent down from the rain clouds (al-muʿṣirāt) pouring water' (78:14).

primaryMeaning: To cover widely and include. ʿAmm is a paternal uncle and ʿamma a paternal aunt — relatives who belong to the whole family line.
extendedMeaning: The Prophet may marry 'the daughters of your paternal uncles (ʿammika)' (33:50).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, in rulings on family: 'your fathers' sisters (ʿammātukum)' are forbidden in marriage (4:23). There is no blame in eating 'in the houses of your paternal uncles (aʿmāmikum) or paternal aunts' (24:61).

primaryMeaning: Hardship that breaks someone down — distress and difficulty. ʿAnat is suffering, and falling into sin under pressure; aʿnata is to put in hardship.
extendedMeaning: Marriage to slave women is for 'whoever fears falling into sin (al-ʿanat)' (4:25). 'If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty (la-ʿanittum)' (49:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The Prophet is grieved by 'what you suffer (ʿanittum)' (9:128). The hypocrites 'love what distresses you (ʿanittum)' (3:118). 'If Allah had willed, He could have put you in difficulty (la-aʿnatakum)' (2:220).

primaryMeaning: To cry out for help, and to bring relief. Istaghātha is to call for help; aghātha is to rescue; ghayth is rain that brings relief.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'When you sought help (tastaghīthūna) from your Lord, He answered you' — at Badr (8:9). 'If they call for relief (yastaghīthū), they will be relieved (yughāthū) with water like molten brass' (18:29). The man 'called him for help (fa-staghāthahu)' against his enemy — Musa (28:15).

primaryMeaning: Single, alone — one without a partner. Fard is alone; furādā are individuals, each by himself.
extendedMeaning: 'Stand for Allah in pairs and individually (furādā)' (34:46).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone (fardā)' (19:95). 'You have come to Us alone (furādā), as We created you the first time' (6:94). Zakariyya prayed, 'My Lord, do not leave me alone (fardan)' (21:89).

primaryMeaning: To pass by and slip away — to be missed. Fāta is to escape; fawt is escape; tafāwut is discrepancy, one part passing out of step with another.
extendedMeaning: 'If you could see when they are terrified, but there is no escape (fawta)' (34:51).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'So that you not grieve over what escaped you (fātakum)' (57:23; 3:153). 'You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any discrepancy (tafāwutin)' (67:3).

primaryMeaning: A group moving together, a troop. Fawj is a company; afwāj are crowds.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'You see the people entering the religion of Allah in crowds (afwājan)' (110:2). 'The Day the trumpet is blown and you will come forth in crowds (afwājan)' (78:18). 'Every time a group (fawjun) is thrown into it, its keepers ask them' (67:8).

primaryMeaning: To be tight and sparing — and dust or darkness. Qatara is to be stingy; qatūr is miserly; muqtir is one of narrow means; qatar is dust, and qatara darkness.
extendedMeaning: 'No darkness (qatarun) will cover their faces' — the people of Paradise (10:26), while the deniers' faces are 'covered by darkness (qatara)' (80:41).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The servants of the Most Merciful 'when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy (yaqturū)' (25:67). 'Man is ever stingy (qatūrā)' (17:100). A divorced woman's gift is 'on the poor (al-muqtir) according to his means' (2:236).

primaryMeaning: To cut lengthwise, to tear straight along. Qadda is to rip; qidad are divisions — groups going separate ways.
extendedMeaning: The jinn said, 'We were of different ways (ṭarā'iqa qidadā)' (72:11).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times, mostly for Yusuf's shirt: 'she tore (qaddat) his shirt from behind' (12:25), and 'if his shirt is torn (qudda) from behind, she has lied' (12:27).

primaryMeaning: To knock, to strike hard. Al-qāriʿa, 'the Striking Calamity', is a name of the Day of Judgment, which strikes hearts with terror.
extendedMeaning: Surah 101 is Al-Qāriʿa.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'The Striking Calamity (al-qāriʿa)! What is the Striking Calamity?' (101:1–2). Thamud and ʿĀd 'denied the Striking Calamity' (69:4). 'A disaster (qāriʿatun) will continue to strike the disbelievers' (13:31).

primaryMeaning: To peel off the bark of a tree — and so to acquire, to take something for oneself, usually wrongdoing. Iqtarafa is to commit or earn.
extendedMeaning: 'So that they may commit (li-yaqtarifū) what they are committing' (6:113).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit (yaqtarifūn)' (6:120). 'Whoever earns (yaqtarif) a good deed, We increase it for him in good' (42:23). 'Wealth that you have acquired (iqtaraftumūhā)' (9:24).

primaryMeaning: To be far, to lie at the outer edge. Aqṣā is the farthest; qaṣiyy is remote.
extendedMeaning: At Badr, the enemy was 'on the farther (al-quṣwā) side' (8:42).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'From the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque (al-masjid al-aqṣā)' (17:1). 'A man came running from the farthest end (aqṣā) of the city' (28:20; 36:20). Maryam 'withdrew with him to a remote (qaṣiyyan) place' (19:22).

primaryMeaning: A drop, and the sides of something. Qiṭr is molten copper that drips; qaṭirān is tar; aqṭār are the regions or sides.
extendedMeaning: 'If you are able to pass beyond the regions (aqṭār) of the heavens and the earth, pass' (55:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Dhu al-Qarnayn said, 'Bring me molten copper (qiṭran) to pour over it' (18:96). 'We made flow for him a spring of molten copper (al-qiṭr)' — Sulayman (34:12). 'Their garments will be of tar (qaṭirān)' (14:50).

primaryMeaning: The back of the neck — and following, walking right behind someone. Qaffā is to send one after another; qafā is to pursue.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We followed up (qaffaynā) after him with messengers' — Musa (2:87), and 'We sent following in their footsteps ʿĪsā' (5:46; 57:27). 'Do not pursue (lā taqfu) that of which you have no knowledge' (17:36).

primaryMeaning: To cut into pieces. Kisf is a fragment; kisaf are pieces, as of a sky falling.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The deniers demanded, 'Cause the sky to fall on us in pieces (kisafan)' (17:92; 26:187). 'If they saw a fragment (kisfan) of the sky falling, they would say, "Heaped-up clouds"' (52:44).

primaryMeaning: To clothe, to cover the body with garments. Kasā is to clothe; kiswa is clothing.
extendedMeaning: 'Look at the bones, how We raise them, then We cover them (naksūhā) with flesh' (2:259).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Fathers must provide mothers' 'provision and clothing (kiswatuhunna)' (2:233). Expiation includes 'clothing them (kiswatuhum)' — ten poor people (5:89). 'We clothed (fa-kasawnā) the bones with flesh' (23:14).

primaryMeaning: To be complete and whole, with every part in place. Kāmil is complete; akmala is to perfect.
extendedMeaning: 'That is ten complete (kāmilatun)' — the fast of Hajj (2:196).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Today I have perfected (akmaltu) your religion for you' (5:3). 'That you may complete (li-tukmilū) the number' — of fasting days (2:185). Mothers nurse 'two complete (kāmilayn) years' (2:233).

primaryMeaning: A star — a shining heavenly body. Kawkab is a star or planet; kawākib are stars.
extendedMeaning: The glass of the lamp is 'as if it were a pearly star (kawkabun durriyy)' (24:35). 'When the stars (al-kawākib) are scattered' (82:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Ibrahim 'saw a star (kawkaban) and said, "This is my Lord"' (6:76). Yusuf saw 'eleven stars (kawkaban), the sun and the moon prostrating to me' (12:4). 'We adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment — the stars (al-kawākib)' (37:6).

primaryMeaning: To cling to something without letting go. Lazima is to stick to; alzama is to fasten on or compel; lizām is what is inevitable.
extendedMeaning: 'Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable (lizāman)' (20:129).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Every person's fate We have fastened (alzamnāhu) to his neck' (17:13). Nuh said, 'Should we compel you (a-nulzimukumūhā) to accept it while you are averse?' (11:28). 'He made them adhere (alzamahum) to the word of piety' (48:26).

primaryMeaning: To touch with the hand, to feel — and to seek by feeling for something. Lamasa is to touch; lāmasa is marital contact; iltamasa is to seek.
extendedMeaning: The jinn said, 'We sought to touch (lamasnā) the sky' (72:8). The hypocrites are told, 'Go back and seek (fa-ltamisū) light' (57:13).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Or you have touched (lāmastum) women' — requiring ablution (4:43; 5:6). 'Had We sent down to you a written scripture on parchment and they touched it (fa-lamasūhu) with their hands' (6:7).

primaryMeaning: To twist, to bend something from its straight line. Lawā is to twist; layy is twisting the tongue; lawwā is to turn the head away.
extendedMeaning: At Uhud 'you were not looking back (talwūna) at anyone' (3:153). The hypocrites 'turn (lawwaw) their heads aside' (63:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Some 'distort (yalwūna) the Book with their tongues' (3:78). 'If you distort (talwū) or turn away, Allah is aware of what you do' — in testimony (4:135). 'Twisting (layyan) with their tongues' (4:46).

primaryMeaning: Softness — the opposite of hardness. Layyin is soft or gentle; alāna is to make pliable; līna is a kind of palm tree.
extendedMeaning: 'Their skins and hearts soften (talīnu) to the remembrance of Allah' (39:23). 'Whatever palm trees (līnatin) you cut down' (59:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'By mercy from Allah you were gentle (linta) with them' (3:159). Musa and Harun were told, 'Speak to him a gentle word (qawlan layyinan)' — to Pharaoh (20:44). 'We made iron pliable (alannā) for him' — Dawud (34:10).

primaryMeaning: To be bare and smooth — a tree stripped of leaves, a youth without a beard — and from bareness, to be obstinate and rebellious, stripped of all good. Mārid and marīd are rebellious; mumarrad is made smooth.
extendedMeaning: Sulayman's palace was 'made smooth (mumarradun) with glass' (27:44).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The sky is guarded 'from every rebellious (māridin) devil' (37:7). Some 'follow every rebellious (marīdin) devil' (22:3). Some of the people of Madinah 'persist (maradū) in hypocrisy' (9:101).

primaryMeaning: A boundary between two lands — and a settled city with its borders. Miṣr is a city, and the name of Egypt.
extendedMeaning: Pharaoh said, 'Is not the kingdom of Egypt (miṣra) mine?' (43:51).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The Israelites were told, 'Go down to a city (miṣran); you will have what you asked for' (2:61). The one who bought Yusuf 'from Egypt (miṣra)' (12:21), and 'Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in safety' (12:99).

primaryMeaning: To go on, to pass by and be gone. Maḍā is to proceed or to have passed; muḍiyy is going forward.
extendedMeaning: 'We could have transformed them in their places, so they could not proceed (muḍiyyan)' (36:67).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Lut was told, 'go on (wa-mḍū) where you are commanded' (15:65). 'The example of the former peoples has passed (maḍat)' (8:38). Musa said, 'I will continue (amḍiya) for a long time' until he reached the meeting of the seas (18:60).

primaryMeaning: To sway and shake. Māda is to tremble; mā'ida is a table spread with food, classically named for moving under its load.
extendedMeaning: Surah 5 is Al-Mā'ida, 'the Table Spread'.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'He placed in the earth firm mountains lest it should shake (tamīda) with you' (16:15; 21:31). The disciples asked, 'Can your Lord send down to us a table spread (mā'idatan) from the sky?' (5:112).

primaryMeaning: To uproot and blow away, to scatter into fine particles. Nasafa is to blast something to dust.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'They ask you about the mountains; say, my Lord will blast them (yansifuhā) into particles (nasfan)' (20:105). 'When the mountains are blown away (nusifat)' (77:10). Musa said of the calf, 'We will scatter it (la-nansifannahu) in the sea' (20:97).

primaryMeaning: Raised ground — and from it, rising up; in marriage, nushūz is one spouse rising against the other — ill conduct or aversion.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Look at the bones, how We raise them (nunshizuhā)' (2:259). 'When you are told, Rise up (unshuzū), then rise up' (58:11). Rulings on nushūz, 'ill-conduct', are set out for wives (4:34) and husbands (4:128).

primaryMeaning: To run out, to be used up completely. Nafida is to be exhausted; nafād is running out.
extendedMeaning: 'This is Our provision; it has no depletion (nafādin)' (38:54).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'What is with you will run out (yanfadu), and what is with Allah remains' (16:96). 'If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted (la-nafida) before the words of my Lord were exhausted (tanfada)' (18:109; 31:27).

primaryMeaning: To rescue, to pull someone out of danger. Anqadha is to save; istanqadha is to recover something.
extendedMeaning: 'Can you save (tunqidhu) one who is in the Fire?' (39:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'You were on the brink of a pit of fire, and He saved you (fa-anqadhakum) from it' (3:103). 'Their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me (yunqidhūn)' (36:23). If a fly takes something from the idols, 'they cannot recover it (yastanqidhūhu)' (22:73).

primaryMeaning: A restraint — a heavy fetter — and so a punishment that makes an example and deters others. Nakāl is exemplary punishment; ankāl are shackles.
extendedMeaning: 'With Us are shackles (ankālan) and a Blaze' (73:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. The Sabbath-breakers were made 'a deterrent punishment (nakālan) for those present and those after them' (2:66). The thief's punishment is 'a deterrent from Allah' (5:38). Allah seized Pharaoh 'with the exemplary punishment (nakāla) of the Hereafter and the first' (79:25).

primaryMeaning: To shake, to set something in quick motion. Hazza is to shake; ihtazza is to stir or quiver.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Maryam was told, 'Shake (huzzī) towards you the trunk of the palm tree' (19:25). Musa's staff was 'moving (tahtazzu) as if it were a snake' (27:10). When rain falls on dry land, 'it stirs (ihtazzat) and swells' (22:5).

primaryMeaning: To raise the voice — at the sighting of the new moon, or in calling a name over a sacrifice. Hilāl is the new crescent; uhilla is for a name to be invoked.
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Forbidden is 'what has been dedicated (uhilla) to other than Allah' (2:173). 'They ask you about the new moons (al-ahilla); say, they are markers of time for people and for Hajj' (2:189).

primaryMeaning: Fear that makes the heart tremble — awe mixed with dread. Wajila is to be afraid; wajil is fearful.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim told his guests, 'We are afraid (wajilūn) of you', and they said, 'Do not be afraid (lā tawjal)' (15:52–53).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'The believers are those whose hearts tremble (wajilat) when Allah is mentioned' (8:2; 22:35). Those who give 'with their hearts fearful (wajilatun) that they will return to their Lord' (23:60).

primaryMeaning: To hold back and keep in order — to restrain a crowd so it moves in ranks. Yūzaʿūn is 'arranged in rows'; awzaʿa is to inspire, to keep someone steadily at something.
extendedMeaning: 'The enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, driven in rows (yūzaʿūn)' (41:19).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. Sulayman's hosts 'were marshalled in rows (yūzaʿūn)' (27:17). Sulayman prayed, 'My Lord, enable me (awziʿnī) to be grateful for Your favour' (27:19), a prayer repeated in 46:15.

primaryMeaning: The middle — the centre of something, and so the best and most balanced part. Wasaṭ is middle or moderate; wusṭā is the middle one; awsaṭ is the most moderate.
extendedMeaning: 'The most moderate (awsaṭuhum) of them said' (68:28). The chargers 'penetrate into the centre (fa-wasaṭna)' of the enemy (100:5).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'We made you a middle (wasaṭan) nation, so that you may be witnesses over mankind' (2:143). 'Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer (al-wusṭā)' (2:238). The expiation is feeding 'from the average (awsaṭi) of what you feed your families' (5:89).

primaryMeaning: A soft, repeated whisper — the faint sound of jewellery or a hidden voice. Waswasa is whispering evil suggestions; waswās is the whisperer.
extendedMeaning: 'We know what his soul whispers (tuwaswisu) to him' (50:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 5 times. 'Satan whispered (fa-waswasa) to them' — Adam and his wife (7:20; 20:120). 'From the evil of the whisperer (al-waswās) who withdraws, who whispers (yuwaswisu) in the breasts of people' (114:4–5).

primaryMeaning: To set, to disappear from view — as the stars and sun go down.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times, all in Ibrahim's reasoning: when the star set (afala), he said, 'I do not love those that set (al-āfilīn)' (6:76), then the moon set (6:77), then the sun set (afalat) (6:78) — showing that what disappears cannot be God.

primaryMeaning: A limit or end point — the distance to a final term. Amad is an extent of time.
extendedMeaning: 'I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a term (amadan)' (72:25).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Each soul will wish 'there were between it and its evil a great distance (amadan)' (3:30). 'Which of the two parties best calculated the time (amadan) they remained?' (18:12). 'The time (al-amad) was prolonged for them, and their hearts hardened' (57:16).

primaryMeaning: To make something new, with no model before it. Badīʿ is the Originator; bidʿ is something unprecedented; ibtadaʿa is to invent.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Originator (badīʿu) of the heavens and the earth' (2:117; 6:101). 'Say, I am not something new (bidʿan) among the messengers' (46:9). 'Monasticism they invented (ibtadaʿūhā); We did not prescribe it' (57:27).

primaryMeaning: The mind and its condition — how a matter stands. Bāl is state or concern.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Pharaoh asked, 'What then is the case (bālu) of the former generations?' (20:51). Yusuf said, 'Ask him, what is the case (bālu) of the women who cut their hands?' (12:50). Allah 'will amend their condition (bālahum)' — those who believe (47:2).

primaryMeaning: Loss that leads to ruin — to perish, to be cut off. Tabba is to perish; tabāb and tatbīb are ruin.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Perish (tabbat) the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he (wa-tabba)' (111:1). The false gods 'did not increase them other than in ruin (tatbībin)' (11:101). 'The plan of Pharaoh was not but in ruin (tabābin)' (40:37).

primaryMeaning: A wall — and from what fits within its bounds, being fitting and suited. Jidār is a wall; ajdar is more fitting or more likely.
extendedMeaning: The bedouins are 'more likely (ajdaru) not to know the limits of what Allah revealed' (9:97).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Musa and al-Khiḍr found 'a wall (jidāran) about to collapse, so he set it straight' (18:77), and 'as for the wall (al-jidār), it belonged to two orphan boys' (18:82). They will not fight you 'except from behind walls (judurin)' (59:14).

primaryMeaning: To wound — and to earn, to gain with the limbs. Jurḥ is a wound; jawāriḥ are hunting animals, which catch prey, and the limbs that act; ijtaraḥa is to commit.
extendedMeaning: 'Do those who commit (ijtaraḥū) evil deeds think We will make them like those who believe?' (45:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'For wounds (al-jurūḥ) is legal retribution' (5:45). Lawful is what is caught by 'the hunting animals (al-jawāriḥ) you have trained' (5:4). Allah 'knows what you have committed (jaraḥtum) by day' (6:60).

primaryMeaning: A body — a physical form without a spirit. Jasad is a body or a lifeless image.
extendedMeaning: 'We placed on his throne a body (jasadan); then he turned back' — Sulayman (38:34).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The Israelites took 'a calf — a body (jasadan) that made a lowing sound' (7:148; 20:88). 'We did not make them bodies (jasadan) not eating food' — the prophets (21:8).

primaryMeaning: To equip and prepare someone for a journey. Jahhaza is to furnish with supplies; jahāz is provisions.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times, in the story of Yusuf: 'when he had furnished them (jahhazahum) with their supplies (bi-jahāzihim), he said, Bring me a brother of yours' (12:59). The second time, he put the cup in his brother's bag (12:70).

primaryMeaning: Black, altered mud — dark clay that has changed in smell and colour.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'We created man from dry clay of altered black mud (ḥama'in masnūn)' (15:26; 15:28; 15:33). Dhu al-Qarnayn found the sun setting 'in a spring of dark mud (ḥami'atin)' (18:86).

primaryMeaning: To flow — used for a woman's menstrual flow. Maḥīḍ is menstruation.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'They ask you about menstruation (al-maḥīḍ); say, it is a hurt, so keep away from wives during menstruation' (2:222). The waiting period is set for women who 'have despaired of menstruation (al-maḥīḍ)' and those who 'have not yet menstruated (yaḥiḍna)' (65:4).

primaryMeaning: To tear through, to make a hole — and to fabricate, to tear a lie out of nothing. Kharaqa is to pierce or to invent falsely.
extendedMeaning: 'They falsely attribute (kharaqū) to Him sons and daughters without knowledge' (6:100).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Al-Khiḍr 'made a hole in it (kharaqahā)' — the boat — and Musa asked, 'Have you made a hole in it (a-kharaqtahā) to drown its people?' (18:71). 'You will never tear (takhriqa) the earth apart, nor reach the mountains in height' (17:37).

primaryMeaning: To drive away with contempt — as one drives off a dog. Khasi'a is to be rejected and despised; khāsi' is humbled and worn out.
extendedMeaning: 'Your sight will return to you humbled (khāsi'an) and fatigued' (67:4).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The Sabbath-breakers were told, 'Be apes, despised (khāsi'īn)' (2:65; 7:166). The people of the Fire will be told, 'Remain despised therein (ikhsa'ū) and do not speak to Me' (23:108).

primaryMeaning: To single out something for oneself or for someone — as opposed to what is general. Ikhtaṣṣa is to choose specially; khāṣṣatan is exclusively; khaṣāṣa is poverty — a gap, a narrow need.
extendedMeaning: The Ansar 'give preference over themselves, even though they are in poverty (khaṣāṣa)' (59:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Allah chooses (yakhtaṣṣu) for His mercy whom He wills' (2:105; 3:74). 'Fear a trial that will not strike those who wronged among you exclusively (khāṣṣatan)' (8:25).

primaryMeaning: To lower, to bring down — the opposite of raising. Khafaḍa is to lower; khāfiḍa is one that brings down.
extendedMeaning: The Event will be 'bringing down (khāfiḍatun), raising up' (56:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Lower (wa-khfiḍ) to them the wing of humility out of mercy' — to parents (17:24). 'Lower your wing (wa-khfiḍ) to the believers' (15:88; 26:215).

primaryMeaning: To drive away with force and humiliation. Madḥūr is expelled and banished; duḥūr is being repelled.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Iblis was told, 'Get out of it, disgraced and expelled (madḥūran)' (7:18). Whoever wants only this world will burn in Hell 'disgraced and banished (madḥūran)' (17:18). The devils are 'repelled (duḥūran)' from the heavens (37:9).

primaryMeaning: To slip and fall — for a foot to slide. Adḥaḍa is to refute, to make an argument slip; dāḥiḍ is invalid; mudḥaḍ is one who loses.
extendedMeaning: Yunus cast lots with the ship's crew 'and was among the losers (al-mudḥaḍīn)' (37:141).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The disbelievers 'dispute with falsehood to refute (li-yudḥiḍū) the truth by it' (18:56; 40:5). 'Their argument is invalid (dāḥiḍatun) with their Lord' (42:16).

primaryMeaning: To be humbled and lowly. Dākhir is one who is abased.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The shadows of all things 'prostrate to Allah while they are humble (dākhirūn)' (16:48). 'Those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell humbled (dākhirīn)' (40:60). 'All will come to Him humbled (dākhirīn)' (27:87).

primaryMeaning: To flow abundantly, like milk from the udder. Midrār is pouring rain in abundance; durriyy is brilliant, shining like a pearl (durr).
extendedMeaning: The glass of the lamp is 'as if it were a brilliant (durriyyun) star' (24:35).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'We sent the sky upon them in abundant showers (midrāran)' (6:6). Hud and Nuh promised their peoples that Allah 'will send the sky upon you in abundant rain (midrāran)' (11:52; 71:11).

primaryMeaning: To let down a bucket into a well. Dalw is a bucket; adlā is to let down — and to present one's case, to lower it to a judge; tadallā is to draw near, coming down.
extendedMeaning: 'Then he drew near and came down (fa-tadallā)' — Jibrīl (53:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. A caravan 'sent their water-drawer, and he let down (fa-adlā) his bucket (dalwahu)' and found Yusuf (12:19). 'Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, nor present it (tudlū) to the rulers' (2:188).

primaryMeaning: To set things in good order, evenly spaced — teeth well arranged. Tartīl is reciting clearly and measuredly, each word distinct.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Recite the Quran with measured recitation (rattili al-qur'āna tartīlā)' (73:4). 'We have recited it (rattalnāhu) with distinct recitation' — sent down in stages (25:32).

primaryMeaning: To be wide and spacious. Raḥuba is to be vast; marḥaban is 'welcome' — may you find space.
extendedMeaning: The people of the Fire say of newcomers, 'No welcome (lā marḥaban) for them' (38:59–60).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. At Hunayn 'the earth, despite its vastness (raḥubat), was straitened for you' (9:25). The three who stayed behind felt the earth 'straitened for them, despite its vastness' (9:118).

primaryMeaning: To set out on a journey — to saddle up and move on. Riḥla is a journey; raḥl is a saddlebag.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Their accustomed security in the journey (riḥlata) of winter and summer' — Quraysh (106:2). Yusuf had the cup put 'in his brother's bag (raḥli)' (12:70), and the goods 'in their saddlebags (riḥālihim)' (12:62).

primaryMeaning: To be low and base — the worst of something. Ardhal is the lowest or most despised; ardhal al-ʿumur is decrepit old age.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Among you is one returned to the most decrepit (ardhali) age, so he knows nothing after having known' (16:70; 22:5). Nuh's people said, 'We see only the lowest of us (arādhilunā) follow you' (11:27).

primaryMeaning: To climb, to go up. Raqiya is to ascend; irtaqā is to climb up; rāqin is one who recites a healing charm.
extendedMeaning: At death it will be said, 'Who will cure (rāqin) him?' (75:27).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The deniers demanded, 'or you ascend (tarqā) into the sky, and we will not believe your ascension (li-ruqiyyika)' (17:93). 'Let them ascend (fal-yartaqū) by the ways' (38:10).

primaryMeaning: The strong side of something, a support to lean on. Rukn is a pillar or support; rakana is to incline towards and rely on.
extendedMeaning: Pharaoh 'turned away with his supporters (bi-ruknihi)' (51:39).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Do not incline (lā tarkanū) towards those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you' (11:113). 'We strengthened you, or you would have inclined (tarkanu) to them a little' (17:74). Lut said, 'If only I had strength, or could take refuge in a strong support (ruknin)' (11:80).

primaryMeaning: Gold — and any glittering adornment. Zukhruf is ornament, and decorated, attractive speech that deceives.
extendedMeaning: 'And ornaments of gold (zukhrufan) — all that is only the enjoyment of worldly life' (43:35). Surah 43 is Al-Zukhruf.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. When the earth 'takes on its adornment (zukhrufahā)', its people think they have power over it (10:24). Devils inspire one another 'with decorative (zukhrufa) speech' (6:112). The deniers demanded 'a house of ornament (zukhrufin)' (17:93).

primaryMeaning: To slip — to slide from where one stood. Zalla is to slip; azalla and istazalla are to make someone slip.
extendedMeaning: 'Lest a foot slip (fa-tazilla) after being firmly planted' (16:94).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Satan caused them to slip (fa-azallahumā) out of it' — Adam and his wife (2:36). 'If you slip (zalaltum) after clear proofs have come to you, know that Allah is Almighty' (2:209). At Uhud, 'Satan made them slip (istazallahum) for some of what they had earned' (3:155).

primaryMeaning: To move away from its place, to cease being there. Zāla is to vanish or be removed; zawāl is coming to an end.
extendedMeaning: 'Their plot was not such as to move (li-tazūla) the mountains' (14:46).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease (tazūlā); if they ceased (zālatā), no one could hold them after Him' (35:41). The wrongdoers had sworn 'that for you there would be no end (zawālin)' (14:44).

primaryMeaning: Sijill is a written record or scroll. Sijjīl, 'stones of baked clay', is placed here too, though classical scholars differ over its origin — some relate it to sijill, stones recorded for punishment, and others treat it as a borrowed word.
extendedMeaning: 'The Day We will fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll (al-sijill) for records' (21:104).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The people of Lut were rained upon with 'stones of baked clay (sijjīlin)' (11:82; 15:74), and the army of the Elephant struck 'with stones of baked clay (sijjīl)' (105:4).

primaryMeaning: To destroy root and branch, to wipe out. Suḥt is unlawful gain — earnings that destroy their owner's blessing; asḥata is to annihilate.
extendedMeaning: Musa warned the magicians, 'Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you (fa-yusḥitakum) with punishment' (20:61).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. They are 'avid listeners to falsehood, devourers of the forbidden (lil-suḥt)' (5:42). 'Why do the rabbis not forbid them from eating the forbidden (al-suḥt)?' (5:63).

primaryMeaning: Anger and strong displeasure — the opposite of riḍā. Sakhaṭ is wrath; sakhiṭa is to be angry; askhaṭa is to provoke anger.
extendedMeaning: If not given charity, 'they are enraged (yaskhaṭūn)' (9:58).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Is one who pursues the pleasure of Allah like one who brings upon himself the wrath (bi-sakhaṭin) of Allah?' (3:162). 'Evil is what their souls put forth, that Allah became angry (sakhiṭa) with them' (5:80). 'They followed what angered (askhaṭa) Allah' (47:28).

primaryMeaning: The lote tree — the sidr, a thorny tree of the desert with shade and small fruit.
extendedMeaning: The gardens of Saba' were replaced with 'something of sparse lote trees (sidrin)' (34:16).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The Prophet saw Jibrīl 'at the Lote Tree of the utmost boundary (sidrat al-muntahā)' (53:14), 'when there covered the Lote Tree (al-sidra) what covered it' (53:16). In Paradise, 'among lote trees (sidrin) with thorns removed' (56:28).

primaryMeaning: To move along freely, to go one's way — like water running in a channel. Sarāb, 'mirage', is shimmering heat that seems to flow like water; saraba is a path, an opening.
extendedMeaning: The fish 'took its way into the sea, slipping away (saraban)' (18:61). Allah knows 'one who goes freely (sāribun) by day' (13:10).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The deeds of the disbelievers are 'like a mirage (ka-sarābin) in a lowland, which a thirsty one thinks is water' (24:39). 'The mountains will be moved and become a mirage (sarāban)' (78:20).

primaryMeaning: A lamp that gives light. Sirāj is a lamp.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'He placed in it a lamp (sirājan) and an illuminating moon' — the sun (25:61; 71:16). 'We placed therein a burning lamp (sirājan wahhājā)' (78:13). The Prophet is 'a light-giving lamp (sirājan munīrā)' (33:46).

primaryMeaning: To pour out, to spill freely. Masfūḥ is poured out; musāfiḥ is one who spills his desires unlawfully — a fornicator.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Marriage is for men 'seeking chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse (musāfiḥīn)' (4:24; 5:5), and women 'chaste, not committing immorality (musāfiḥāt)' (4:25). Forbidden is 'blood poured forth (masfūḥan)' (6:145).

primaryMeaning: To peel off, to scrape the surface. Safīna, 'a ship', is classically explained as the one that cuts through the surface of the water.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'We saved him and the people of the ship (al-safīna)' — Nuh (29:15). Al-Khiḍr made a hole in the ship (18:71), and explained, 'As for the ship (al-safīna), it belonged to poor people working at sea' (18:79).

primaryMeaning: A roof — a covering raised over something. Saqf is a roof or ceiling.
extendedMeaning: Had it not been for people becoming one community in disbelief, their houses would have 'roofs (suqufan) of silver' (43:33).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'We made the sky a protected roof (saqfan)' (21:32). 'By the roof (wal-saqf) raised high' (52:5). 'The roof (al-saqf) fell upon them from above them' (16:26).

primaryMeaning: Weapons — the arms one carries. Silāḥ is arms; asliḥa are weapons.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times, all in the ruling on prayer in fear: 'let a group of them stand with you and take their arms (asliḥatahum)' (4:102). There is no blame if rain or illness makes you 'put down your arms (asliḥatakum)' — but 'take your precautions' (4:102).

primaryMeaning: To talk by night. Sāmir is one who converses at night; al-Sāmirī is the man who led the Israelites to worship the calf.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'The Samiri (al-sāmiriyy) has led them astray' (20:85). Musa asked, 'What is your case, O Samiri (yā sāmiriyy)?' (20:95). The deniers were 'arrogant about it, conversing by night (sāmiran)' (23:67).

primaryMeaning: A small opening — the eye of a needle, or a pore that lets in poison. Samm is a hole; samūm is a scorching wind that penetrates the pores.
extendedMeaning: 'Allah protected us from the punishment of the scorching fire (al-samūm)' (52:27). The companions of the left are 'in scorching wind (samūmin) and boiling water' (56:42).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The deniers will not enter Paradise 'until a camel passes through the eye (samm) of a needle' (7:40). The jinn were created 'from the fire of scorching wind (al-samūm)' (15:27).

primaryMeaning: Fatness — being plump and well fed. Samīn is fat; asmana is to fatten or nourish.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The king saw 'seven fat (simānin) cows eaten by seven lean' (12:43). Ibrahim 'brought a fat (samīnin) calf' for his guests (51:26). The food of the Fire 'neither nourishes (yusminu) nor avails against hunger' (88:7).

primaryMeaning: To make something seem easy and attractive — to entice. Sawwala is to tempt, to make a wrong seem pleasing.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Yaʿqub told his sons, 'Your souls have enticed (sawwalat) you to something' (12:18; 12:83). The Samiri said, 'Thus did my soul entice (sawwalat) me' (20:96). 'Satan enticed (sawwala) them and prolonged hope for them' (47:25).

primaryMeaning: To flow, to run like water. Sāla is to flow; sayl is a torrent or flood; asāla is to make flow.
extendedMeaning: 'We made flow (asalnā) for him a spring of molten copper' — Sulayman (34:12).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow (fa-sālat) according to their measure, and the torrent (al-sayl) carries a rising foam' (13:17). 'We sent upon them the flood (sayla) of the dam' — Saba' (34:16).

primaryMeaning: An affair or matter — something one is concerned with. Sha'n is a state or business.
extendedMeaning: 'When they ask your permission for some affair of theirs (sha'nihim)' (24:62).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'You are not in any situation (sha'nin) … but We are witness over you' (10:61). 'Every day He is in a matter (sha'nin)' (55:29). 'Every man that Day will have a matter (sha'nun) enough to occupy him' (80:37).

primaryMeaning: To draw out honey from the hive — and to seek out another's view. Shāwara is to consult; shūrā is mutual consultation; ashāra is to point, to indicate.
extendedMeaning: Maryam 'pointed (fa-ashārat) to him' — the infant ʿĪsā (19:29). Surah 42 is Al-Shūrā.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Consult them (shāwirhum) in the matter' (3:159). The believers' 'affair is by consultation (shūrā) among them' (42:38). Weaning may be decided 'by mutual consent and consultation (tashāwur)' (2:233).

primaryMeaning: An old man — one whose age shows. Shaykh is an elder; shuyūkh are old men.
extendedMeaning: 'Then He brings you out as a child, then you reach full strength, then become old (shuyūkhan)' (40:67).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Sarah said, 'This is my husband, an old man (shaykhan)' (11:72). Shuʿayb's daughters said, 'Our father is a very old man (shaykhun kabīr)' (28:23). Yusuf's brothers said, 'He has a very old father (shaykhan kabīran)' (12:78).

primaryMeaning: To be clear and plain — and a tall, clearly visible building. Ṣarḥ is a lofty tower or palace.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, build me a tower (ṣarḥan)' (28:38; 40:36). The Queen of Sheba was told, 'Enter the palace (al-ṣarḥ)' — and 'it is a palace (ṣarḥun) made smooth with glass' (27:44).

primaryMeaning: The ringing sound of something dry — clay that rings when struck. Ṣalṣāl is dry, sounding clay.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times, all for the creation of man: 'We created man from sounding clay (ṣalṣālin), from altered black mud' (15:26). 'He created man from sounding clay (ṣalṣālin) like pottery' (55:14).

primaryMeaning: To cover one thing with another that fits it exactly — layer upon layer. Ṭabaq is a layer or stage; ṭibāq are layers, one above another.
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'He who created seven heavens in layers (ṭibāqan)' (67:3; 71:15). 'You will surely pass from stage to stage (ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaqin)' (84:19).

primaryMeaning: Softness and tenderness — a small child. Ṭifl is an infant; aṭfāl are children.
extendedMeaning: Women may show adornment to 'children (al-ṭifl) who are not yet aware of women's private matters' (24:31).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Then We bring you out as a child (ṭiflan)' (22:5; 40:67). 'When the children (al-aṭfāl) among you reach puberty, let them ask permission' (24:59).

primaryMeaning: To seek, to try to find or obtain something. Ṭalab is seeking; ṭālib is a seeker; maṭlūb is what is sought.
extendedMeaning: 'Its water may sink into the ground, so you will not be able to find it (ṭalaban)' (18:41).
