quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The night 'seeks it (yaṭlubuhu) rapidly' — the day (7:54). If a fly snatches something from the idols, 'weak are the seeker (al-ṭālib) and the sought (al-maṭlūb)' (22:73).

primaryMeaning: The capacity to bear something — and a collar encircling the neck. Ṭāqa is strength or ability; ṭawwaqa is to put a collar on.
extendedMeaning: What the misers withheld 'will be a collar around their necks (sa-yuṭawwaqūna)' on the Day of Resurrection (3:180).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength (ṭāqata) to bear' (2:286). Talut's army said, 'We have no strength (ṭāqata) today against Jalut' (2:249). 'For those who can afford it only with hardship (yuṭīqūnahu), a ransom' (2:184).

primaryMeaning: To be unclear in speech. Aʿjam is one who does not speak Arabic clearly; aʿjamiyy is foreign, non-Arabic.
extendedMeaning: 'Had We sent it down to one of the non-Arabs (al-aʿjamīn)' (26:198).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. 'The tongue of the one they point to is foreign (aʿjamiyyun), and this is a clear Arabic tongue' (16:103). 'Had We made it a foreign (aʿjamiyyan) Quran, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained?"' (41:44).

primaryMeaning: To hold back from what is not lawful or fitting — restraint and chastity. Taʿaffuf is modest restraint; istaʿaffa is to keep oneself chaste.
extendedMeaning: For elderly women, 'to modestly refrain (yastaʿfifna) is better for them' (24:60).
quranUsage: Occurs 4 times. The ignorant think the poor are rich 'because of their restraint (al-taʿaffuf)' from begging (2:273). 'Let those who cannot find the means to marry keep chaste (wal-yastaʿfif)' (24:33). A rich guardian of an orphan 'should refrain (fal-yastaʿfif)' from taking a wage (4:6).

primaryMeaning: barren, sterile
extendedMeaning: Barren, sterile.
quranUsage: 'Aqīm (عقيم) is barren. 'A barren ('aqīm) wind.' 'I am barren ('aqim).'

primaryMeaning: nakedness, shame
extendedMeaning: Nakedness, shame, defect.
quranUsage: 'Awrah (عورة) is nakedness/vulnerable. 'Our houses are exposed ('awrah).'

primaryMeaning: darkness, dusk
extendedMeaning: Darkness, dusk.
quranUsage: Ghasaq (غسق) is darkness. 'The darkness (ghasaq) of night.'

primaryMeaning: washing, ritual bath
extendedMeaning: Washing and ritual bathing (ghusl).
quranUsage: 'If you are in a state of major impurity, purify yourselves.' Ghusl is ritual bath.
notes: Ghusl is required after certain states for prayer.

primaryMeaning: to lower, reduce
extendedMeaning: Lowering, reducing.
quranUsage: Yaghuddu means to lower. 'Lower (ughdudd) your voice.' 'Lower (yaghuddu) their gaze.'

primaryMeaning: to cover, immerse
extendedMeaning: Covering, immersing.
quranUsage: Ghamrah (غمرة) is covering/flood. 'In their flood (ghamratihim) of ignorance.'

primaryMeaning: to sink, depth
extendedMeaning: Sinking, depth.
quranUsage: Ghawran (غورا) is sinking/deep. 'Its water becomes sunken (ghawran).'

primaryMeaning: rain, relief, help
extendedMeaning: Beneficial rain that brings relief.
quranUsage: 'He sends down the rain (ghayth).' Ghayth is saving rain.
notes: Ghayth implies rain that relieves drought - a mercy.

primaryMeaning: to fail, weaken
extendedMeaning: Failing, weakening.
quranUsage: Tafshalū means to fail. 'Lest you fail (tafshalū).'

primaryMeaning: split, cleave, dawn
extendedMeaning: Splitting, cleaving, daybreak.
quranUsage: 'Splitter (Faliq) of the seed.' Falaq is daybreak/splitting.
notes: Surah Al-Falaq - The Daybreak. Seeds split to grow.

primaryMeaning: boil, erupt, immediate
extendedMeaning: Boiling, erupting, immediately.
quranUsage: 'When Hell boils over (farat).' Fawran is immediately. Fawr is boiling.
notes: Hell boils and erupts with fury.

primaryMeaning: necklace, imitate
extendedMeaning: Necklace, imitation.
quranUsage: Qalā'id (قلائد) are necklaces/garlands. 'The garlanded (qalā'id) animals.'

primaryMeaning: pen, to cut/trim
extendedMeaning: Pen (originally a trimmed reed) for writing.
quranUsage: 'By the pen (qalam) and what they write.' Al-Qalam is Surah 68.
notes: The pen was among the first things created.

primaryMeaning: heaps of wealth
extendedMeaning: Heaps of wealth, quintals.
quranUsage: Qanātīr (قناطير) are heaps. 'Heaps (qanātīr) of gold and silver.'

primaryMeaning: distress, anguish
extendedMeaning: Distress, anguish.
quranUsage: Karb (كرب) is distress. 'We saved him from the distress (karb).'

primaryMeaning: ankle, cube, Kaaba
extendedMeaning: Ankle, cube shape, and the Kaaba.
quranUsage: 'To the ankles (ka'bayn).' Ka'b is ankle. Ka'bah is cube-shaped.
notes: The Kaaba is cube-shaped. Feet are washed to the ankles.

primaryMeaning: cup, goblet
extendedMeaning: Cup, goblet.
quranUsage: Akwāb (أكواب) are cups. 'With cups (akwāb) and jugs.'

primaryMeaning: deep sea, persist
extendedMeaning: Deep sea, and persisting stubbornly.
quranUsage: 'Darkness in a deep sea (lujji).' Lujjah is deep sea.
notes: Disbelief is like being in deep, dark waters.

primaryMeaning: to criticize, mock
extendedMeaning: Criticizing, mocking.
quranUsage: Yalmizūna means to criticize. 'Those who criticize (yalmizūna).' Lumazah is slanderer.

primaryMeaning: glory, honor, nobility
extendedMeaning: Glory, honor, and noble generosity.
quranUsage: Al-Majid (The Glorious) is Allah's name. 'Quran Majid' - Glorious Quran.
notes: Majid implies glorious and generous together.

primaryMeaning: to tear, rend
extendedMeaning: Tearing, rending.
quranUsage: Mazzaqnā means to tear apart. 'We tore them (mazzaqnāhum) apart.'

primaryMeaning: contemptible, lowly
extendedMeaning: Contemptible, lowly.
quranUsage: Mahīn (مهين) is contemptible. 'From water contemptible (mahīn).'

primaryMeaning: to distinguish, separate
extendedMeaning: Distinguishing, separating.
quranUsage: Yamīzu means to distinguish. 'Until He distinguishes (yamīza) the evil from the good.'

primaryMeaning: to carve, hew
extendedMeaning: Carving, hewing.
quranUsage: Tanhitūn means to carve. 'You carve (tanhitūn) houses from mountains.'

primaryMeaning: to abrogate, copy
extendedMeaning: Abrogating, copying.
quranUsage: Nansakh means to abrogate. 'What We abrogate (nansakh) of a verse.'

primaryMeaning: offspring, to hurry
extendedMeaning: Offspring, hurrying.
quranUsage: Nasl (نسل) is offspring. Yansilūn means they hasten. 'They hasten (yansilūn).'

primaryMeaning: forelock
extendedMeaning: Forelock, front of head.
quranUsage: Nāsiya (ناصية) is forelock. 'A lying, sinful forelock (nāsiya).'

primaryMeaning: ewe, female sheep
extendedMeaning: Ewe, female sheep.
quranUsage: Na'jah (نعجة) is ewe. 'Ninety-nine ewes (na'jah).'

primaryMeaning: extra, spoils
extendedMeaning: Extra, spoils of war.
quranUsage: Anfāl (أنفال) are spoils. Surah Al-Anfāl. Nāfilah is extra prayer.

primaryMeaning: to peck, examine
extendedMeaning: Pecking, examining.
quranUsage: Naqīr (نقير) is speck. 'Not even a speck (naqīran).' Also: nāqūr (trumpet).

primaryMeaning: ant
extendedMeaning: Ant - example of small yet organized creature.
quranUsage: An-Naml (The Ant) is Surah 27. An ant warned others of Sulaiman's army.
notes: Ants show organization and communication.

primaryMeaning: to bring, give
extendedMeaning: Bringing, giving.
quranUsage: Hātū means bring. 'Bring (hātū) your proof.'

primaryMeaning: pleasant, enjoyable
extendedMeaning: Pleasant, enjoyable.
quranUsage: Hanī'an (هنيئا) is pleasant/wholesome. 'Eat it pleasantly (hanī'an).'

primaryMeaning: to prepare, make ready
extendedMeaning: Preparing, making ready.
quranUsage: Hayyi' means to prepare. 'Prepare (hayyi') for us.'

primaryMeaning: to leave, put down
extendedMeaning: Leaving, putting down.
quranUsage: Wadda'a means to leave. 'Your Lord has not left (wadda'aka) you.'

primaryMeaning: leaf, paper
extendedMeaning: Leaf, foliage, and paper.
quranUsage: 'They began to cover themselves with leaves (waraq).' Waraq is leaves/paper.
notes: Adam and Hawwa covered themselves with Paradise leaves.

primaryMeaning: to succeed, agree
extendedMeaning: Succeeding, agreeing.
quranUsage: Tawfīq (توفيق) is success. 'My success (tawfīqī) is only through Allah.'

primaryMeaning: to stop, stand, pause
extendedMeaning: Stopping, standing still, and pausing.
quranUsage: 'Stop (qif) them, they will be questioned.' Wuquf is standing (at Arafah).
notes: Standing at Arafah is the pillar of Hajj.

primaryMeaning: dry, withered
extendedMeaning: Dryness, being withered.
quranUsage: 'Green or dry (yabis)' - all recorded in a clear book. Yabis is dry.
notes: Nothing escapes Allah's knowledge - fresh or dry.

primaryMeaning: camels
extendedMeaning: Camels.
quranUsage: Ibil (إبل) is camels. 'Do they not look at the ibil (camels)?'

primaryMeaning: to kindle, blaze
extendedMeaning: Kindling, blazing.
quranUsage: Ujaj (أجاج) is salty/bitter. 'And this is salty, bitter (ujaj).'

primaryMeaning: to approach, draw near
extendedMeaning: Approaching, drawing near.
quranUsage: Azifah (آزفة) is the Approaching. 'The Approaching Day (azifah) has approached.'

primaryMeaning: to found, base
extendedMeaning: Founding, establishing a base.
quranUsage: Assasa means to found. 'One who founded (assasa) his building on taqwa.'

primaryMeaning: burden, covenant
extendedMeaning: Heavy burden, covenant.
quranUsage: Isr (إصر) is burden. 'The burden (isr) that was upon them.'

primaryMeaning: expression of disgust
extendedMeaning: Expression of annoyance.
quranUsage: Uff (أف) is an expression of disgust. 'Do not say to them uff.'

primaryMeaning: horizon
extendedMeaning: Horizon, region.
quranUsage: 'On the clear horizon (ufuq).' Ufuq is horizon. Afaq are horizons/regions.
notes: The Prophet saw Jibril on the clear horizon.

primaryMeaning: nose, self, pride
extendedMeaning: Nose, oneself, and pride/disdain.
quranUsage: 'The nose (anf) for a nose' - in retribution laws. Anifa means to disdain.
notes: Anf also relates to self-respect and pride.

primaryMeaning: seed, scatter, waste
extendedMeaning: Seeds, scattering seed, and wasting.
quranUsage: 'Do not waste (tubaddhir) wastefully.' Badhr is seed. Tabdhir is wasting.
notes: Don't scatter resources wastefully.

primaryMeaning: to depart, cease
extendedMeaning: Departing, ceasing.
quranUsage: Bariha means to cease. 'I will not cease (abrahu) until I reach.'

primaryMeaning: barrier, isthmus
extendedMeaning: A barrier between two things.
quranUsage: Barzakh (برزخ) is barrier. 'Between them is a barzakh (barrier).' Also the realm after death.

primaryMeaning: beauty, joy
extendedMeaning: Beauty, joy.
quranUsage: Bahij (بهيج) is beautiful. 'Pairs of every beautiful (bahij) kind.'

primaryMeaning: cattle, beasts
extendedMeaning: Cattle, livestock.
quranUsage: Bahimah (بهيمة) is beast. 'Bahimah (beast) of cattle.'

primaryMeaning: to destroy
extendedMeaning: Destroying.
quranUsage: Related to destruction.

primaryMeaning: to cry out, supplicate
extendedMeaning: Crying out, supplicating loudly.
quranUsage: Ja'ara means to cry out. 'You cry out (taj'arun) to Him.'

primaryMeaning: kneel, crouch
extendedMeaning: Kneeling, crouching on knees.
quranUsage: 'Every nation kneeling (jathiyah).' Juthuuw is kneeling.
notes: Surah Al-Jathiyah - nations kneeling before judgment.

primaryMeaning: grave
extendedMeaning: A grave.
quranUsage: Ajdath (أجداث) are graves. 'They come out from the graves (ajdath).'

primaryMeaning: trunk, stem
extendedMeaning: Trunk of a tree, stem.
quranUsage: 'We will crucify you on the trunks (judhoo') of palm trees.' Jidh' is trunk.
notes: Pharaoh's magicians were threatened with crucifixion on palm trunks.

primaryMeaning: part, piece
extendedMeaning: A part, piece.
quranUsage: Juz' (جزء) is part. 'For each gate a part (juz') of them.'

primaryMeaning: pocket, collar
extendedMeaning: Pocket, collar opening.
quranUsage: Jayb (جيب) is pocket. 'Put your hand in your jayb (pocket).' Also collar.

primaryMeaning: to surround, eye
extendedMeaning: Surrounding, or the pupil.
quranUsage: Hadaqa means to stare. Hadiqah is garden.

primaryMeaning: to incite, urge
extendedMeaning: Inciting, urging.
quranUsage: Harrada means to urge. 'Urge (harrid) the believers.'

primaryMeaning: to urge, encourage
extendedMeaning: Urging, encouraging.
quranUsage: Hadda means to urge. 'You do not urge (tahadduna) feeding the poor.'

primaryMeaning: barefoot, eager
extendedMeaning: Barefoot, or being eager.
quranUsage: Hafiy (حفي) is well-informed. 'As if you were eager (hafiy) about it.'

primaryMeaning: to shave, ring
extendedMeaning: Shaving, or a ring.
quranUsage: Halaqa means to shave. 'Shaving (muhaliqin) your heads.'

primaryMeaning: need
extendedMeaning: Need, poverty.
quranUsage: Hajah (حاجة) is need. 'No need (hajah) in their hearts.'

primaryMeaning: to be humble
extendedMeaning: Being humble.
quranUsage: Akhbata means to be humble. 'Those who humble (akhbatu) themselves.'

primaryMeaning: to abandon, forsake
extendedMeaning: Abandoning someone, leaving without support.
quranUsage: 'If Allah forsakes (yakhdhul) you, who can help you?'
notes: Being abandoned by Allah is the worst fate.

primaryMeaning: to lower voice, be soft
extendedMeaning: Lowering voice, speaking softly.
quranUsage: 'Do not be loud in your prayer nor silent, but seek between.' Khaft is lowering voice.
notes: Moderation in voice during prayer is recommended.

primaryMeaning: thread, sew
extendedMeaning: Thread, sewing, stitching.
quranUsage: 'Until the white thread (khayt) is distinct from the black.' Khayt is thread.
notes: Dawn is when white and black threads of light are distinguishable.

primaryMeaning: to push, repulse
extendedMeaning: Pushing away.
quranUsage: Yadu'u means to push. 'Repulses (yadu'u) the orphan.'

primaryMeaning: wolf
extendedMeaning: Wolf.
quranUsage: Dhi'b (ذئب) is wolf. 'The wolf (dhi'b) ate him.'

primaryMeaning: peak, summit, top
extendedMeaning: Peak, summit, highest point.
quranUsage: Dhirwah is peak. The highest point.
notes: Mountains have peaks that reach the sky.

primaryMeaning: chin
extendedMeaning: Chin, beard.
quranUsage: Adhqan (أذقان) are chins. 'Fall on their chins (adhqan).'

primaryMeaning: to follow
extendedMeaning: Following, successive.
quranUsage: Murdif means following. 'Followed (murdifin) by a thousand.'

primaryMeaning: plentiful, comfortable
extendedMeaning: Plentiful, comfortable.
quranUsage: Raghadan (رغدا) is plentifully. 'Eat plentifully (raghadan).'

primaryMeaning: writing, number, to mark
extendedMeaning: Writing, numbering, and marking.
quranUsage: 'A written (marqum) register.' Raqm is number/writing.
notes: Our deeds are numbered and recorded precisely.

primaryMeaning: to strike with foot
extendedMeaning: Striking, running.
quranUsage: Rurkud means to run. 'When they were running (yarkudun).'

primaryMeaning: to heap up
extendedMeaning: Heaping up.
quranUsage: Rukam (ركام) is heaped. 'Heaped clouds (rukam).'

primaryMeaning: pomegranate
extendedMeaning: Pomegranate fruit.
quranUsage: 'Therein are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates (rumman).'
notes: Pomegranates are Paradise fruits.

primaryMeaning: group, clan
extendedMeaning: A group, clan.
quranUsage: Raht (رهط) is clan. 'Your clan (rahtuka) is powerful.'

primaryMeaning: pledge, hostage
extendedMeaning: Pledge, mortgage.
quranUsage: Rahn (رهن) is pledge. 'A pledge (rihan) taken.'

primaryMeaning: to turn aside
extendedMeaning: Turning aside, evading.
quranUsage: Ragha means to turn aside. 'He turned (raga) to them.'

primaryMeaning: foam, froth
extendedMeaning: Foam, froth, scum.
quranUsage: 'As for the foam (zabad), it vanishes.' Zabad is foam.
notes: Falsehood is like foam - it appears but vanishes.

primaryMeaning: to drive
extendedMeaning: Driving.
quranUsage: Yazji means to drive. 'Drives (yazji) clouds.'

primaryMeaning: sigh, exhale, groan
extendedMeaning: Sighing, exhaling, groaning.
quranUsage: 'For them therein is sighing (zafir).' Zafir is sighing/groaning.
notes: The people of Hell sigh and groan.

primaryMeaning: Zaqqum tree
extendedMeaning: A tree in Hell.
quranUsage: Zaqqum (زقوم) is the tree in Hell. 'The tree of Zaqqum.'

primaryMeaning: to become weary
extendedMeaning: Weariness.
quranUsage: Sa'ima means to be weary. 'They do not weary (yas'amun).'

primaryMeaning: to cover, conceal, veil
extendedMeaning: Covering and concealing, especially faults or private matters.
quranUsage: Sitr is covering. Allah is As-Satir/As-Sittir who covers faults. Satr al-'awrah is covering private parts.
notes: Covering others' faults is praised.

primaryMeaning: to heat, fill
extendedMeaning: Heating, filling.
quranUsage: Sujjirat means kindled. 'The seas are set ablaze (sujjirat).'

primaryMeaning: garment
extendedMeaning: Garment, coat.
quranUsage: Saraabil are garments. 'Garments (saraabil).'

primaryMeaning: to strip off
extendedMeaning: Stripping off.
quranUsage: Naslakhu means to strip. 'We strip (naslakhu) from it the night.'

primaryMeaning: chain
extendedMeaning: Chain, series.
quranUsage: 'A chain (silsilah) of seventy cubits.' Silsilah is chain.
notes: Chains bind the people of Hell.

primaryMeaning: lineage, extract, draw out
extendedMeaning: Lineage (drawn from ancestors), extracting.
quranUsage: 'From an extract (sulalah) of clay.' Sulalah is extract/lineage.
notes: Humans are created from an extract of clay.

primaryMeaning: quail
extendedMeaning: Quail.
quranUsage: Salwa (سلوى) is quail. 'The manna and salwa (quail).'

primaryMeaning: to be easy to swallow
extendedMeaning: Being easy to swallow.
quranUsage: Yusīghuhu means can swallow. 'He can hardly swallow (yusīghuhu) it.'

primaryMeaning: to travel, flow
extendedMeaning: Traveling, flowing.
quranUsage: Siha means to travel. 'Travel (sihu) four months.'

primaryMeaning: left, ill-omen
extendedMeaning: Left side, ill-omen.
quranUsage: Ash'am is ill-fated. 'Most ill-fated (ash'aha).'

primaryMeaning: to load a ship
extendedMeaning: Loading a ship.
quranUsage: Mashun is laden. 'The laden (mashun) ship.'

primaryMeaning: to go too far
extendedMeaning: Going to excess.
quranUsage: Shatat (شطط) is excess. 'We said excessively (shatatan).'

primaryMeaning: to complain, grieve
extendedMeaning: Complaining, expressing grief or hardship.
quranUsage: 'I only complain (ashku) of my grief to Allah.' Shakwa is complaint.
notes: Ya'qub complained only to Allah, not to people.

primaryMeaning: to hate
extendedMeaning: Hatred.
quranUsage: Shana'ana is hatred. 'Let not hatred (shana'anu) make you unjust.'

primaryMeaning: gray hair, old age
extendedMeaning: Gray hair, old age.
quranUsage: Shayb (شيب) is gray hair. 'My head has kindled with gray (shayban).'

primaryMeaning: Sabians
extendedMeaning: Sabians (religious group).
quranUsage: Sabi'un (صابئون) are Sabians.

primaryMeaning: dye, color, baptism
extendedMeaning: Dyeing, coloring, and baptism.
quranUsage: 'The coloring (sibghah) of Allah.' Sibghah is dye/coloring.
notes: Islam is Allah's sibghah - His coloring of the soul.

primaryMeaning: to incline, youth
extendedMeaning: Inclining to youth.
quranUsage: Saba means to incline. 'I might incline (asbu) to them.'

primaryMeaning: rock, boulder
extendedMeaning: Large rock or boulder.
quranUsage: 'Even if it be inside a rock (sakhrah).' Sakhr is rock/boulder.
notes: Nothing is hidden from Allah, even inside solid rock.

primaryMeaning: cold violent wind
extendedMeaning: Extremely cold, howling wind.
quranUsage: 'A screaming wind (sarsar).' Sarsar is freezing violent wind.
notes: The 'Ad were destroyed by sarsar wind.

primaryMeaning: to cut, harvest
extendedMeaning: Cutting, harvesting.
quranUsage: Sarim (صريم) is harvested. 'Like a garden harvested (sarim).'

primaryMeaning: lie down, recline
extendedMeaning: Lying down, reclining.
quranUsage: 'Their sides forsake their beds (madaji').' Daj' is lying down. Madja' is bed.
notes: The righteous leave their beds for night prayer.

primaryMeaning: bunch, confused dreams
extendedMeaning: Bunch, confused dreams.
quranUsage: Adghath (أضغاث) are confused dreams. 'Confused dreams (adghath).'

primaryMeaning: to extinguish
extendedMeaning: Extinguishing.
quranUsage: Taffa means to extinguish. 'They want to extinguish (yutfi'u).'

primaryMeaning: to begin
extendedMeaning: Beginning continuously.
quranUsage: Tafiqa means to begin. 'They began (tafiqa) patching.'

primaryMeaning: thirst
extendedMeaning: Thirst.
quranUsage: Zama' (ظمأ) is thirst. 'No thirst (zama').'

primaryMeaning: to frown
extendedMeaning: Frowning.
quranUsage: 'Abasa means to frown. 'He frowned ('abasa).' Surah 80.

primaryMeaning: to happen, befall
extendedMeaning: Happening.
quranUsage: 'Urwah (عروة) is handhold. 'The firmest handhold ('urwah).'

primaryMeaning: nakedness, bare, to be naked
extendedMeaning: Being uncovered, naked, or bare.
quranUsage: 'That he may expose (yubdi) their nakedness ('awrat).' 'Awrah is what must be covered.
notes: Adam and Hawwa's nakedness was exposed after eating from the tree.

primaryMeaning: to help, honor
extendedMeaning: Helping, honoring.
quranUsage: 'Azzara means to honor. 'Honor ('azzaruhu) and help him.'

primaryMeaning: caravan, donkey
extendedMeaning: Caravan, donkey.
quranUsage: 'Ir (عير) is caravan. 'Ask the caravan ('ir).'

primaryMeaning: to slacken
extendedMeaning: Slackening, weakening.
quranUsage: Yafturu means to slacken. 'They do not slacken (yafturun).'

primaryMeaning: to twist
extendedMeaning: Twisting.
quranUsage: Fatil (فتيل) is thread. 'A thread (fatilan).'

primaryMeaning: mountain pass
extendedMeaning: Mountain pass, road.
quranUsage: Fajj (فج) is road. 'From every distant road (fajj).'

primaryMeaning: to crush, crumble
extendedMeaning: Crushing, crumbling.
quranUsage: Farat is scattered. Related to scattering.

primaryMeaning: to disturb, excite
extendedMeaning: Disturbing, exciting.
quranUsage: Istafziz means to disturb. 'Disturb (astafziz) whom you can.'

primaryMeaning: to make room
extendedMeaning: Making room.
quranUsage: Tafsahu means to make room. 'Make room (tafsahu).'

primaryMeaning: to lose, miss
extendedMeaning: Losing, missing, and lacking.
quranUsage: 'They said: We are missing (nafqidu) the king's cup.' Faqd is loss.
notes: Opposite of و-ج-د (finding).

primaryMeaning: to take fire
extendedMeaning: Taking fire, brand.
quranUsage: Qabas (قبس) is firebrand. 'Or I find a firebrand (qabas).'

primaryMeaning: wound, ulcer
extendedMeaning: Wound, ulcer.
quranUsage: Qarḥ (قرح) is wound. 'If a wound (qarḥ) has touched you.'

primaryMeaning: monkey, ape
extendedMeaning: Monkey, ape.
quranUsage: Qiradah (قردة) is apes. 'Be apes (qiradatan) despised.'

primaryMeaning: to suppress, humiliate
extendedMeaning: Suppressing, humiliating.
quranUsage: Kubitu means suppressed. 'They were suppressed (kubitū).'

primaryMeaning: to wrap, coil
extendedMeaning: Wrapping, coiling.
quranUsage: Kuwwirat means wrapped. 'When the sun is wrapped up (kuwwirat).'

primaryMeaning: to seek refuge
extendedMeaning: Seeking refuge.
quranUsage: Malja' (ملجأ) is refuge. 'No refuge (malja').'

primaryMeaning: pleasure, delight
extendedMeaning: Pleasure, delight.
quranUsage: Ladhdhah (لذة) is pleasure. 'A pleasure (ladhdhatan) for the drinkers.'

primaryMeaning: to turn, distract
extendedMeaning: Turning, distracting.
quranUsage: Talattafat means turned. Talfit: distraction.

primaryMeaning: to wrap
extendedMeaning: Wrapping.
quranUsage: Iltaffat means wrapped. 'When the legs are wrapped (iltaffat).'

primaryMeaning: to turn aside
extendedMeaning: Turning aside.
quranUsage: Talaqqā means to receive. 'He received (talaqqā) from his Lord words.'

primaryMeaning: to swallow, snatch
extendedMeaning: Swallowing, snatching.
quranUsage: Talqaf means to swallow. 'It will swallow (talqaf) what they made.'

primaryMeaning: flame
extendedMeaning: Flame.
quranUsage: Lahab (لهب) is flame. Surah Al-Masad. 'Father of flame (lahab).'

primaryMeaning: strong, firm
extendedMeaning: Strong, firm.
quranUsage: Matīn (متين) is firm. 'The Possessor of Power, the Firm (matīn).'

primaryMeaning: to erase, wipe out
extendedMeaning: Erasing, wiping out.
quranUsage: Yamḥū means to erase. 'Allah erases (yamḥū) what He wills.'

primaryMeaning: to be joyful, arrogant
extendedMeaning: Joyfulness, arrogance.
quranUsage: Maraḥan is arrogant. 'Do not walk arrogantly (maraḥan).'

primaryMeaning: mix, blend
extendedMeaning: Mixing drinks, blending.
quranUsage: 'A cup mixed (mizaj) with ginger.' Mazj is mixing.
notes: Paradise drinks are mixed with special flavors.

primaryMeaning: chewed substance, morsel
extendedMeaning: Chewed lump, morsel of flesh.
quranUsage: 'Then from a chewed lump (mudghah).' Mudghah is chewed substance.
notes: Stage of embryo resembling chewed flesh.

primaryMeaning: to move, sway
extendedMeaning: Moving, swaying.
quranUsage: Tamūru means to sway. 'The earth will sway (tamūru).'

primaryMeaning: to be distant
extendedMeaning: Being distant.
quranUsage: Yan'awna means to distance. 'They distance (yan'awna) from it.'

primaryMeaning: to scatter
extendedMeaning: Scattering.
quranUsage: Intatharat means scattered. 'When the stars are scattered (intatharat).'

primaryMeaning: copper, brass, misfortune
extendedMeaning: Copper/brass, and ill omen or misfortune.
quranUsage: 'Sent upon them a screaming wind in days of misfortune (nahisat).' Nuhas is copper.
notes: Copper and brass were important metals in ancient times.

primaryMeaning: lineage, genealogy, relate
extendedMeaning: Lineage, genealogy, and relating to.
quranUsage: 'They made between Him and the jinn a lineage (nasab).' Nasab is lineage.
notes: False claims of lineage between Allah and jinn are rejected.

primaryMeaning: to arrange, pile up
extendedMeaning: Arranging, piling up.
quranUsage: Manḍūd means piled up. 'Bananas piled up (manḍūd).'

primaryMeaning: bloom, flourish, radiant
extendedMeaning: Blooming, flourishing, radiance.
quranUsage: 'Radiant (nadirah) faces.' Nadrah is radiance/bloom.
notes: Faces of the blessed will be radiant.

primaryMeaning: to penetrate, pass through
extendedMeaning: Penetrating, passing through.
quranUsage: Tanfudhū means to pass through. 'If you can pass through (tanfudhū).'

primaryMeaning: to pierce, explore
extendedMeaning: Piercing, exploring.
quranUsage: Naqqabū means they explored. 'They explored (naqqabū) in the lands.'

primaryMeaning: to reverse, turn upside down
extendedMeaning: Reversing, turning upside down.
quranUsage: Nukisū means reversed. 'Then they were reversed (nukisū).'

primaryMeaning: to disdain
extendedMeaning: Disdaining.
quranUsage: Yastankif means to disdain. 'Would never disdain (yastankifa).'

primaryMeaning: defeat, to rout
extendedMeaning: Defeat, routing an army.
quranUsage: 'They defeated (hazamu) them.' Hazimah is defeat.
notes: Armies are defeated by Allah's permission.

primaryMeaning: to hasten, crane neck
extendedMeaning: Hastening, craning neck.
quranUsage: Muhṭi'īn means hastening with necks craned. 'Racing with heads raised (muhṭi'īna).'

primaryMeaning: to slander, goad
extendedMeaning: Slandering, goading.
quranUsage: Humazah (همزة) is slanderer. Surah Al-Humazah. 'Every slanderer (humazah).'

primaryMeaning: peg, stake
extendedMeaning: Peg, stake.
quranUsage: Awtād (أوتاد) are stakes. 'Pharaoh of the stakes (awtād).'

primaryMeaning: odd, single, string
extendedMeaning: Being odd (number), single, and bowstring.
quranUsage: 'By the odd (watr) and the even.' Witr is odd. Watar is string.
notes: Witr prayer has an odd number of units.

primaryMeaning: idol
extendedMeaning: Idol.
quranUsage: Wathan (وثن) is idol. 'The idols (awthān).'

primaryMeaning: to feel, sense
extendedMeaning: Feeling, sensing fear.
quranUsage: Awjasa means to feel. 'He felt (awjasa) fear.'

primaryMeaning: to close, shut
extendedMeaning: Closing, shutting.
quranUsage: Mu'ṣadah means closed. 'It is closed (mu'ṣadah) upon them.'

primaryMeaning: furniture, goods
extendedMeaning: Furniture, household goods.
quranUsage: Athath (أثاث) is furniture. 'Furniture (athath) and enjoyment.'

primaryMeaning: need, skill
extendedMeaning: Need, requirement, or skill.
quranUsage: Irbah (إربة) is need. 'Those without irbah (need) for women.'

primaryMeaning: to support, strengthen
extendedMeaning: Supporting, strengthening.
quranUsage: Azara means to support. 'Strengthen (azirni) me.' Izar is waist-wrapper.

primaryMeaning: to shake, incite
extendedMeaning: Shaking, inciting.
quranUsage: Azza means to incite. 'We sent devils to incite (ta'uzzuhum) them.'

primaryMeaning: proud, exultant
extendedMeaning: Proud, insolent.
quranUsage: Ashir (أشر) is proud. 'Is he the proud (ashir) liar?'

primaryMeaning: to lament
extendedMeaning: Lamenting.
quranUsage: Related to expression of distress.

primaryMeaning: hope, wish
extendedMeaning: Hope, wish, aspiration.
quranUsage: Amal (أمل) is hope. 'Let them hope (amal) extend their life.'

primaryMeaning: maidservant
extendedMeaning: Maidservant.
quranUsage: Amah (أمة) is maidservant. 'A believing slave girl (amah).'

primaryMeaning: alas, grief
extendedMeaning: Expression of grief.
quranUsage: Awwah (أواه) is one who sighs. 'Ibrahim was forbearing, awwah (sighing).'

primaryMeaning: to devote, cut off
extendedMeaning: Devoting oneself, cutting off.
quranUsage: Tabattul is devotion. 'Devote (tabattal) yourself to Him.'

primaryMeaning: to destroy oneself
extendedMeaning: Destroying oneself from grief.
quranUsage: Bakha'a means to destroy oneself. 'Will you destroy (bakhi') yourself?'

primaryMeaning: body, sacrificial camel
extendedMeaning: Body, or large sacrificial animal.
quranUsage: Badan (بدن) is body. 'Today We will save your body (badan).' Budn are sacrificial camels.

primaryMeaning: leprosy
extendedMeaning: Leprosy, skin disease.
quranUsage: Abras (أبرص) is leper. 'I cure the abras (leper).'

primaryMeaning: to twist, dislike
extendedMeaning: Twisting, or disliking.
quranUsage: Barima means to be weary. 'Have they decided (abramu) an affair?'

primaryMeaning: to rise, shine
extendedMeaning: Rising, shining (of celestial bodies).
quranUsage: Bazagha means to rise. 'When the sun rose (bazaghat).'

primaryMeaning: to frown, unripe dates
extendedMeaning: Frowning, or unripe dates.
quranUsage: Basara means to frown. 'Then he frowned (basara).'

primaryMeaning: to crumble
extendedMeaning: Crumbling.
quranUsage: Bussat means crumbled. 'The mountains will be crumbled (bussat).'

primaryMeaning: to give up, detained
extendedMeaning: Being given up, detained for sin.
quranUsage: Ubsilat means to be detained. 'A soul detained (ubsilat) for what it earned.'

primaryMeaning: insolence, ingratitude
extendedMeaning: Insolent ingratitude.
quranUsage: Batira means to be insolent. 'They were insolent (batirat) in their living.'

primaryMeaning: to scatter
extendedMeaning: Scattering, overturning.
quranUsage: Bu'thira means to be scattered. 'When graves are scattered (bu'thirat).'

primaryMeaning: dung, camel
extendedMeaning: Camel dung.
quranUsage: Ba'ir (بعير) is camel. 'A camel-load (ba'ir).'

primaryMeaning: fingertips
extendedMeaning: Fingertips.
quranUsage: Banan (بنان) is fingertips. 'Strike their fingertips (banan).'

primaryMeaning: bowl, basin
extendedMeaning: A bowl, basin.
quranUsage: At-Tawr (التور) can be related to Mount Tur.

primaryMeaning: to weaken, overcome
extendedMeaning: Weakening through fighting.
quranUsage: Athkhana means to overcome. 'Until he has overcome (yuthkhina) in the land.'

primaryMeaning: snake, serpent
extendedMeaning: Snake, large serpent.
quranUsage: 'It became a serpent (thu'ban).' Thu'ban is large snake.
notes: Musa's staff became a great serpent.

primaryMeaning: to pierce, penetrate
extendedMeaning: Piercing, penetrating.
quranUsage: Thaqib (ثاقب) is piercing. 'A piercing (thaqib) flame.'

primaryMeaning: well, cistern
extendedMeaning: A well, cistern.
quranUsage: Jubb (جب) is well. 'Cast him into the bottom of the well (jubb).'

primaryMeaning: to cut into pieces
extendedMeaning: Cutting into pieces.
quranUsage: Judhadhan means pieces. 'He made them into pieces (judhadhan).'

primaryMeaning: locust, to strip
extendedMeaning: Locust, and stripping bare.
quranUsage: 'We sent upon them locusts (jarad).' Jarad is locusts.
notes: Locusts stripped Egypt as a plague.

primaryMeaning: barren land
extendedMeaning: Barren land without vegetation.
quranUsage: Juruz (جرز) is barren. 'A barren (juruz) land.'

primaryMeaning: impatience, distress
extendedMeaning: Impatience, distress, anguish.
quranUsage: 'When evil touches him, he is impatient (jazu'an).' Jaza' is impatience.
notes: Impatience is the opposite of sabr (patience).

primaryMeaning: body, physical
extendedMeaning: Body, physical form.
quranUsage: Jism (جسم) is body. 'Increased him in body (jism) and knowledge.'

primaryMeaning: to bring, incite
extendedMeaning: Bringing, inciting.
quranUsage: Ajlib means to gather. 'Gather (ajlib) against them.'

primaryMeaning: majesty, glory, magnificence
extendedMeaning: Overwhelming greatness and majesty that inspires awe.
quranUsage: Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram - Owner of Majesty and Honor. Jalal is Allah's majestic aspect.
notes: Jalal (majesty) complements Jamal (beauty) in describing Allah.

primaryMeaning: to incline unjustly
extendedMeaning: Inclining to injustice.
quranUsage: Janaf (جنف) is inclination. 'Fearing inclination (janaf) to sin.'

primaryMeaning: harvest, pick fruit
extendedMeaning: Harvesting, picking fruits.
quranUsage: 'Its harvest (janaha) is near.' Jany is picking fruit.
notes: Paradise fruits are easy to pick.

primaryMeaning: generosity, excellence
extendedMeaning: Generosity, excellence, quality.
quranUsage: Jud is generosity. Jawad is generous. Jayyid is excellent.
notes: The Prophet was the most generous of people.

primaryMeaning: to confine, detain
extendedMeaning: Confining, detaining.
quranUsage: Habasa means to confine. 'Detain (tahbisuna) them.'

primaryMeaning: barrier, to prevent
extendedMeaning: A barrier, preventing.

extendedMeaning: Churning, labor pains.
quranUsage: Makhāḍ (مخاض) is labor. 'The labor pains (makhāḍ) drove her.'

primaryMeaning: flint stone
extendedMeaning: Flint stone.
quranUsage: Marwah (مروة) is Marwah. 'Ṣafā and Marwah.'

primaryMeaning: balance, scales
extendedMeaning: Balance, scales for weighing.
quranUsage: 'We will set up the scales (mawazin) of justice.' Mizan is scale/balance.
notes: Deeds will be weighed on precise scales.

primaryMeaning: to transform
extendedMeaning: Transforming.
quranUsage: Masakhnāhum means We transformed. 'We transformed (masakhnāhum) them.'

primaryMeaning: twisted fiber
extendedMeaning: Twisted fiber, rope.
quranUsage: Masad (مسد) is rope. Surah Al-Masad. 'A rope (masad) of palm fiber.'

primaryMeaning: to wipe
extendedMeaning: Wiping.
quranUsage: Imsaḥū means wipe. 'Wipe (imsaḥū) your heads.'

primaryMeaning: mixed
extendedMeaning: Mixed.
quranUsage: Amshāj (أمشاج) is mixed. 'A drop mixed (amshāj).'

primaryMeaning: to stretch
extendedMeaning: Stretching.
quranUsage: Yatamaṭṭā means to stretch. 'Then he went to his family strutting (yatamaṭṭā).'

primaryMeaning: goat
extendedMeaning: Goat.
quranUsage: 'And of the goats (ma'z), two.' Ma'z is goat.
notes: Goats are mentioned among the eight pairs of livestock.

primaryMeaning: entrails
extendedMeaning: Entrails.
quranUsage: Am'ā' (أمعاء) are intestines. 'Cuts up their intestines (am'ā'ahum).'

primaryMeaning: to whistle
extendedMeaning: Whistling.
quranUsage: Mukā'an (مكاء) is whistling. 'Whistling (mukā'an) and clapping.'

primaryMeaning: provisions
extendedMeaning: Provisions.
quranUsage: Namīru means we get provisions. 'We get provisions (namīru).'

primaryMeaning: to call names
extendedMeaning: Calling names.
quranUsage: Tanābazū means call names. 'Do not call names (tanābazū).'

primaryMeaning: to draw out water
extendedMeaning: Drawing out water.
quranUsage: Yastanbiṭūna means to extract. 'Those who extract (yastanbiṭūnahu) it.'

primaryMeaning: to shake, raise
extendedMeaning: Shaking, raising.
quranUsage: Nataqnā means We raised. 'We raised (nataqnā) the mountain.'

primaryMeaning: highland, path
extendedMeaning: Highland, path.
quranUsage: Najdayn (نجدين) are two ways. 'The two ways (najdayn).'

primaryMeaning: impurity, filth
extendedMeaning: Ritual impurity and filth.
quranUsage: 'The polytheists are impure (najas).' Najas is impurity. Najis is impure.
notes: Spiritual impurity of shirk is worse than physical impurity.

primaryMeaning: sob, weep, vow
extendedMeaning: Sobbing, weeping loudly.
quranUsage: 'Some fulfilled their vow (nahb).' Nahib is sobbing. Nahb is vow fulfilled.
notes: Some believers fulfilled their pledge through martyrdom.

primaryMeaning: sacrifice camel, throat
extendedMeaning: Slaughtering camels, the throat area.
quranUsage: 'Pray and sacrifice (wanhar).' Nahr is sacrificing camels.
notes: Camels are sacrificed by cutting the throat area.

primaryMeaning: to snort, decay
extendedMeaning: Snorting, decaying.
quranUsage: Nākhirah (ناخرة) is decayed. 'Decayed (nākhirah) bones.'

primaryMeaning: eagle, vulture
extendedMeaning: Eagle, vulture.
quranUsage: Nasr (نسر) is Nasr (idol). 'And Yaghūth and Ya'ūq and Nasr.'

primaryMeaning: to be cooked, ripe
extendedMeaning: Being cooked, ripe.
quranUsage: Naḍijat means is roasted. 'Their skins are roasted (naḍijat).'

primaryMeaning: to gush
extendedMeaning: Gushing.
quranUsage: Naḍḍākhatān are gushing. 'Two gushing (naḍḍākhatān) springs.'

primaryMeaning: to gore, butt
extendedMeaning: Goring, butting.
quranUsage: Naṭīḥah (نطيحة) is gored. 'That gored (naṭīḥah).'

primaryMeaning: croak, bleat, call
extendedMeaning: Animal sounds, croaking, bleating.
quranUsage: 'Like one who calls (yan'iqu) to that which hears nothing.' Na'iq is one who calls.
notes: Calling disbelievers is like calling animals that don't understand.

primaryMeaning: sandal, shoe
extendedMeaning: Sandal, shoe.
quranUsage: Na'layka (نعليك) is your sandals. 'Remove your sandals (na'layk).'

primaryMeaning: to shake head
extendedMeaning: Shaking head.
quranUsage: Yunghiḍūna means they shake. 'They shake (yunghiḍūna) their heads.'

primaryMeaning: to blow, spit
extendedMeaning: Blowing, spitting.
quranUsage: Naffāthāt (نفاثات) are those who blow. 'Those who blow (naffāthāt) on knots.'

primaryMeaning: to blow, waft
extendedMeaning: Blowing, wafting.
quranUsage: Nafḥah (نفحة) is breath. 'If a breath (nafḥatun) touches them.'

primaryMeaning: to banish, exile
extendedMeaning: Banishing, exiling.
quranUsage: Yunfaw means banished. 'Or be banished (yunfaw).'

primaryMeaning: to soak, pool
extendedMeaning: Soaking, pool.
quranUsage: Naq' (نقع) is stirring up dust. 'Stirring up (naq'an) thereby dust.'

primaryMeaning: to be barren, unproductive
extendedMeaning: Being barren, unproductive.
quranUsage: Nakidan (نكدا) is barren. 'It comes forth barren (nakidan).'

primaryMeaning: cushion
extendedMeaning: Cushion.
quranUsage: Namāriq (نمارق) are cushions. 'Cushions (namāriq) lined up.'

primaryMeaning: to slander, gossip
extendedMeaning: Slandering, gossiping.
quranUsage: Nammām (نمام) is slanderer. 'A spreader of slander (nammām).'

primaryMeaning: to pant, clear path
extendedMeaning: Panting, clear path.
quranUsage: Minhāj (منهاج) is path. 'A law and a path (minhājan).'

primaryMeaning: to be heavy, burden
extendedMeaning: Being heavy, burden.
quranUsage: Tanū'u means to burden. 'Its keys would burden (tanū'u).'

primaryMeaning: to seize, catch
extendedMeaning: Seizing, catching.
quranUsage: Tanāwush (تناوش) is seizing. 'How can they seize (tanāwush) from afar?'

primaryMeaning: to escape, flee
extendedMeaning: Escaping, fleeing.
quranUsage: Manāṣ (مناص) is escape. 'No time for escape (manāṣ).'

primaryMeaning: fish, letter noon
extendedMeaning: Fish, letter noon.
quranUsage: Nūn (نون) is fish/letter. Surah Nūn. 'Companion of the fish (nūn).'

primaryMeaning: intention, to intend
extendedMeaning: Intention and purpose behind actions.
quranUsage: Niyyah is intention. The Prophet said: 'Actions are by intentions.'
notes: Every act of worship requires proper intention (niyyah).

primaryMeaning: to give, grant
extendedMeaning: Giving, granting.
quranUsage: Hā' is here/take. Related to presenting.

primaryMeaning: to stay awake, pray at night
extendedMeaning: Staying awake for prayer.
quranUsage: Tahajjud (تهجد) is night prayer. 'Pray tahajjud (tahajjad).'

primaryMeaning: to sleep at night
extendedMeaning: Sleeping at night.
quranUsage: Hāji'ūn (هاجعون) are sleeping. Related to night rest.

primaryMeaning: to demolish, threaten
extendedMeaning: Demolishing, threatening.
quranUsage: Yahaddu means to collapse. 'About to collapse (yahaddu).'

primaryMeaning: to demolish, destroy
extendedMeaning: Demolishing, tearing down.
quranUsage: 'Destroyed (huddimat) would have been monasteries.' Hadm is demolition.
notes: Without Allah's protection, places of worship would be destroyed.

primaryMeaning: hoopoe
extendedMeaning: Hoopoe bird.
quranUsage: 'He inspected the birds and said: Why do I not see the hoopoe (hudhud)?' Hudhud is hoopoe.
notes: The hoopoe brought Sulayman news of the Queen of Sheba.

primaryMeaning: to flee
extendedMeaning: Fleeing.
quranUsage: Harab (هرب) is fleeing. Related to escape.

primaryMeaning: to joke, jest
extendedMeaning: Joking, jesting.
quranUsage: Hazl (هزل) is jest. 'It is not a jest (hazl).'

primaryMeaning: to beat down leaves
extendedMeaning: Beating down leaves.
quranUsage: Ahushsha means to beat down. 'I beat down (ahushsha) leaves.'

primaryMeaning: anxiety, impatience
extendedMeaning: Anxiety, impatience, fretfulness.
quranUsage: 'Man was created anxious (halu'an).' Hala' is anxiety.
notes: Humans are naturally anxious except those who pray.

primaryMeaning: to be still, extinguished
extendedMeaning: Being still, extinguished.
quranUsage: Hāmidah (هامدة) is lifeless. 'You see the earth lifeless (hāmidatan).'

primaryMeaning: to pour down
extendedMeaning: Pouring down.
quranUsage: Munhamir (منهمر) is pouring. 'Water pouring (munhamir).'

primaryMeaning: whisper, faint sound
extendedMeaning: Whispering, hushed sound.
quranUsage: 'You will hear only whispers (hams).' Hams is whisper.
notes: On Judgment Day, voices will be hushed before Allah.

primaryMeaning: to invite
extendedMeaning: Inviting.
quranUsage: Hayta means come. 'Come (hayta) to you.'

primaryMeaning: to pour
extendedMeaning: Pouring.
quranUsage: Mahīl (مهيل) is poured. 'A heap poured (mahīlan).'

primaryMeaning: to bury alive
extendedMeaning: Burying alive.
quranUsage: Wu'idat means buried. 'When the girl buried alive (wu'idat) is asked.'

primaryMeaning: to flee for refuge
extendedMeaning: Fleeing for refuge.
quranUsage: Maw'il (موئل) is refuge. 'No refuge (maw'ilan).'

primaryMeaning: camel hair
extendedMeaning: Camel hair.
quranUsage: Awbār (أوبار) is camel hair. 'From their wool and fur (awbārihā).'

primaryMeaning: jugular vein
extendedMeaning: Jugular vein.
quranUsage: Watīn (وتين) is life-artery. 'Cut from him the artery (watīn).'

primaryMeaning: necessary, obligatory, to fall
extendedMeaning: Being necessary, obligatory, and falling due.
quranUsage: 'When their sides fall (wajabat).' Wajib is obligatory.
notes: Wajib in fiqh means religiously obligatory.

primaryMeaning: loneliness, wild
extendedMeaning: Loneliness, wildness, being untamed.
quranUsage: 'Wild beasts (wuhush) are gathered.' Wahsh is wild beast. Wahshah is loneliness.
notes: Wild animals will be gathered on Judgment Day.

primaryMeaning: to be drowsy
extendedMeaning: Being drowsy.
quranUsage: Sinah (سنة) is drowsiness. 'Neither drowsiness (sinah) nor sleep.'

primaryMeaning: to embroider
extendedMeaning: Embroidering.
quranUsage: Wāshiyah (واشية) is embroidered. Related to decoration.

primaryMeaning: to inlay, arrange
extendedMeaning: Inlaying, arranging.
quranUsage: Mawḍūnah (موضونة) is inlaid. 'Inlaid (mawḍūnah) couches.'

primaryMeaning: homeland
extendedMeaning: Homeland.
quranUsage: Mawāṭin (مواطن) are places. 'In many places (mawāṭin).'

primaryMeaning: delegation
extendedMeaning: Delegation.
quranUsage: Wafd (وفد) is delegation. 'As a delegation (wafdan).'

primaryMeaning: abundance, plentiful
extendedMeaning: Abundance, being plentiful.
quranUsage: 'Reward most abundant (awfar).' Wafir is abundant.
notes: Allah's rewards are always abundant.

primaryMeaning: to hasten
extendedMeaning: Hastening.
quranUsage: Yūfiḍūna means they hasten. 'They hasten (yūfiḍūna).'

primaryMeaning: to set, darkness
extendedMeaning: Setting, darkness.
quranUsage: Ghāsiq (غاسق) waqab is night when it settles. 'When it becomes dark (waqab).'

primaryMeaning: to strike fatally
extendedMeaning: Striking fatally.
quranUsage: Mawqūdhah (موقوذة) is beaten to death. 'That beaten to death (mawqūdhah).'

primaryMeaning: to confirm, stress
extendedMeaning: Confirming, stressing.
quranUsage: Tawkīd (توكيد) is emphasis. Related to affirming.

primaryMeaning: to strike, punch
extendedMeaning: Striking, punching.
quranUsage: Wakaz means to strike. 'He struck (wakazahu) him.'

primaryMeaning: to weaken, flag
extendedMeaning: Weakening, flagging.
quranUsage: Taniyā means to weaken. 'Do not weaken (taniyā).'

primaryMeaning: to burn, glow
extendedMeaning: Burning, glowing.
quranUsage: Wahhāj (وهاج) is blazing. 'A blazing (wahhājan) lamp.'

primaryMeaning: to be weak
extendedMeaning: Being weak.
quranUsage: Wāhiyah (واهية) is weak/torn. 'Like a torn (wāhiyah) tent.'

primaryMeaning: wakefulness, to awaken
extendedMeaning: Being awake, alertness, and awakening.
quranUsage: 'You would think them awake (ayqaz).' Yaqazah is wakefulness.
notes: The People of the Cave appeared awake while sleeping.

primaryMeaning: ripen
extendedMeaning: Ripening of fruit.
quranUsage: 'Look at its fruit when it ripens (yani').' Yan' is ripening.
notes: Fruit ripening is a sign of Allah's power.
